I. Executive Summary
1. Overview
1.1. Summary of Regulatory Action
The Applicant (Ionis Pharmaceuticals) submitted an NDA for donidalorsen (proposed
tradename: Dawnzera), an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) targeting prekallikrein mRNA, for
prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and adolescent patients
12 years and older at a dose of 80 mg subcutaneous (SC) every 4 weeks; a dosing interval of
(b) (4) may be considered
(b) (4)
once every
(b) (4) . The ASO is conjugated to a ligand containing three
N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residues to enable delivery of the ASO to hepatocytes, where
prekallikrein is synthesized, supporting a lower dose than for nonconjugated ASOs. The NDA
was reviewed by a multidisciplinary review team; no issues were identified from any discipline
that preclude approval.
Substantial evidence of effectiveness of donidalorsen in patients with HAE was established using
data from a single adequate and well-controlled trial (CS5) studying two dosing regimens (80 mg
every 4 weeks [Q4W] and 80 mg every 8 weeks [Q8W]) and placebo, and confirmatory evidence
(CE) based on mechanistic data; see the description in Section 1.2. The available safety data
demonstrated that donidalorsen is safe for its intended use. Anaphylaxis occurred in one subject.
Common adverse reactions included injection site reactions, upper respiratory tract infection,
urinary tract infection, and abdominal discomfort. Laboratory findings with donidalorsen
treatment included decreased platelet counts and increased liver enzymes, consistent with the
ASO class effect. The safety profile for donidalorsen is acceptable for an HAE population and
can be adequately managed through labeling and further evaluated during routine
pharmacovigilance. A clinical postmarketing requirement will be included with this approval to
complete the ongoing multi-year open-label extension (OLE) trials (CS3 and CS7) to evaluate
the potential for drug-induced liver injury with donidalorsen.
Based on the positive dose response relationship of the 80 mg Q4W dosing regimen, the
recommended dosage of donidalorsen is 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks.
Because Q8W also independently met the primary efficacy endpoint and some secondary
endpoints a dosage of 80 mg every 8 weeks may also be considered at the discretion of the
prescriber.
The NDA includes appropriate preapproval nonclinical studies, but a nonclinical postmarketing
requirement will be included with this approval to complete the ongoing 2-year carcinogenicity
study in rats administered donidalorsen (see Section 24).
The submitted clinical program is adequate to support the efficacy and safety of donidalorsen for
the proposed indication. The clinical review team concludes that the reduction in acute HAE
attacks observed with donidalorsen treatment compared to placebo outweighs the risks, and that
4
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
donidalorsen will provide a novel option in the treatment armamentarium for HAE prophylaxis.
The benefit-risk assessment is favorable and supports the approval of donidalorsen for
“prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients
12 years of age and older.” The recommended dose is 80 mg administered subcutaneously every
4 weeks. A dosage of 80 mg every 8 weeks may also be considered.
The action for this application will be an Approval, with nonclinical and clinical postmarketing
requirements.

1.2. Conclusions on Substantial Evidence of
Effectiveness
Substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) was established with one adequate and wellcontrolled clinical investigation and confirmatory evidence.
The single adequate and well-controlled trial (CS5), was a 24-week multicenter, randomized,
double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating 90 adult and adolescent subjects with HAE
Type I or II. Subjects were randomized to one of the following treatment arms:


Donidalorsen 80 mg SC every 4 weeks (hereafter referred to as the donidalorsen-4 group).



Donidalorsen 80 mg SC every 8 weeks (hereafter referred to as the donidalorsen-8 group).



Placebo SC every 4 or 8 weeks (hereafter referred to as the pooled placebo group).

Trial CS5 met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically
meaningful reduction in the number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks in the donidalorsen-4 group
(least squares [LS] mean =0.44, 95% CI =0.27, 0.73) and the donidalorsen-8 group (LS
mean =1.02, 95% CI =0.65, 1.59), compared to the pooled placebo group (LS mean =2.26, 95%
CI =1.66, 3.09); this represents a percentage reduction in the means relative to placebo for the
donidalorsen-4 group of 81% (95% CI =65%, 89%) and for the donidalorsen-8 group of 55%
(95% CI =22%, 74%). These findings were supported by the results of secondary endpoints,
including the proportion of subjects with a ≥70% reduction in attacks, attack-free subjects,
moderate-to-severe HAE attacks, and HAE attacks requiring on-demand therapy. While both
dosing regimens demonstrated efficacy compared to placebo, donidalorsen-4 demonstrated
greater efficacy compared to donidalorsen-8 across primary and secondary endpoints.
The CE providing strong mechanistic support includes the well-established pathophysiology of
the disease and the mechanism of action of the therapy. Donidalorsen is conjugated to a ligand
containing three GalNAc residues that target the ASO to the liver. Donidalorsen inhibits
production of prekallikrein, a key protein in the contact/kallikrein-kinin system pathway that is
primarily synthesized in the liver, thereby reducing the downstream production of bradykinin,
the main mediator of angioedema in HAE. The mean percentage reduction from baseline to
Week 24 in trough plasma prekallikrein (PKK) concentrations were 73% and 47% following
treatment in the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 groups, respectively, compared with a slight
increase (2%) observed in the pooled placebo group. The mean percentage reduction from
baseline at Week 4 across both treatment groups was 48%. Based on the well-understood
5
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
pathophysiology of this genetic disease, demonstrated pharmacologic effect of donidalorsen on
the kallikrein-kinin pathway, and established efficacy of numerous approved HAE therapies (for
prophylaxis and acute attacks) that inhibit plasma kallikrein, the Applicant has provided
adequate mechanistic data to serve as CE to support SEE for the proposed indication.
Extrapolation of efficacy from adults with HAE to adolescent patients 12 to 17 years of age with
HAE is supported by the identical disease pathophysiology, mechanism of action, anticipated
treatment response, and clinical manifestations across age groups.
Overall, SEE was demonstrated by the results from Trial CS5 and the mechanistic data provided
by the Applicant. The use of a single adequate and well-controlled trial plus CE to demonstrate
SEE is supported by: (1) hereditary angioedema being a rare, serious, and potentially lifethreatening condition; (2) the efficacy results from the single trial are statistically significant and
clinically meaningful across primary and secondary endpoints; and (3) conduct of a second trial
would be infeasible. Use of a single adequate and well-controlled trial to demonstrate SEE is
consistent with the approach used for other HAE drug development programs.

2. Benefit-Risk Assessment
2.1. Benefit-Risk Framework
Table 2. Benefit-Risk Framework

condition

Conclusions and Reasons



HAE is a rare, genetic, potentially life-threatening disease
HAE is a rare condition caused by autosomal dominant
mutations in the SERPING1 gene, resulting in deficiency or characterized by unpredictable, recurrent, and self-limited skin
and submucosal swelling attacks.
dysfunction of C1-INH protein.



The pathophysiology of the disease is well-characterized.
Approximately 85% of patients have Type I HAE,
characterized by low production of normal C1-INH protein.
The remaining 15% of patients have Type II HAE,
characterized by production of dysfunctional C1-INH. Types
I and II have the same clinical phenotypes and responses
to available treatments.



Insufficient quantities of functional C1-INH lead to
dysregulation of the kallikrein-kinin system, a plasma
protease cascade initiated by Factor XII and culminating in
the generation of bradykinin. Uncontrolled bradykinin
production leads to increased vascular permeability and the
subcutaneous/submucosal swelling seen in acute HAE
attacks.



Acute HAE attacks are sporadic, recurrent, unpredictable,
and typically self-resolve after 48 to 72 hours. Attacks often
involve the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tract,
extremities (hands/feet), and face/upper airway. Attacks are
associated with significant morbidity due to pain, impact on
daily functioning, and disfigurement, and can be lifethreatening in cases of laryngeal edema resulting in airway
compromise.1



No cure exists; however, there are several approved
therapies for prophylaxis, as well as for on-demand
treatment of acute attacks.

Although there are numerous approved prophylactic therapies
for patients with HAE, the availability of additional treatment
options from a new pharmacologic class is desirable.



Approved therapies for HAE prophylaxis include plasmaderived C1-INH replacement therapies (intravenous and
subcutaneous), attenuated androgens (oral), a factor XIIa
inhibitor (subcutaneous), and plasma kallikrein inhibitors
(oral and subcutaneous).



Efficacy for both donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing
regimens is based on the results from a single, adequate
and well-controlled trial (CS5) in 90 adults and adolescents
with Type I or II HAE. Treatment with both dosing regimens
of donidalorsen resulted in statistically significant and
clinically persuasive reductions in the primary endpoint,
number of HAE attacks per month, throughout the 24-week
Treatment Period compared to placebo.

Donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens
demonstrated statistically significant and clinically relevant
treatment benefits on the reduction of number of acute HAE
attacks in adult and adolescent subjects with Types I and II
HAE, with further support from secondary endpoints.

Confirmatory evidence is provided by mechanistic data for
the well-established role of prekallikrein in the
pathophysiology of HAE attacks: this is supported by the
effectiveness of approved products of the same
pharmacological class (kallikrein inhibitors).

2.2. Conclusions Regarding Benefit-Risk
Hereditary angioedema is a rare, autosomal dominant condition, most often caused by
pathogenic variants in the SERPING1 gene that encodes C1-esterase inhibitor (C1-INH), a serine
protease-inhibitor involved in the kallikrein-kinin pathway, as well as the classical and lectin
complement, contact system/intrinsic coagulation, and fibrinolytic pathways. Under homeostatic
circumstances, activated Factor XII (FXIIa) triggers the kallikrein-kinin system, resulting in the
downstream production of bradykinin, a potent vasodilator and enhancer of vascular
permeability. C1-INH normally serves as an inhibitory check on the system by inhibiting both
kallikrein and FXIIa; in the absence of sufficient quantities of functional C1-INH, bradykinin
production is relatively unchecked and leads to recurrent subcutaneous and submucosal swelling
(or angioedema). Clinically, HAE is characterized by episodic, spontaneous, unpredictable
attacks of nonhistaminergic angioedema involving the subcutaneous and submucosal tissues, and
can include the face, gastrointestinal tract, genitourinary tract, extremities (hands/feet), and/or
throat and upper airway, the last of which can be particularly serious and potentially lifethreatening. Several products are approved for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks as well as for the
treatment of acute HAE attacks; however, breakthrough attacks still occur, and additional
prophylactic therapy options for HAE patients are beneficial.
Substantial evidence of effectiveness for donidalorsen in the prophylactic treatment of HAE is
based on the efficacy results from the single adequate and well-controlled clinical trial (CS5),
with confirmatory evidence from mechanistic data, as presented in Section 1.2. Although the
donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen demonstrated greater efficacy than the donidalorsen-8 dosing
regimen across primary and secondary endpoints, because both dosing intervals independently
met the primary efficacy endpoint, both dosing options are being approved for use. However,
based on the greater efficacy of the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen, the recommended dosage of
donidalorsen is 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks. A dosage of donidalorsen
80 mg administered subcutaneously every 8 weeks may also be considered, as included in
labeling, at the discretion of the prescriber.
Although the safety database is small, strengths include the placebo-controlled design, use of two
doses to assess dose-response, the 6-month treatment duration with additional long-term
exposure in the open-label extension period, the low study drop-out rate, and the small amount of
missing data. The safety assessment of donidalorsen revealed no concerning safety signals that
would preclude approval. No deaths occurred in the clinical development program. Serious
adverse events, severe adverse events, and adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation
were rare with no major imbalances between treatment groups. Anaphylaxis occurred in one
subject. Overall, treatment-emergent adverse events were predominantly mild or moderate in
severity, with the most common adverse reactions being injection site reactions, upper
respiratory tract infection, urinary tract infection, and abdominal discomfort.
As with other GalNac-ASOs, effects on clinical laboratory results including decreased platelet
counts, increased liver enzymes, and an increase in international normalized ratio (INR) were
observed, but these did not result in a safety signal in terms of adverse events. Generally, the
safety profile of donidalorsen is consistent with expected class effects of ASOs and kallikreindirected therapeutics. Potential risks can be addressed through labeling and routine
10
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
pharmacovigilance, as well as postmarketing requirements to assess for drug-induced liver injury
in the multi-year OLE trials (CS3 and CS7) and to complete the ongoing 2-year carcinogenicity
study in rats.
Although Trial CS5 enrolled a limited number of adolescent subjects (seven in the donidalorsen
group and zero in the placebo group), the efficacy and safety of donidalorsen in adolescent
patients 12 to <18 years of age is based on extrapolation from adults and matching
pharmacokinetic (PK) exposure and pharmacodynamic (PD) response. Extrapolation of efficacy
is supported by the same underlying pathophysiology and clinical manifestations of disease,
mechanism of action of donidalorsen, and similar expected response to treatment across age
groups.
Overall, the Agency concludes that the benefit-risk assessment is favorable and supports the
approval of donidalorsen 80 mg SC every 4 weeks or every 8 weeks for the proposed indication
of prophylaxis to prevent HAE attacks in adults and adolescents 12 years of age and above.

II. Interdisciplinary Assessment
3. Introduction
This review serves as the interdisciplinary assessment for the NDA for donidalorsen.
Donidalorsen is a new molecular entity, first-in-class chimeric GalNAc-conjugated 2′-Omethoxyethyl–modified antisense oligonucleotide targeting prekallikrein mRNA. The proposed
indication is for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and adolescent patients aged 12
(b) (4) . A dosing interval
years and older. The proposed dosage is 80 mg administered SC
(b) (4) may also be considered
(b) (4)
of 80 mg
(b) (4) .
Hereditary angioedema is a rare genetic condition characterized by recurrent episodes of
swelling in various body parts, including the hands/feet, genitals, gastrointestinal tract, face,
and/or throat (USHAA 2024). It is most often caused by pathogenic variants in the SERPING1
gene that encodes C1-INH, resulting in either low levels of C1-INH (Type I) or normal levels of
dysfunctional C1-INH (Type II) (Busse et al. 2021). The inheritance of HAE is autosomal
dominant, with approximately 25% of patients having de novo mutations. Patients with HAE
experience recurrent episodes of swelling that typically last for 2 to 3 days, but occasionally up
to 5 days. Symptom onset usually occurs in childhood, with 50% of patients experiencing
angioedema episodes by 10 years of age, and symptoms often increase after puberty. There is a
high degree of inter- and intrapatient variability in both the frequency and severity of attacks.
Characteristically, HAE symptoms do not respond to mast-cell targeted treatments, such as
antihistamines, corticosteroids, or epinephrine. Pharmacologic treatment of HAE consists of
access to on-demand therapies to treat acute episodes of angioedema and consideration for longterm prophylaxis on an individual basis. Approved therapies for the on-demand treatment of
acute attacks consist of products that target the kallikrein-kinin pathway (i.e., C1-INH
replacements, plasma kallikrein inhibitors (ecallantide and sebetralstat), and a bradykinin B2receptor antagonist (icatibant)). Similarly, approved therapies for maintenance prophylaxis to
prevent acute attacks consist of products that target the kallikrein-kinin pathway (i.e., C1-INH
replacement, a Factor XIIa inhibitor (garadacimab), and plasma kallikrein inhibitors
(lanadelumab and berotralstat)). Danazol, an attenuated androgen, is also approved for
prophylaxis, although its mechanism of action in HAE is unclear.
The Applicant submitted an IND application (IND 142564; July 15, 2019) to investigate
donidalorsen for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks. To support the NDA, the Applicant submitted
the results of a single, adequate, and well-controlled phase 3 trial (CS5). This 24-week,
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated 90 adult and adolescent subjects
with HAE Type I or II. The primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized number of
investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 25.
During the course of the application review, the Agency identified several key efficacy and
safety review issues, as listed below. In-depth analyses and assessments of these issues can be
found in Sections 6.3 and 7.7.

5. Pharmacologic Activity, Pharmacokinetics,
and Clinical Pharmacology
5.1. Nonclinical Assessment of Potential
Effectiveness
The unconjugated human PKK ASO parent compound of donidalorsen, ISIS 546254, which has
the same nucleobase sequence as donidalorsen, is perfectly matched to only PKK mRNA in the
human transcriptome (targets site free of meaningful sequence variation).

19
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Donidalorsen does not align perfectly to the mouse PKK gene sequence and is not
pharmacologically active in the mouse. The human sequence targeted by donidalorsen has a
single-base sequence mismatch within the binding site of monkey PKK mRNA (position 19).
Despite this mismatch, donidalorsen demonstrated dose-dependent inhibition of liver target
mRNA expression and reductions in PKK protein and activity levels in peripheral circulation of
Cynomolgus monkeys.
Incubation of donidalorsen with HepatoPac® (co-culture system of primary human hepatocytes
and stromal cells [mouse fibroblasts]) reduced PKK mRNA in a dose-dependent manner and
resulted in a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) value of 0.19μM.
In an in vivo study in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice, single SC administration of
donidalorsen on Day 0 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent reduction of plasma PKK protein
that approached 91% at the highest dose tested (10 mg/kg) on Day 14 after treatment. PKK
levels were still 20% below baseline levels by Day 56 (last time point evaluated) at 10 mg/kg.
The established pharmacologic class (EPC) for donidalorsen has been designated as
“prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide” based on in vitro and in vivo pharmacology
data.

5.2. Clinical Pharmacology/Pharmacokinetics
Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) is a chimeric GalNAc-conjugated 2’-O-methoxyethyl (2’-MOE)modified ASO. The ASO is covalently bound to GalNAc via a trishexylamino (THA) linker.
GalNAc is a ligand with affinity for the hepatocyte-specific asialoglycoprotein receptor
(ASGPR). This GalNAc conjugate approach results in ASO delivery to hepatocytes. The
modifications in ASO chains have been seen in other approved ASO products, such as
eplontersen (NDA 217388), tofersen (NDA 215887), inotersen (NDA 211172), and olezarsen
(NDA 218614). Eplontersen also contains an identical THA linker to that used in donidalorsen.

Mechanism of action
Donidalorsen is an ASO-GalNAc conjugate that causes RNase H1-mediated degradation of PKK mRNA through

Drug Information
Two dosing regimens, 80 mg Q4W and 80 mg Q8W, were evaluated and both demonstrated efficacy and safety for
the prevention of HAE attacks in the pivotal phase 3 trial (CS5). Refer to Section 6 for more details.
80 mg SC Q4W was the highest dose tested in the phase 3 trial (CS5). One subject received 100 mg Q4W in Trial
CS3, an open-label extension to the phase 2 trial (CS2).
Donidalorsen AUCtau,ss increased in a greater than dose-proportional manner between dosages of 20 mg Q4W and
80 mg Q4W. Donidalorsen AUCtau,ss increased by about 6-fold for a 4-fold increase in dose.
No accumulation in Cmax and AUC was observed following administration of 4 doses of 80 mg Q4W donidalorsen in
healthy subjects as well as in subjects with HAE. However, a 2-fold increase in mean Ctrough was observed in both
healthy subjects and subjects with HAE at steady state. Of note, the observed Ctrough is about 1% of the value of
Cmax.
The steady-state Ctrough following administration of 80 mg Q4W was reached by Day 85 for healthy subjects and by
Day 113 for subjects with HAE. The steady state for change from baseline in plasma PKK was reached by around
Day 85 in subjects with HAE following administration of 80 mg Q4W or Q8W donidalorsen.
The drug product used in clinical trials was a vial product while the to-be-marketed formulation is proposed as a
prefilled syringe with autoinjector. Bioequivalence based on Cmax and AUC between the drug product presentations
was demonstrated in Trial CS9 conducted in healthy subjects.
Absorption
Absolute bioavailability after SC administration of donidalorsen has not been determined.
Following a single SC dose of 80 mg in healthy subjects, the median (range) T max for donidalorsen in plasma is
2 (0.25, 8) hours.
Not applicable.

Distribution
Central compartment volume (Vc/F) is 69.8 L
Peripheral compartment volume (Vp/F) is 1840 L
Donidalorsen is highly plasma protein bound (>98%) with minimal change in protein binding over a concentration
range of 5 to 150 µg/mL.
Donidalorsen is not a substrate of P-gp, BCRP, OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE1,
MATE2K, and BSEP.
THA-linker major metabolite M8 is not a substrate of OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, MATE1, MATE2-K,
BCRP, and P-gp. However, M8 is a substrate of BSEP and OATP1B3.

Drug Information
Elimination
Human mass balance study was not conducted.
Apparent clearance (CL/F) is 12.8 L/h
Terminal elimination half-life is 31.4 days, which likely reflects the half-life in tissue (i.e., liver). The apparent half-life
in plasma, reflecting tissue distribution, is estimated to be 4 to 5 hours.
The unconjugated ASO portion is expected to be metabolized by endo-and exo-nucleases to form fragmented
oligonucleotide metabolites. The GalNAc-THA linker moiety is hydrolyzed intracellularly following uptake into tissue.
After hydrolysis, GalNAc sugars undergo endogenous carbohydrate catabolism, while the THA linker undergoes
oxidative metabolism. No specific CYP enzyme was identified to majorly contribute to the metabolism of
donidalorsen. Minimal linker-related metabolites (e.g., M8 and M12) were detected in human plasma, with mean
concentrations <2% of those determined for parent drug at 2-hours postdose.
The mean fraction of donidalorsen (including fully conjugated, partially conjugated, and unconjugated donidalorsen)
excreted in the urine within 24 hours is <1% of the administered dose in healthy subjects. The fragmented
oligonucleotide metabolites formed by metabolism of unconjugated ASO are excreted in urine or feces. Metabolites
of the THA linker are also excreted in the urine, representing ≤6.4% of the dose detected in urine samples collected
over 24 hours following the four doses of 80 mg Q4W on Day 85.
Intrinsic Factors and Specific Populations
No clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were observed
based on body weight (37 to 152 kg).
Based on population PK analysis, the estimated steady-state plasma donidalorsen systemic exposure (Cmax,ss,
AUCtau,ss and Ctrough,ss) in a subject weighing 100 kg is about 38% to 54% lower as compared to that in a subject
weighing 70 kg.
No clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were observed
based on age (12 to 68 years).
No clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were observed
in subjects with mild renal impairment (i.e., eGFR ≥60 to <90 mL/min/1.73 m2) compared to subjects with normal
renal function.
Donidalorsen was not studied in subjects with moderate renal impairment, severe renal impairment, or ESRD.
No clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were observed
in subjects with mild hepatic impairment (defined using NCI-ODWG criteria: total bilirubin ≤1× ULN and AST >1×
ULN, or total bilirubin >1 to 1.5× ULN and any AST) compared to subjects with normal hepatic function.
Donidalorsen was not evaluated in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Given that the site of
action of donidalorsen is in the liver, the long-term safety and efficacy in patients with moderate or severe hepatic
impairment is not known.

Immunogenicity (if Applicable)
Antidrug antibodies against donidalorsen in human plasma were assessed using a validated multitiered ELISA.
In the pivotal trial (CS5) with a treatment duration of 24 weeks, the incidence rates of treatment-emergent ADAs
were 20% (9 out of 45 subjects) and 22% (5 out of 23 subjects) among subjects who received donidalorsen 80 mg
Q4W and 80 mg Q8W, respectively.
In the ongoing OLE trial (CS7), subjects who were rolled over from Trial CS5 continued treatment with donidalorsen
in 80 mg Q4W or Q8W groups for up to 3 years (median exposure duration of 227 days). The incidence rate of
treatment-emergent ADAs was 35% (22 of 63 subjects) in the Q4W group, including subjects initially randomized to
Q4W (36%, 16 out of 44 subjects) in Trial CS5 and subjects initially randomized to placebo in Trial CS5 (32%, 6 out
of 19 subjects). The incidence rate of treatment-emergent ADAs was 21% (3 of 14 subjects) among subjects who
received Q8W in both Trial CS5 and Trial CS7.
The presence of ADAs was not found to impact the pharmacodynamics (i.e., change from baseline in plasma PKK),
safety, or efficacy of donidalorsen. An increase in donidalorsen plasma C trough was observed in ADA-positive
subjects with high titers. Because of the small sample size, the effect of ADAs on the PK, PD, safety, and
effectiveness of donidalorsen is inconclusive.

Trial CS3
Switching from the donidalorsen-4 to donidalorsen-8 dosing regimen was investigated in the
open-label Trial CS3 (an extension of the phase 2 trial [CS2]). In Trial CS3, Rollover subjects
from Trial CS2 initially entered a 12-week Fixed Treatment Period where all subjects received
the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen. Following completion of the Fixed Treatment Period, the
dosing regimen could be switched in the subsequent Flexible Dosing Period. For additional
details, refer to Section 14.2.5. In Trial CS3, eight subjects who were attack free for at least 12
weeks on the donidalorsen-4 regimen during the Fixed Treatment Period were switched to the
less frequent donidalorsen-8 regimen during the Flexible Treatment Period. However, three of
these eight subjects switched back to the donidalorsen-4 regimen due to experiencing HAE
attacks.
Thus, based on observations from Trial CS3, it is not clear that subjects who were responsive on
the donidalorsen-4 regimen would also be responsive to the donidalorsen-8 regimen. Therefore,
as three out of eight subjects experienced an HAE attack after extension of the dosing interval
despite being controlled for >12 weeks on the donidalorsen-4 regimen, the available data are not
sufficient to support a recommendation to switch from the donidalorsen-4 to the donidalorsen-8
regimen based on HAE attack incidence. Given that HAE is a heterogeneous disease, the
response from the more frequent donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen may not be predictive of who
may benefit from the longer donidalorsen-8 dosing interval.
Although a positive dose-response relationship was observed in Trial CS5 between the
donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens, both for the mean percent reduction from
baseline in plasma PKK concentrations and HAE attack rate, variability in these responses was
observed at the individual level within each dosing group (Figure 2 and Figure 3). The data
suggest that there is heterogeneity in the disease and response to donidalorsen. While the
reduction in plasma PKK trough concentrations following donidalorsen treatment was generally
associated with the reduction in HAE attack rate, there are no dedicated data showing a clear
association between the magnitude of change from baseline in plasma PKK trough concentration
and HAE attack rate at the individual level.
Taken together, the effectiveness of both the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens
compared to placebo are supported by efficacy data from the pivotal trial (CS5). However, the
available data do not support the switch from the donidalorsen-4 to the donidalorsen-8 dosing
29
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
regimens for all subjects who are responsive with the donidalorsen-4 regimen. The positive doseresponse relationship between donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 observed in CS5 supported
that donidalorsen-4 is the preferred regimen. In addition, as there were subjects who remained
controlled and continued treatment with donidalorsen-8 when rolling over from CS5 to CS7,
donidalorsen-8 regimen may also be considered.

6.2. Clinical Studies/Trials Intended To
Demonstrate Efficacy
6.2.1. Results of Pooled Analyses
The evaluation of efficacy was based on the analyses of the individual trials. Pooled efficacy
analyses will not be discussed in this review.

6.2.2. Trial CS5
6.2.2.1. Design and Conduct, Trial CS5
Results of the pivotal trial (CS5) served as the basis for efficacy evaluation. This was a 24-week,
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, phase 3 trial that
treated 90 subjects aged 12 years or older with Type I or II HAE who had ≥2 HAE attacks during
the Screening Period. Subjects were randomized 2:1 to either Cohort A (donidalorsen-4 or
matched placebo) or Cohort B (donidalorsen-8 or matched placebo), respectively (see Figure 4).
Within each cohort, subjects were randomized 3:1 to receive donidalorsen or a matching volume
of placebo. Treatment was provided over a 24-week Treatment Period. Data from subjects
receiving placebo in Cohorts A and B were pooled for analyses, and this is referred to as the
pooled placebo group for primary analyses.

randomized to begin trial treatment as soon as the subject experienced ≥2 HAE attacks during
the Screening Period.

The overall design of Trial CS5 is consistent with previous programs for HAE prophylaxis. The
duration of the controlled Treatment Period (24 weeks) is acceptable for this indication.
Concomitant Medications
Consistent with the eligibility criteria, continued use of a stable dose of androgens or tranexamic
acid for HAE prophylaxis was allowed while on trial; this differs from some HAE products’
development programs, which disallow the use of these agents. Once enrolled, including during
the Screening Period, subjects were not allowed to use other HAE prophylaxis agents, such as
lanadelumab or berotralstat. Other disallowed concomitant therapies included angiotensinconverting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and estrogen-containing medications with systemic
absorption.
Subjects were required to have access to, and the ability to use, on-demand medication to treat
acute HAE attacks, per the recommendation of their treating physician.
Primary Objective and Endpoint
The primary objective of Trial CS5 was to evaluate the efficacy of donidalorsen as prophylaxis
in patients with HAE. The primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized number of
investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks during the Treatment Period (from Week 1 to
Week 25) for the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo. The primary endpoint was
calculated per subject as:
[number of HAE attacks ÷ length subject contributed to analysis period in days] ×28
Length subject contributed to analysis period (in days) was calculated as:
[End date of Treatment Period (if completed) or Date of 25 weeks after first dose (if did not
complete) or Date of follow-up discontinuation or Date of end of participation (whichever is
first)] − Date of first dose
Treatment Period in the above formula is defined as the period from the first dose date/time to
the last dose date/time +28 days for Cohort A and +56 days for Cohort B.
The selected primary endpoint is acceptable and consistent with previous programs for HAE
prophylaxis.

The secondary endpoints encompass the most clinically relevant endpoints that are typically
evaluated in HAE prophylaxis programs. Some objectives/endpoints aimed to evaluate quality of
life via the clinical outcome tools AE-QoL and AECT. These tools have not been found to be fitfor-purpose for the regulatory assessment of efficacy in HAE (see Section 6.2.2.4.6.2), and as
such, these endpoints are not appropriate to support efficacy or appear in product labeling.
6.2.2.2. Eligibility Criteria, Trial CS5
Key eligibility criteria are summarized below. Trial CS5 enrolled subjects ≥12 years of age with
clinically confirmed HAE and an attack frequency that would likely warrant prophylactic HAE
therapy. The inclusion and exclusion criteria are acceptable and consistent with those used in
previous trials of approved products for HAE prophylaxis.

Key Inclusion Criteria


Male or female ≥12 years of age at the time of informed consent.



Diagnosed with clinically confirmed C1-INH (Type I or Type II) HAE based on all of the
following:
– Documented clinical history consistent with HAE (SC or mucosal, nonpruritic swelling
episodes without accompanying urticaria).
– C1-INH functional level <40% normal level. Patients with a functional level of 40% to
50% of normal could be enrolled if their complement factor C4 level was below the
lower limit of normal (LLN) or when a known pathogenic mutation in the SERPING1
gene had been demonstrated.
– At least one of the following: age at HAE onset ≤30 years, family history consistent with
Type I or II HAE, or complement component 1q within the normal range.



Experienced ≥2 HAE attacks during the Screening Period.



Female subjects: nonpregnant, nonlactating, and either surgically sterile, postmenopausal,
abstinent, or using acceptable contraceptive methods.



Male subjects: either surgically sterile or using an acceptable contraceptive method.

Key Exclusion Criteria


Concomitant diagnosis of another form of angioedema, such as idiopathic or acquired
angioedema, recurrent angioedema associated with urticaria, or Type III HAE.



Exposure to any of the following medications:
– ACE inhibitors or any estrogen containing medications with systemic absorption (such as
oral contraceptive or hormonal replacement therapy) within 4 weeks prior to Screening.
– Chronic prophylaxis with Takhzyro® (lanadelumab), Haegarda® (C1-esterase inhibitor
SQ), Cinryze® and Ruconest® (C1 esterase inhibitor), or Orladeyo® (berotralstat) within
5 half-lives prior to Screening (i.e., Takhzyro within 10 weeks prior to Screening,
Haegarda/Berinert 2000/3000® subcutaneously/Cinryze/Ruconest within 2 weeks prior
to Screening, or Orladeyo within 3 weeks prior to Screening).
– Oligonucleotides within 4 months of Screening (if a single administration) or 12 months
of Screening (if multiple doses received); does not apply to vaccines.

6.2.2.3. Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial CS5

The statistical analysis plan (SAP) for Trial CS5 was Version 2 dated December 13, 2023. The
primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized HAE attack rate per month (28 days)
comparing the donidalorsen-4 group to pooled placebo for the full analysis set (FAS). The FAS
was defined as all randomized subjects who received at least one dose of trial drug; subjects were
analyzed according to the treatment group to which they were randomized. The definition of the
Safety set was the same as the FAS. Only investigator-confirmed HAE attacks were included in
the evaluation of efficacy for all primary and secondary endpoints. Treatment policy strategy was
used for the intercurrent events of use of not allowed concomitant therapy or procedures and
early termination of treatment, which included subjects escaping early to the OLE trial (CS7) due
to experiencing ≥5 recurrent HAE attacks per month for 2 consecutive months during the
Treatment Period, subjects discontinuing the trial treatment early due to recurrent HAE attacks
and not enrolling in Trial CS7, and subjects discontinuing trial treatment early due to COVID-19
or war-related events.
Primary Analysis
The primary analysis used a Poisson regression model and Pearson chi-square scaling of
standard errors to account for potential overdispersion on the FAS, including subjects from the
donidalorsen-4, donidalorsen-8, and pooled placebo groups. The model included fixed effects for
treatment group (three categories), baseline (the time-normalized Run-In Period attack rate,
continuous), and the treatment-by-baseline interaction as covariates, and the logarithm of time
each subject was observed from Week 1 to Week 25 as an offset variable.
From this model, the least squares mean rate, the standard error, and the corresponding 95%
confidence interval for each treatment group, as well as the model adjusted mean rate ratios of
donidalorsen-4 relative to the pooled placebo group and the corresponding 95% confidence
interval were estimated. The comparison between donidalorsen-8 and pooled placebo was
calculated from this model as a key secondary endpoint. These estimates were reported as mean
37
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
event rates per 4 weeks by transforming the estimates using the exponential function. The pvalue of the Wald-based chi-square test was reported for testing the hypothesis.
The percentage difference in mean HAE attack rate between donidalorsen-4 and the pooled
placebo was calculated as 100%× (model adjusted mean rate ratio –1). Similarly, the estimated
upper and lower confidence limits for the model adjusted mean rate ratio were transformed by
subtracting 1 and multiplying by 100% to calculate 95% confidence intervals for the percentage
change.
Sensitivity and Supplementary Analyses
A sensitivity analysis was prespecified that investigated whether the results for the primary
endpoint were robust to departures from the assumption that the mean and variance are equal, as
in Poisson regression. The analysis was the same as the primary analysis, except that negative
binomial regression was performed instead of Poisson regression.
The primary analysis assumed missing data were missing at random for subjects who
discontinued the Treatment Period early. A sensitivity analysis was prespecified to investigate
the robustness of the conclusions to the missing at random assumption. The analysis was
performed on imputed data by using a multiple imputation method assuming jump to reference,
used the Poisson regression model of the primary analysis, and combined the results using
Rubin’s rules.
A tipping point sensitivity analysis was prespecified to investigate the effect of missing data on
the reliability of the primary efficacy analysis. A range of progressively more conservative
assumptions about the number of events occurring in the post withdrawal period was explored to
search for the assumption which would reverse the conclusion.
A supplementary analysis repeated the primary analysis and the negative binomial sensitivity
analysis on the per-protocol set, which included all subjects in the FAS who were treated
according to the protocol without any major deviations that could compromise the interpretation
of efficacy.
Subgroup Analyses
The Applicant prespecified subgroup analyses based on the following:


Age category in years (12 to 17, 18 to 39, 40 to 64, ≥65)



Sex (male, female)



Race (Caucasian, Other)



Regions (North America, Europe, Middle East)



Taken any predefined prophylactic therapy, including lanadelumab, berotralstat, C1-esterase
inhibitor? (Yes, No)

The Agency conducted subgroup analyses by race (American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian,
Black or African American, Multiple, White, Other), by ethnicity (Hispanic or Latino, Not
38
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Hispanic or Latino), and by HAE type (Type I, Type II). The final SAP specified that HAE
attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to Week 25 would be summarized by each subgroup. The
primary endpoint was also analyzed by adding region and the interaction of region and treatment
group as covariates. The Agency analyzed all other subgroups similarly to the prespecified
analysis of region.
A subgroup analyses that excluded subjects considered to be not “typical patients” was
prespecified. These subjects were identified prior to trial unblinding based on clinical history
and/or Screening Period characteristics considered to be atypical for Type I/II HAE. The
analyses restricted the analysis set to “typical patients” and reevaluated the primary endpoint of
time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to 25, as well as the
secondary endpoints from Week 5 to 25 of time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4
weeks), time-normalized number of moderate or severe HAE attacks (per 4 weeks), and timenormalized number of HAE attacks requiring acute therapy (per 4 weeks).
Additional analyses by HAE attack location and severity were completed by the Agency to
inform regulatory decision-making, presented in Section 6.2.2.4.6.4.
Secondary Endpoints
The Applicant prespecified key secondary endpoints for both the comparison between
donidalorsen-4 and pooled placebo, and the comparison between donidalorsen-8 and pooled
placebo. All methods used data from all subjects in the FAS and for each endpoint the same
model was used to calculate comparisons between both treatment groups and pooled placebo.
Section 6.2.2.1 describes the order of multiplicity-controlled hierarchical testing of the secondary
endpoints. At each level of the hierarchy, a test was performed at two-sided alpha of 5% if the
test of the previous null hypothesis was rejected.
The time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 5 to Week 25 was
analyzed using the same methods as described for the primary efficacy endpoint, based on the
Poisson regression model on FAS with the treatment policy strategy. The time-normalized
number of moderate or severe HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 5 to Week 25 and the timenormalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) requiring acute therapy from Week 5 to Week
25 were analyzed similarly.
A responder analysis was conducted for subjects who achieved a clinical response, defined as a
≥70% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate. The percentage reduction is defined as:
(Postbaseline rate − Baseline rate) ÷ Baseline rate ×100%
The postbaseline is the HAE attack rate from Week 5 to Week 25 and baseline is Run-In Period
HAE attack rate.
The odds ratio, corresponding 95% confidence intervals, and p-value were calculated using a
logistic regression model with the baseline, treatment, and the treatment by-baseline interaction
as covariates. The clinical response of HAE attack-free from Week 5 to Week 25 was analyzed
using a similar logistic regression model. Exploratory analyses which defined clinical response
as ≥50% and ≥90% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate were conducted similarly.

6.2.2.4.1. Subject Disposition, Trial CS5
Disposition information is presented in Table 8 and Table 9. A total of 91 subjects were
randomized. One subject withdrew consent prior to receiving trial drug and 90 subjects received
at least one dose of trial drug. Lack of efficacy was defined per protocol as subjects who
experienced at least five HAE attacks per month for 2 consecutive months after Week 5. One
subject in each of the donidalorsen groups and three subjects in the pooled placebo group
discontinued the trial drug due to lack of efficacy, and these subjects were rolled over into the
open-label extension trial (CS7). One subject in the donidalorsen-8 group discontinued trial drug
due to the adverse event of ALT increased. One subject in the pooled placebo group discontinued
trial drug due to pregnancy.
Most subjects completed the Trial CS5 treatment and then rolled over to Trial CS7 for open-label
extended treatment.

6.2.2.4.2. Baseline Demographics and Clinical
Characteristics, Trial CS5
The demographics and clinical characteristics of the Full Analysis Set at baseline are
summarized in Table 10 and were reasonably similar between the treatment groups given the
small sample size. Seven adolescents were enrolled, with none randomized to the placebo group;
acknowledging that this is small, note that the pathophysiology of HAE Type I or II is similar
across age groups. Racial and ethnic group representation in Trial CS5 is congruent with the
overall subject population. Most subjects had Type I HAE (93%) and a history of laryngeal HAE
attacks (52%; data not shown). Some subjects (17%) were previously on prophylaxis treatment.
A total of seven (8%) subjects continued their allowed androgen or tranexamic acid prophylaxis
(six (7%) on danazol and one (1%) on tranexamic acid; data not shown). Enrollment occurred at
sites in the United States (20%) and outside the United States.

6.2.2.4.3. Primary Efficacy Results, Trial CS5
The primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks
from Week 1 to Week 25. This endpoint is clinically meaningful and consistent with previous
programs for HAE prophylaxis. Details regarding the reporting, collection, and investigator
confirmation of HAE attacks are provided in Section 15.1.1.
Table 11 summarizes the efficacy results for the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per
4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 25 for the primary endpoint comparison between donidalorsen-4
and pooled placebo, as well as the key secondary results for the comparison between
donidalorsen-8 and pooled placebo. Note that the latter comparison was tested eighth in the
Applicant’s prespecified testing hierarchy, and all preceding endpoints achieved statistical
significance. After adjusting for baseline attack rate by treatment group, the estimated least
square mean time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks was lower in both the
donidalorsen-4 (LS mean =0.44, 95% CI =0.27, 0.73) and donidalorsen-8 (LS mean =1.02, 95%
CI =0.65, 1.59) groups compared to pooled placebo (LS mean =2.26, 95% CI =1.66, 3.09). The
estimated attack rate ratio relative to placebo was 0.19 (95% CI =0.11, 0.35) for the
donidalorsen-4 group and 0.45 (95% CI =0.26, 0.78) for the donidalorsen-8 group. Additionally,
the percentage reduction in the means for the donidalorsen-4 group was 81% (95% CI =65%,
89%) and for the donidalorsen-8 group was 55% (95% CI =22%, 74%) relative to placebo.

6.2.2.4.4. Key Secondary Efficacy Results, Trial CS5
Table 12 presents the results for the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from
Week 5 to Week 25 for the comparison of both donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 to pooled
placebo. After adjusting for baseline attack rate by treatment group, the estimated least square
mean time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks was lower in both the donidalorsen-4
(LS mean =0.30, 95% CI =0.15, 0.58) and donidalorsen-8 (LS mean =0.90 95% CI =0.53, 1.52)
groups compared to pooled placebo (LS mean =2.25, 95% CI =1.59, 3.18). The estimated attack
rate ratio relative to placebo was 0.13 (95% CI =0.06, 0.28) for the donidalorsen-4 group and
0.40 (95% CI =0.21, 0.75) for the donidalorsen-8 group. Additionally, the percentage reduction
in the means for the donidalorsen-4 group was 87% (95% CI =72%, 94%) and for the
donidalorsen-8 group was 60% (95% CI =25%, 79%) relative to placebo. The results of analyses
of this secondary endpoint agree with the primary efficacy results. This provides limited
additional information for evidence of effectiveness of the trial drug as it is the same as the
primary endpoint with a shortened time window starting at Week 5.

to the limited enrollment of subjects aged 65 years and older (n=2; one enrolled in each
donidalorsen treatment arm, 0 randomized to placebo). Although efficacy in this age group has
not been established by direct evidence, it may be inferred from the overall efficacy results.
Conclusion
The interpretation of the subgroup analyses above is limited by small sample sizes. However, the
treatment benefit of donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 based on the primary endpoint appears to
be similar across subgroups based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, region, predefined prophylactic
use, and HAE type.
6.2.2.4.6. Additional Efficacy Analyses, Trial CS5
6.2.2.4.6.1. Sensitivity Analysis, Trial CS5
Results of the sensitivity analyses based on negative binomial regression and multiple imputation
using jump to reference were consistent with the primary analysis of the primary endpoint of
time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to 25.
The number of subjects who discontinued early from the FAS was four in the pooled placebo
group, one in the donidalorsen-4 group, and two in the donidalorsen-8 group. Of these subjects,
three had at least 5 months of follow-up, three had between 3 and 5 months of follow-up, and
one had almost 3 months of follow-up. The tipping point analysis investigated the effect of this
missing data on the results of the primary analysis. The range of plausible assumptions explored
did not identify a tipping point that would reverse the conclusion of the primary analysis.
Six subjects who were from the FAS were excluded from the per-protocol set. Results of the
supplementary analysis based on the per-protocol set using both Poisson and negative binomial
regression were consistent with the primary analysis.

6.2.2.4.6.2. Angioedema Quality of Life Total Score,
Trial CS5
Issue
Determine whether the AE-QoL total score is fit-for-purpose for the context of use, that is, to
(b) (4)
support regulatory evaluation of effectiveness
(b) (4)

Background
HAE is characterized by unpredictable, recurrent episodes of angioedema, which impact quality
of life and daily functioning. At the HAE Patient-Focused Drug Development meeting held at
the Agency on September 25, 2017 (CBER 2018), patients with HAE shared the aspects of the
disease that had the greatest impact on their lives, including the unpredictability of attack
occurrence, the painful abdominal attacks, the dramatic change swelling had on their physical
appearance, and the emotional toll the disease had on their lives.
(b) (4)
The AE-QoL was used to derive secondary and exploratory endpoints,
(b) (4) There is currently no fit-for-purpose
patient-reported outcomes (PROs) for use in HAE prophylaxis clinical trials.

During the course of the donidalorsen clinical development program, other developers of HAE
therapies have also positioned AE-QoL as supportive of efficacy in their respective programs.
During the FDA review of another prophylaxis HAE product, AE-QoL total score was reviewed
by the Division of Clinical Outcomes Assessment (DCOA). Important deficiencies with the
COA tool were identified, rendering AE-QoL unfit for purpose for the regulatory evaluation of
efficacy. These deficiencies (outlined below) cannot be overcome with the supportive evidence
dossier provided in the donidalorsen NDA.
Assessment
During development, the Applicant requested Agency feedback on the AE-QoL and endpoints.
The NDA submission includes exact copies of the tool, associated materials, and a supportive
evidence dossier.
The AE-QoL questionnaire was developed to assess quality of life impairment in recurrent
angioedema patients, including patients with HAE (Weller et al. 2012). This 17-item instrument
uses a 5-point Likert scale with response options of never, rarely, sometimes, often, and very
often, rated over a recall period of the last 4 weeks. The 17 items within the AE-QoL are
organized into 4 distinct domains labeled as follows: functioning, fatigue/mood, fears/shame, and
food/nutrition.
Each domain has its own score, and a total score can also be calculated. The items are scored
from 0 to 4, and they are summed to provide raw domain scores, which are then transformed into
linear scores ranging from 0 to 100. The total score is the sum of all 17 items. Higher scores in
the AE-QoL domains and total scores indicate greater levels of impairment of quality of life. In

51
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Trial CS5, the AE-QoL was administered using electronic forms, displayed via a tablet device,
on Days 1, 85, and 169 in the Treatment Period, and on Day 91 of the Post-Treatment Period.
There is inadequate qualitative evidence in the published literature, including
(Weller et al. 2012), to support the content validity of the AE-QoL for efficacy evaluation in the
Applicant’s drug development program. In addition, the domains of the AE-QoL are not welldefined and reliable to inform regulatory decision-making. Specifically, for the AE-QoL
functioning domain, asking patients about restrictions in their daily lives due to swelling
episodes, regardless of whether or not they have actually experienced swelling episodes during
the 4-week recall period, will not provide useful information for assessing treatment benefit in
the context of a clinical trial. While the core concepts of disease-related symptoms and physical
function are reasonable PRO measurement strategies for demonstrating treatment benefit,
emotional impacts (such as anxiety and embarrassment) as assessed by the AE-QoL fears/shame
domain are distal concepts, and as such, they may be affected by factors external to HAE disease
or effect of the investigational product. In addition, the 4-week recall period of the AE-QoL is
not appropriate as patients may not reliably recall the occurrence of their HAE attacks during this
timeframe. As such, the AE-QoL is not content valid for this context of use.
Conclusion
Based on the construction of the instrument, the AE-QoL is not well-defined and reliable to
(b) (4)
inform regulatory decision-making
6.2.2.4.6.3. Adequacy of Trial Blinding, Trial CS5
Issue
Trial CS5 studied two different dosing regimens: donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8.
Donidalorsen 80 mg was matched to a placebo group with the same dosing regimen. Subjects
and investigators were aware of the assigned dosing regimen. An alternative design to maintain
blinding to the dosing regimen is double dummy dosing, in which all subjects take either placebo
or the donidalorsen-4 regimen. In the absence of double dummy dosing, it is of interest to
examine the sensitivity of the results to the assumption that the two placebo groups were
equivalent and trial blinding was adequate.
Background
Trial blinding is a fundamental feature of removing bias from experimental results. Because
subjects in Trial CS5 were blinded to receipt of drug versus placebo but were aware if their
dosing interval was donidalorsen-4 or donidalorsen-8, we sought to evaluate any potential bias
introduced to the efficacy results by awareness of dosing interval.
Assessment
As an exploratory analysis, the Agency analyzed the time-normalized HAE attack rate (per 4weeks) as in the primary analysis except that the placebo every 4 weeks and placebo every 8
weeks arms were considered as separate treatment groups. The comparison of each donidalorsen
52
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
80-mg regimen was to its matched placebo. The results of this analysis are presented in Table 17.
Although the confidence intervals are wider for this exploratory analysis than in the primary
analysis (Table 11), the conclusions remain unchanged. This supports the robustness of the
results despite the lack of blinding to the treatment interval. Additionally, an investigatorconfirmed HAE attack is considered an objective clinical outcome, and as such, less susceptible
to bias from knowledge of assigned treatment interval.

Compared to matched placebo means that the donidalorsen 80 mg every 8 weeks group is compared to placebo every 8 weeks

b
The Run-In Period (Screening) HAE attack rate (per 4 weeks) for each subject was calculated as the number of HAE attacks that

by 28.
c
The time-normalized HAE attack rate (per 4 weeks) was calculated as number of HAE attacks that occurred from Week 1 to Week
25, divided by the number of days the subject contributed to that period, and then multiplied by 28.

The Poisson regression model included treatment groups, baseline (the Run-In Period HAE attack rate), the treatment-by-baseline
interaction as a covariate, and the logarithm of time in every 4 weeks that each subject was observed from Week 1 to Week 25 used
as an offset variable (e.g., log (6) if the subject stayed in the trial for 24 weeks). Pearson chi-square scaling of standard errors was
used to account for potential overdispersion.
e
The percentage difference in mean HAE attack rate between donidalorsen 80 mg and placebo groups were calculated as 100% ×
(mean rate ratio -1). Similarly, the estimated upper and lower confidence limits for the mean rate ratio can be transformed by
subtracting 1 and multiplying by 100% to calculate 95% confidence intervals for the percentage change.

Conclusion
The Trial CS5 efficacy results do not appear to have been impacted by the lack of blinding to
dosing interval.

6.2.2.4.6.4. Efficacy in Reducing HAE Attacks by
Location, Trial CS5
Issue
An exploratory analysis of efficacy of donidalorsen in reducing HAE attack incidence, analyzed
by anatomic location of the attack, was conducted.
Background
HAE attacks can result in serious and/or life-threatening sequelae if they affect certain anatomic
locations, particularly the larynx. Laryngeal attacks can result in asphyxiation and death. Given
this potentially serious outcome, we sought to analyze the efficacy by anatomic location of HAE
attacks that occurred during Trial CS5.
Assessment
A summary of the history of attacks by location (abdominal, laryngeal, peripheral) is provided in
Table 18. Almost all subjects had a history of abdominal (94%) and peripheral (94%) attacks,
and the majority of subjects had a history of laryngeal attacks (52%).
A summary of the HAE attacks experienced during the Treatment Period by location and
severity is provided in Table 19. The percentage of subjects experiencing abdominal attacks
(regardless of severity) were approximately equal in all three treatment groups, while a lower
percentage of subjects experienced laryngeal or peripheral attacks in the donidalorsen-4 and
donidalorsen-8 groups compared to placebo. Few subjects experienced laryngeal attacks, so
limited conclusions can be drawn from this data. The severity of attacks in each location
followed a trend consistent with the results regardless of severity.

6.2.2.4.6.5. Durability of Treatment Effect, Trial CS5
Issue
Because HAE is a chronic disease, the durability of the efficacy of donidalorsen is of particular
interest and was explored during the development program.
Background
The Applicant conducted two OLE trials: Trial CS7 (extension of the pivotal trial [CS5]) and
Trial CS3 (extension of the phase 2 trial [CS2]). See Table 3 for more information. Long-term
data from these trials allowed for exploration of durability of efficacy.
Assessment
A total of 44 subjects on the donidalorsen-4 regimen for Trial CS5 were enrolled in the openlabel extension trial (CS7) and continued the donidalorsen-4 regimen. An additional 14 subjects
on the donidalorsen-8 regimen for Trial CS5 who were attack-free for Weeks 17 to 25 were
enrolled in the open-label extension Trial (CS7) and continued on the donidalorsen-8 regimen.
Figure 9 presents the mean time-normalized HAE attack rate (per 4-weeks) during Trial CS5 and
Trial CS7 for these subject groups.

Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)

Abbreviations: HAE, hereditary angioedema; n, number of subjects

The time-normalized HAE attack rate was generally consistent across Trial CS7 for the subjects
who maintained the treatment as assigned in Trial CS5. However, Trial CS7 lacks a control
group and blinding, and therefore these results should be interpreted with caution. Additionally,
caution is needed in interpreting the results for the donidalorsen-8 group because the subjects
who continued on the donidalorsen-8 regimen in Trial CS7 were a subset of the subjects
randomized to the donidalorsen-8 regimen in Trial CS5. Subjects who experienced an HAE
attack during Weeks 17 to 25 of Trial CS5 were switched to the donidalorsen-4 regimen for Trial
CS7 and their data are not examined here in the evaluation of the durability of the treatment
effect.
Although small in sample size, long-term data from Trial CS3 (not presented) were consistent
with the results of Trial CS7 and supportive of the durability of efficacy.
Conclusion
While the OLE trial data are limited by the lack of randomization or a control comparator, due to
the well-established natural history of HAE, these data remain useful for characterizing the
durability of effectiveness over the longer treatment duration. The HAE attack rate in Trial CS7
supports the longer-term durability of efficacy of donidalorsen, at both donidalorsen-4 and
donidalorsen-8 dosing intervals, for HAE.

6.3. Key Efficacy Review Issues
6.3.1. Dosing Interval

(b) (4)

Issue
The Applicant proposed a dosing interval extension from donidalorsen-4 to donidalorsen-8 in
subjects who are attack free with donidalorsen-4 for at least 3 months. The proposed labeling
language for dosing states: “The recommended dosage of donidalorsen is 80 mg administered
(b) (4)
subcutaneously
(b) (4)
(b) (4)

”

Background
The pivotal phase 3, placebo-controlled trial (CS5) evaluated both safety and efficacy of two
dosing regimens (donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8) in comparison to placebo. The phase 2,
open-label extension trial (CS3) enrolled Rollover subjects from the phase 2 trial (CS2) who
previously received either placebo or the donidalorsen-4 regimen and placed them all in the
donidalorsen-4 regimen for 12 weeks; subjects then either continued the donidalorsen-4 regimen
or received the donidalorsen-8 regimen based on clinical response. The phase 3, open-label
extension trial (CS7) included enrollment of Rollover subjects from the phase 3 trial (CS5) who
previously received the donidalorsen-8 regimen and placed them on the donidalorsen-8 regimen
if they are attack free for ≥8 weeks (Weeks 17 to 25 in Trial CS5) and otherwise placed them on
the donidalorsen-4 regimen.
Assessment
Both the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens demonstrated significantly better
efficacy compared to placebo based on the results of Trial CS5. On the primary endpoint, the
donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 regimens showed greater reduction in HAE attack rate
compared to placebo (−81% and −55%, respectively [Table 11]). Thus, the donidalorsen-4
demonstrated greater efficacy compared to donidalorsen-8, but both dosing intervals can be
considered effective.
PK/PD results from Trial CS5 showed that the mean donidalorsen steady-state trough
concentrations following administration of donidalorsen-4 (0.81 ng/mL) was about 2-fold higher
than that following administration of donidalorsen-8 (0.39 ng/mL). In addition, the mean percent
reduction from baseline in PKK following the donidalorsen-4 regimen was numerically greater
than that following the donidalorsen-8 regimen during the Treatment Period (at Week 25:
−73.8% and −47.2% for donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8, respectively). The smaller PKK
reduction following the donidalorsen-8 compared to the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen is
consistent with the dose response relationship for efficacy between these two regimens. Despite
the positive dose-response relationship observed for mean change from baseline in plasma PKK
trough concentrations and HAE attack rate, there was variability in these responses at the
individual level, suggesting heterogeneity in the disease and response to donidalorsen. While the
reduction in plasma PKK trough concentrations following donidalorsen treatment was generally
58
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
associated with the reduction in HAE attack rate, there are no dedicated data showing clear
association between the magnitude of change from baseline in plasma PKK trough concentration
and HAE attack rate at the individual level. See Section 6.1 for more details.
For subjects in the donidalorsen-8 group, fluctuations were observed in the change from baseline
in plasma PKK trough concentrations, with an increase in PKK trough concentrations observed
just prior to administration of the next dose (i.e., at Week 9 and Week 17). The data suggest that
this fluctuation may be associated with the longer dosing interval. Nevertheless, the fluctuation
in PKK reduction did not appear to affect clinical response, as no increase in HAE attacks was
observed at predose, around the time when PKK was increased (in the donidalorsen-8 group).
See Section 14 for more details.
Subjects who were attack-free with donidalorsen-4 for ≥12 weeks may not respond well with
donidalorsen-8 based on Trial CS3, as three out of eight subjects who switched from the
donidalorsen-4 to the donidalorsen-8 regimen switched back to the donidalorsen-4 regimen due
to experiencing an HAE attack. Despite the small sample size leading to limited data, the
Applicant’s proposal to switch regimens if “attack free for at least 3 months” does not appear to
be well supported.
Subjects who were attack free with donidalorsen-8 for Weeks 17 to 25 in Trial CS5 and rolled
over to Trial CS7 on donidalorsen-8 (n=14) had a mean baseline HAE attack rate of 2.87 (SD
2.06) per 4 weeks and mean of 32.6 (SD 19.3) HAE attacks in the 12 months prior to Screening
in Trial CS5. This group was comprised of five females (36%) and had a mean age of 30.2 (SD
9.0). Subjects who were not attack free with donidalorsen-8 for Weeks 17 to 25 in Trial CS5 and
rolled over to Trial CS7 on donidalorsen-4 (n=6) had a mean baseline HAE attack rate of 4.32
(SD 2.44) per 4 weeks and mean of 34.8 (SD 27.3) HAE attacks in the 12 months prior to
Screening in Trial CS5. This group was comprised of five females (83%) and had a mean age of
37.7 (SD 16.1). The Agency did not identify characteristics defining a difference between these
two groups.
Safety
The risks of both dose intervals are similar and can be mitigated through labeling. See
Sections 7.6.1 and 7.7 for more information.
Conclusion
Availability of both regimens will permit flexibility in dosing at the physician’s discretion and
permit engagement in shared decision-making with each patient.
The Agency recommends the following labeling for the dosing regimen: “Donidalorsen can be
administered as either 80 mg Q4W or 80 mg Q8W.”

6.3.2. Confirmatory Evidence
Issue
The substantial evidence of effectiveness of donidalorsen for HAE is established by the single
adequate and well-controlled clinical trial (CS5) and CE based on mechanistic data. The purpose
of this review issue is to evaluate the source(s) of CE.
Background
The CE providing strong mechanistic support includes the well-established pathophysiology of
HAE: defective C1-INH leading to dysregulated activity of bradykinin-mediated angioedema.
Donidalorsen is an ASO-GalNAc conjugate that causes RNase H1-mediated degradation of PKK
mRNA through selective binding to PKK mRNA, which results in decreased production of PKK
protein. PKK is a pro-enzyme for plasma kallikrein, which results in the release of bradykinin, a
vasodilator causing swelling and pain in HAE. Less substrate for the bradykinin-mediated
angioedema pathway leads to less HAE attacks. PKK is a target of several approved HAE
therapies.
Additionally, CE is derived from the in vitro and in vivo pharmacology data, the PD data, and
clinical dose-ranging data that were reviewed with the NDA.
Assessment
In Vitro Pharmacology
Treatment of HepatoPac® (co-culture system of primary human hepatocytes and stromal cells
[mouse fibroblasts]) with ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS
721744) resulted in a dose-dependent reduction of PKK mRNA. The IC50 for ISIS 721744 and
ISIS 546254 were 0.19μM and 8.73μM , respectively, indicating that ISIS 721744 is about 46fold more potent than ISIS 546254 (likely due to cellular uptake through hepatocyte-specific
ASGPR).
In Vivo Pharmacology
ISIS 721744 does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As such, an
unconjugated mouse-specific ASO (i.e., ISIS 482584) was used for in vivo pharmacology studies
in mice.
Male C57Bl/6 albino mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle or PKK ASO ISIS
482584 (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, or 160 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. ISIS 482584 inhibited PKK liver
mRNA and PKK plasma protein expression in a dose-dependent manner.
Permeability assays were performed in male C57Bl/6 albino mice treated with PKK ASO ISIS
482584 (80 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. Evans Blue tracer was injected into the tail vein of mice
and analyzed for its accumulation in the colon tissue. Some mice were also treated
intraperitoneally with the ACE inhibitor captopril (1 mg/kg) at the time of Evans Blue tracer
injection or with a C1-inhibitor ASO (40 mg/kg/week for 3 weeks) to enhance vascular
60
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
permeability. ISIS 482584 inhibited basal vascular permeability. Further ISIS 482584 inhibited
vascular permeability induced by either captopril or C1-inhibitor ASO.
Male C57Bl/6 albino mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle or PKK ASO ISIS
482584 (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, or 160 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. ISIS 482584 (10 to 160 mg/kg for 3
weeks) reduced basal activated high molecular weight kininogen cleavage in blood of male mice.
Human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice were treated by SC administration with ISIS 721744 (0.1,
0.3, 1, 3, or 10 mg/kg) on Day 0 and plasma was collected on Day −1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 42, and 56. A
single dose of ISIS 721744 resulted in a dose and time-dependent reduction of plasma PKK
protein in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice that approached 91% at 10 mg/kg on Day 14
after treatment. After reaching the lowest point at Days 7 to 14, plasma PKK levels were fully
restored by Day 42 for the 1.0 mg/kg dose or Day 56 for the 3 mg/kg dose. PKK levels were still
20% below baseline levels by Day 56 for the 10 mg/kg dose.
Pharmacodynamic Data
In healthy subjects, a dose-dependent reduction in plasma PKK concentrations from baseline was
observed between dosages of 20 and 80 mg SC Q4W. After 4 doses of donidalorsen-4 (last dose
administered on Day 85), the nadir in plasma PKK reduction was achieved between Day 71 and
Day 99. The mean percent change from baseline for plasma PKK on Day 99 was −53%, −65%,
−87%, and −94%, respectively, for 20 mg, 40 mg, 60 mg, and 80 mg Q4W.
In subjects with HAE Type I or II who were treated in either the donidalorsen-4 or donidalorsen8 groups for 25 weeks, the steady-state PKK change from baseline was achieved by Week 13
(Day 85) and maintained thereafter. The mean percent reduction in plasma PKK from baseline at
Week 25 was greater with the donidalorsen-4 regimen (73%) relative to the donidalorsen-8
regimen (47%). With the donidalorsen-8 regimen, a greater fluctuation in plasma PKK change
from baseline was observed with smaller reduction from baseline was observed prior to
administration of the next dose. This greater fluctuation in plasma PKK is likely associated with
the longer donidalorsen-8 dosing interval.
Clinical Dose Ranging
Refer to Section 6.3.1 for discussion of increased efficacy with more frequent dosing, in support
of clinical dose ranging.
Conclusion
The mechanistic data are sufficiently strong and consistent to serve as CE contributing to SEE
for this program.
