7. Safety (Risk and Risk Management)
7.1. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on
Nonclinical Data
The nonclinical safety of donidalorsen was evaluated in good laboratory practice (GLP)compliant safety pharmacology (cardiovascular, respiratory, and central nervous system [CNS]
in monkeys and human ether-a-go-go related gene [hERG] in human embryonic kidney-293
[HEK-293] cells), repeat-dose toxicity (13-week mouse, 26-week mouse, and 13-week
interim/39-week monkey), genotoxicity (Ames, chromosome aberration, and mouse bone
marrow micronucleus), carcinogenicity (6-month Tg.rasH2 mouse), and reproductive and
developmental toxicity (combined fertility and development mouse and pre- and postnatal
development [PPND] mouse) studies. Donidalorsen does not align perfectly to the mouse PKK
gene sequence, so the mouse toxicity studies also evaluated mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 to
assess on-target effects.
Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion
Unconjugated donidalorsen was measurable in the liver and kidney after SC administration in
mice and monkeys. Donidalorsen was highly bound (≥96.81%) to whole blood plasma proteins
in human, monkey, and mouse.
As determined by the Applicant, the primary route of elimination of donidalorsen is initial rapid
hydrolysis of the GalNAc conjugate in tissues, followed by slow nuclease-mediated metabolism
of the unconjugated oligonucleotide, and subsequent excretion of chain-shortened metabolites, as
well as full-length oligonucleotides, albeit minor in urine and feces. There were no unique
metabolites found in humans compared to animal species. For donidalorsen linker-related
metabolites, the GalNAc moiety is hydrolyzed intracellularly following uptake into tissues and
the THA linker undergoes extensive oxidative metabolism, and is nearly completely eliminated
via biliary excretion, and to a lesser extent, renal excretion, within 24 hours after administration.
Safety Pharmacology
Donidalorsen (single doses of 12 and 30 mg/kg SC) had no adverse effects on cardiovascular,
respiratory, or CNS parameters in monkeys. Donidalorsen did not statistically inhibit hERG
current in HEK-293 cells stably transfected with hERG cDNA with an estimated IC50 greater
than 300μM . In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to interact with the hERG channel.
General Toxicology
Donidalorsen-related toxicity findings in the 26-week mouse study and/or the13-week
interim/39-week monkey study included effects on thrombocytopenia and hematology
(monkeys), coagulation (monkeys), liver (mice and monkeys), kidney (monkeys), and injection
site (mice and monkeys).

62
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Thrombocytopenia, Hematology, and Coagulation
In monkeys, severe thrombocytopenia was noted in one female and one male at 12 and
30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, respectively. Thrombocytopenia was not seen in either animal
during the recovery period. Platelet decreases were accompanied by mild to marked decreases in
red cell mass with mild to moderate increases in reticulocyte counts and/or increased
polychromasia. The female had mild SC tissue necrosis with fibrin and hemorrhage at one of the
injection sites, and both the female and male had red nasal discharge, red skin discoloration,
bruising, and/or petechial hemorrhage at various body sites, which may have accounted for the
decrease in red cell mass and the increase in reticulocyte counts. Complement Bb levels (marker
of alternative pathway activation) were slightly elevated in males at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen
and in females at 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen. Minimal prolongations in mean activated
partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) time were seen in males and females at 30 mg/kg/dose
donidalorsen but were not evident by 24 hours postdose.
Liver
In mice, liver histopathology findings included minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular
hypertrophy in males (1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen) and one female (12 mg/kg/dose
donidalorsen), which correlated with increased mean liver weights (4 and 12 mg/kg/dose
donidalorsen) and liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). There was also an increase in the
severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in males (4 and 12 mg/kg/dose
donidalorsen), which correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose
levels. These findings were consistent with uptake of donidalorsen.
In monkeys, liver histopathology findings included hepatocyte hypertrophy (≥6 mg/kg/dose
donidalorsen terminal), accumulation of basophilic granules in hepatocytes (≥2 mg/kg/dose
donidalorsen terminal and ≥6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim) and Kupffer cells
(≥6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim and terminal), and sporadic perivascular/vascular
inflammation in one male (at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim).
Kidney
In monkeys, kidney histopathology findings included accumulation of basophilic granules in
tubular epithelial cells (≥2 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim and terminal).
Injection Sites
In mice, injection site histopathology findings included increased incidences and/or severity of
infiltrates of vacuolated macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte
vacuolation in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and/or
4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased
leukocyte counts.
In monkeys, injection site histopathology findings at interim and/or terminal sacrifices (generally
at all doses with dose-related incidence and/or severity), included: basophilic granules,
macrophages, fibrosis, mixed leukocyte infiltration, mononuclear cell infiltration, mixed cell

63
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
infiltration/inflammation, perivascular/vascular inflammation, myofiber
degeneration/regeneration, hemorrhage, and necrosis.
Reproductive and Developmental Toxicology
The potential reproductive and developmental toxicity of donidalorsen and mouse surrogate ISIS
722059 were evaluated in combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and a
PPND study in mice. No adverse effects on reproductive and developmental parameters were
seen.
Genotoxicity
Donidalorsen was negative for genotoxicity (mutagenicity or clastogenicity) in the in vitro
bacterial reverse mutation test (Ames assay), in vitro chromosome aberration assay in cultured
Chinese Hamster Lung (CHL) cells, and bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice.
Carcinogenicity
In a 6-month carcinogenicity study in transgenic (Tg.rasH2) mice, SC administration of
donidalorsen (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg for males and 10, 20, or 60 mg/kg for females) or mousespecific surrogate ISIS 722059 (10 mg/kg) once every 2 weeks (Q2W) did not result in a
statistically significant increase in tumors compared to the vehicle control in male mice. The
carcinogenicity study was inadequate for female mice because a maximum tolerated dose (MTD)
was not achieved and no other valid basis to support the high dose was discernable. Of note, at
the time of the special protocol assessment (SPA) for the 6-month carcinogenicity protocol, the
Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee could not recommend doses for female mice
for the proposed study, as no acceptable basis for dose selection could be identified in the nonGLP-compliant 14-week dose range finding (DRF) study in Tg.rasH2 mice.
A 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats is ongoing. At the time of the pre-NDA meeting, the
Division agreed that it would be acceptable to submit a summary of the in-life data for the 2-year
carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the NDA submission and to submit the final report as
a postmarketing requirement (PMR).

7.2. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on
Drug Class or Other Drug-Specific Factors
Donidalorsen is a prekallikrein-directed GalNAc-conjugated ASO. The potential safety concerns
for donidalorsen are based on both the molecule and the target.
ASOs
FDA-approved ASOs for intravenous or subcutaneous administration include mipomersen,
inotersen, eteplirsen, golodirsen, vilpolarsen, casimersen, tofersen, defibrotide, and nusinersen.
Safety risks associated with systemically administered ASOs have included injection site
reactions, liver toxicity (Boxed Warning for mipomersen), thrombocytopenia (Boxed Warning

64
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
for inotersen), coagulation abnormalities, and kidney toxicity (Boxed Warning for inotersen).
Hypersensitivity reactions have also been reported.
Approved GalNAc conjugated ASOs include eplontersen and olezarsen. GalNAc conjugation is
thought to enhance the safety of ASOs by targeting delivery to hepatocytes which improves the
activity of ASO, allowing for lower dosages and potentially improved safety. It is not known if
liver-targeted ASOs accumulate in the liver over time. The known class effects of ASOs (liver
toxicity, thrombocytopenia, and glomerulonephritis) were not identified as risks for eplontersen.
Olezarsen is labeled for hypersensitivity reactions, decreased platelet counts, and increased liver
enzymes.
Kallikrein Inhibitors
Approved HAE products which target prekallikrein include lanadelumab and berotralstat for
prophylaxis, and sebetrolstat for acute treatment of HAE attacks. Safety risks include coagulation
abnormalities and hypersensitivity reactions.

7.3. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Identified
Through Postmarket Experience
Not applicable. This drug is not yet commercially available in any country.

7.4. FDA Approach to the Safety Review
The sources of the clinical trial safety database are shown in Table 3.
The clinical data scientists and clinical reviewer within the Agency performed independent
safety analyses using R Studio 4.1.3, JMP, MAED, and Office of Computational Science
Analysis Studio software programs. The safety assessment is primarily based on data from Trial
CS5; only safety data from Trial CS5 is included in labeling. Supportive safety data is provided
by Trial CS2 part A and the OLE trials (CS7, a continuation of CS5, and CS3, a continuation of
CS2) and is discussed in Section 17. Given the differences in design and duration across trials
safety from each trial was reviewed independently. Given the small sample size of the clinical
program, pooled safety data was used to support the review of the Key Safety Review Issues in
Section 7.7. The pooled safety analysis incorporates data from Trials CS2, CS3, CS5, and CS7.
All safety analyses were conducted in the safety population, which consisted of any subject who
received at least one dose of donidalorsen. For both Trial CS5 and Trial CS2, the safety
population and the intent-to-treat (ITT) population were the same.

of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) were consistent with Code of Federal
Regulations 312.32 (21 CFR 312.12 2004). The Applicant coded AEs using the Medical

7.7. Key Safety Review Issues
7.7.1. Injection Site Reactions
Issue
Injection site reactions are a common adverse reaction from SC injectable drug products and for
antisense oligonucleotide products. Injection site reactions were observed during the
donidalorsen development program. The Applicant proposes to include injection site reactions
(ISRs) in the common adverse drug reaction table in Section 6 of the PI.
Background
Injection site reactions are a known class effect of ASOs, with reported rates as high as 84% for
some ASOs (mipomersen).

71
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Assessment
Findings at the SC injection site were noted in the 26-week mouse study with donidalorsen and
mouse surrogate ISIS 722059, and the 39-week monkey study with donidalorsen.
Our primary safety review focuses on Trial CS5, with supportive safety analysis from the other
clinical trials in the development program (see Table 3 under Section 3) due to the small size of
the safety database.
In terms of ISR AEs in Trial CS5, there was an increased incidence of events in the
donidalorsen-4 group, with 11 (24%) subjects experiencing an ISR based on the Local
Administration Reaction narrow OCMQ compared to 4% for donidalorsen-8 and 5% for placebo
(see Table 24). When accounting for the number of injections, the incidence remained higher for
donidalorsen-4 (11/270 (6 injections x 45 subjects) = 4%) compared to donidalorsen-8 (1/69 (3
injections x 23 subjects) = 1%). Injection site erythema was the most frequently reported of the
OCMQ AEs (n=6, 13%), followed by injection site discoloration, injection site pain, and
injection site pruritus (n=3, 7% for each). All ISRs were nonserious, mild in severity, and did not
result in discontinuation of IP. In contrast, only one subject per group in the donidalorsen-8 and
placebo groups experienced an ISR.
In Trial CS7 (the OLE trial following Trial CS5), which lacked a placebo control group, a greater
proportion of subjects in the Rollover donidalorsen-4 group (16%) experienced ISRs compared
with the Rollover donidalorsen-8 group (6%) per the Local Administration Reaction narrow
OCMQ. All ISRs were nonserious and did not result in any action taken with the trial drug.
Except for one event of moderate severity, all ISRs were mild. Of Naïve subjects, 37%
experienced ISRs per the Local Administration Reaction narrow OCMQ. Although this is the
highest incidence noted in any cohort across the donidalorsen HAE program, all ISRs in Naïve
subjects were non-serious and did not result in any action taken with the trial drug. The majority
of ISRs were mild (25%) or moderate (6%) in severity.
In Trial CS3 (the OLE trial following Trial CS2), which lacked a placebo control group, 35% of
subjects in the HAE-1/HAE-2 group (6/17 subjects, 40 events) experienced at least one ISR per
the Local Administration Reaction narrow OCMQ. One subject in the HAE-1/HAE-2 group
(donidalorsen 100 mg Q4W [Flexible Dosing Period]) permanently discontinued IP due to six
moderate TEAEs of injection site discoloration.
The Applicant provided a pooled safety analysis of 173 subjects who received donidalorsen
across Trials CS2, CS3, CS5 and CS7. The three subjects enrolled in Trial CS2 part B are
excluded from the Agency’s analysis due to their diagnosis with HAE Type III, bringing the
sample size for the pooled safety analysis to 170 subjects.
Out of these 170 subjects, 44 (26%) subjects experienced at least one ISR, with the number of
individual ISR events totaling 237. Thus, those subjects who do experience ISR may experience
multiple and/or repeated events over time. Incidence of ISRs compared across dosing arms
shows the highest incidence in the donidalorsen-4 dosing interval (28%), while donidalorsen-8 is
similar to placebo (7% for both groups). The incidence of ISR appears generally stable with
subsequent injections, i.e., a higher incidence of ISR was not observed with increased number of
previous injections. The most common ISR reported in the any donidalorsen treatment group
72
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
were Injection site erythema [20 (11.8%)], Injection site discoloration [12 (7.1%)], Injection site
pruritus [11 (6.5%)], and Injection site pain [10 (5.9%)].
Regarding the timing of onset of ISRs, ISRs occurring after the first dose of donidalorsen
occurred in 11 (25%) of the 44 subjects who developed ISRs: nine (21%) on the same day as the
first dose and two on Day 2 after the first dose. Out of 44 subjects, 36 (82%) subjects
experienced 135 ISRs within 2 days after the most recent dose of donidalorsen.
Regarding outcome and duration of ISRs, out of 237 ISRs, 209 (88%) were resolved at the time
of database lock, with the remaining 28 (12%) ongoing. Out of 209 resolved ISRs, 45 (22%)
ISRs resolved within 2 days and 84 (40%) ISRs resolved within 7 days. The most common
ongoing ISRs were injection site discoloration (21 events in four subjects). As noted previously,
one (2%) subject out of 44 experienced an ISR leading to permanent trial drug discontinuation;
this subject received donidalorsen 100 mg Q4W and experienced six moderate events of
injection site discoloration.
Regarding severity, out of 237 ISRs, 203 (86%) ISRs in 43 subjects were reported as mild, and
34 (14%) ISR in 7 subjects were reported as moderate. No serious or severe ISRs were reported.
The severity of ISRs appears generally stable with subsequent injections, i.e., an increased
severity of ISRs was not observed with increased number of previous injections.
Overall, the cumulative, pooled data regarding ISRs indicates that the pivotal trial safety data
may provide an accurate overview of this observed risk of donidalorsen use, with additional
supportive data about the characteristics of observed ISRs.
Conclusion
ISRs were observed in 24% of subjects in the donidalorsen-4 group of the pivotal trial (CS5),
while 4 to 5% of subjects in the donidalorsen-8 and placebo groups experienced ISRs. The
features of ISRs were similar between Trial CS5 and the cumulative, pooled safety data from the
four clinical trials. ISRs were nonserious, with the vast majority mild in severity. The incidence
and severity of ISRs did not vary with number of past injections. The most frequent AE PTs
were injection site erythema, discoloration, pain, and pruritus. ISRs developed upon exposure to
the first dose in 25% of subjects who eventually developed ISRs, and whether on the first or
subsequent injection, they most commonly occurred within 1 to 2 days of the injection. The
majority of ISRs resolved within 7 days. Treatment discontinuation due to ISRs was infrequent;
across the program, one subject permanently discontinued donidalorsen due to six moderate ISR
events. Availability of donidalorsen-8 provides options for prescribers to mitigate the risk of
injection site reactions with donidalorsen-4.

7.7.2. Bleeding Events, Thrombocytopenia, and
Coagulation
Issue
Bleeding risks, including thrombocytopenia and effects on the clotting cascade (prolonged aPTT)
(Crooke et al. 2019) are known ASO class effects (regardless of the target protein). The
donidalorsen clinical program was designed to monitor and mitigate this potential risk.
Background
ASO class effects, including thrombocytopenia, are generally thought to be dose-dependent,
transient, and self-limited. Though the precise mechanism of thrombocytopenia is not known, it
is thought to be due to ASOs binding to platelets and causing increased platelet clearance.
Importantly, with chronic ASO administration, nonhuman primate and human clinical trials have
revealed a risk of sporadic, unpredictable, severe thrombocytopenia. To our knowledge, such
events have not been observed in humans receiving GalNAC-conjugated ASOs, which allow for
reduced systemic dosage via increased potency, with the goal of reducing overall toxicities.
Additionally, some kallikrein inhibiting products are known to cause asymptomatic prolongation
of aPTT in clinical use; however, bleeding events are not associated with this laboratory
abnormality. The aPTT assay primarily evaluates the intrinsic coagulation pathway, which
includes kallikrein and other clotting factors. Meanwhile, PT and INR evaluate the extrinsic
pathway, and in the donidalorsen program they were utilized as a means to assess hepatic
synthetic function.
Assessment
In the 13-week interim/39-week monkey study with a 26-week recovery period, severe
thrombocytopenia was noted in one female and one male at 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen,
respectively. Thrombocytopenia was not seen in either animal during the 26-week recovery
period.
In the 13-week interim/39-week monkey study with a 26-week recovery period, minimal
prolongations in mean aPTT time were seen in males and females at 30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen
but were not evident by 24-hours postdose.
Our primary safety review focuses on Trial CS5, which permits placebo-controlled analysis over
24 weeks, with supportive safety analysis from the other clinical trials in the development
program (see Table 3). These other clinical trials, though they have limitations such as a shorter
duration (for Trial CS2) and lack of placebo control (for the OLE trials), are useful due to the
small size of the safety database and the longer-term data of the OLE trials. For each individual
trial, and for pooled results from Trials CS5, CS2, CS7, and CS3, TEAEs and laboratory results
were reviewed for signals of bleeding risk, thrombocytopenia, and aPTT prolongation.
Bleeding Adverse Events
Bleeding TEAEs were identified by the Hemorrhage OCMQ (Narrow).
74

Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407

donidalorsen-4 group (see Table 25). However, the three TEAEs occurring in the donidalorsen-4
group were all mild and self-limited, without concomitant clinically significant abnormalities in
coagulation laboratory results (including platelet counts, PT, and INR), and none led to treatment
discontinuation. The events in donidalorsen-8 and placebo both started on Day 1, making them
very unlikely to be related to the trial drug.

Review of the 120-day safety update report did not reveal substantive, new information about

Platelet Counts
The effect of donidalorsen on platelet counts was also evaluated. There was no apparent
exposure response between donidalorsen systemic exposure and change in platelet counts
according to the clinical pharmacology analysis; see Section 8.1.2 for details.
Aggregate data on platelet counts over time were reviewed. Figure 11 shows the mean absolute
change from baseline for platelet count; the mean values at each timepoint are displayed in the
text box below the figure. Treatment with donidalorsen at both doses tended to decrease platelet
counts, with a sharper downward slope in the donidalorsen-4 group, which converged with the
donidalorsen-8 slope by Week 25. The platelet counts in the donidalorsen-4 group reached a
plateau by Week 17, with the mean absolute value having decreased by 15,000 cells/mm3.

In Trial CS3 (the OLE trial following Trial CS2), which lacked a placebo control group, one

Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time
In Trial CS5, mean aPTT remained within the reference range, and no imbalance in prolonged
aPTT was observed compared to placebo. No clinically relevant changes in aPTT values were
noted in Trial CS5. Review of safety data from Trials CS7, CS2, and CS3 showed, similarly, no
apparent safety signal related to aPTT values.
Conclusion
Bleeding
In Trial CS5, there was a slight trend towards an increased incidence of bleeding TEAEs in the
donidalorsen-4 group (see Table 25). However, the three TEAEs occurring in the donidalorsen-4
group were all mild and self-limited, without concomitant clinically significant abnormalities in
coagulation laboratory results (including platelet counts, PT, and INR), and none led to treatment
discontinuation.
In Trial CS7, 17 (12%) of all subjects experienced one or more bleeding TEAEs, with none
occurring in the subjects who received the donidalorsen-8 dosing regimen. These events were
typically mild or moderate in severity, did not lead to treatment discontinuation, and were not
associated with concomitant clinically significant abnormalities in coagulation laboratory results.
Results from Trials CS2 and CS3 were consistent with Trials CS5 and CS7.
Platelet Counts
The placebo-controlled safety data from Trial CS5 revealed a sustained decrease in platelet
counts, with a magnitude of approximately 15,000 to 20,000 cells/mm3, that stabilized in
approximately 4 months and did not typically result in clinically significant thrombocytopenia or
bleeding events. The donidalorsen treatment arms demonstrated a greater mean percent change
in platelet count at Week 25 (9.6% for donidalorsen-4, 7.9% for donidalorsen-8) compared to
placebo (1.4%). Results from CS2, CS3, and CS7 were consistent with Trial CS5.
Overall, although no serious clinical sequelae related to bleeding or thrombocytopenia were
observed in the clinical program, the theoretical risk of uncommon, severe thrombocytopenia or

bleeding remains, due to the ASO class effects. Therefore, the decreased platelets observed in
Trial CS5 will be included in labeling.

7.7.3. Hepatic Function Effects
Issue
Due to the known ASO class effect of hepatotoxicity and donidalorsen’s pharmacologic
mechanism, which relies on GalNAC binding hepatocytes, the occurrence of clinically
significant hepatocellular injury risk with donidalorsen use was investigated.
Background
Antisense oligonucleotide class effects, including hepatotoxicity, are generally thought to be
dose-dependent, transient, and self-limited. Risk of hepatotoxicity with elevations of ALT and
AST, and hepatic steatosis were seen in the development programs for mipomersen and
inotersen, which are ASOs targeting hepatic gene expression. Inotersen labeling recommends
baseline and monthly monitoring of liver enzymes.
Olezarsen, a GalNAC-conjugated ASO for familial chylomicronemia, was approved in 2024
with a postmarketing requirement to evaluate the potential for drug-induced liver injury (DILI)
with long-term use of this product. Olezarsen is labeled for increase in liver enzymes. Olezarsen
was associated with average increases in ALT, AST, and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)
within the first 3 months which stabilized and remained within reference range. There were a
higher proportion of olezarsen-treated subjects in whom serious hepatic events occurred and
increases in liver enzymes led to discontinuation or interruption of the trial drug. Liver enzymes
returned towards baseline with discontinuation of olezarsen. There were no cases of Hy’s Law,
an indicator of drug-induced liver injury.6
Assessment
Nonclinical
In the 26-week mouse study, liver histopathology findings included minimal or slight
centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy (1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen), which
correlated with increased mean liver weights (4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen) and liver
enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). There was also an increase in the severity (slight to marked)
of hepatocyte vacuolation in males (4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen), which correlated with
gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels. These findings were consistent
with uptake of donidalorsen.
In the 13-week interim/39-week monkey study, liver histopathology findings included
hepatocyte hypertrophy (≥6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen terminal), accumulation of basophilic
granules in hepatocytes (≥2 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen terminal and ≥6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen
6

See FDA Summary Review for Olezarsen (NDA 218614), dated December 19, 2024, available at
https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218614Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf.

80
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
interim) and Kupffer cells (≥6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim and terminal), and sporadic
perivascular/vascular inflammation (12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim).
Our primary safety review focuses on Trial CS5, which permits placebo-controlled analysis over
24 weeks, with supportive safety analysis from the other clinical trials in the development
program (see Table 3, under Section 3). These other clinical trials, though they have limitations
such as a shorter duration (for Trial CS2) and lack of placebo control (for the OLE trials), are
useful due to the small size of the safety database and the longer-term data of the OLE trials. For
each individual trial, and for pooled data from Trials CS5, CS2, CS7, and CS3, TEAEs and
laboratory results were reviewed for signals of hepatotoxicity.
Adverse Events
In Trial CS5, there were no clear imbalances between subjects receiving donidalorsen versus
placebo in the incidence of TEAEs such as ALT and AST elevations, jaundice, PTs in the
hepatic injury OCMQ (narrow or broad), or cases meeting Hy’s Law criteria.
Overall, analysis of TEAEs did not reveal a signal of hepatic injury. However, given that this
result could be consistent with products resulting in DILI, in which premarket clinical trials
reveal only laboratory abnormalities not rising to the level of an imbalance in adverse events,
further investigation was completed.
Liver Function Tests
Because DILI is most commonly asymptomatic and diagnosed by laboratory testing, laboratory
results for AST, ALT, ALP, GGT, bilirubin, and PT/INR were reviewed for each clinical trial.
Figure 13 shows the mean absolute change from baseline for AST, ALT, ALP, and GGT during
Trial CS5; total and direct bilirubin are not shown as these did not reveal a notable trend. The
mean change from baseline and absolute values at each timepoint are displayed in the text boxes
below each figure. Subclinical increases in AST and ALT were observed at a magnitude that was
similar at both doses of donidalorsen, while the increases in ALP and GGT were of larger
magnitude at higher doses. The increases in AST, ALT, and ALP appeared to reach a plateau
during the trial, while there is not a clear plateau in GGT increase.

Integrated Summary
Due to the small sample size of the pivotal trial, safety data from the additional trials (the phase 2
Trial CS2 and the ongoing open-label Trials CS3 and CS7, including data from the 120-day
92
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
safety update) were included in evaluation of hepatic effects of donidalorsen. This summary
incorporates findings across the program.
Regarding TEAEs, all abnormal liver function TEAEs were nonserious and mild to moderate in
severity. Two subjects discontinued the trial drug due to these TEAEs: one for ALT increase
related to donidalorsen, despite not meeting a stopping rule, and one for ALT increase that did
meet a stopping rule.
No subject met criteria for Hy’s law. Clinically relevant levels of LFT elevation occurred
infrequently, while subclinical elevations in ALT, AST, GGT, and INR were observed more
frequently with donidalorsen compared to placebo. Low-level elevations in AST and ALT
(<3× ULN) are common, nonspecific, and not concerning for DILI.
A total of eight donidalorsen recipients (five in the donidalorsen-4 group and three in the
donidalorsen-8 group) experienced ALT or AST elevations ≥3× ULN. Of these, two subjects had
ALT levels that peaked at a level ≥5× ULN (one also experienced an AST ≥3× ULN), and one
subject peaked at ALT >8× ULN (possibly due to acute EBV infection). Two subjects
discontinued donidalorsen due to LFT abnormalities.
Two subjects experienced severe (~1.5× ULN) elevations of bilirubin and two subjects
experienced severe (≥5.0× ULN) increases in GGT, but these did not require treatment
discontinuation. Plausible etiologies were present for these subjects, including Gilbert syndrome,
multiple comorbidities, elevated GGT level at baseline, prior long-term use of danazol, and
congestive cardiac failure.
Conclusion
There was no clear imbalance for liver related TEAEs between donidalorsen and placebo. There
were no cases of Hy’s law. Clinically relevant levels of LFT elevation occurred infrequently,
while subclinical elevations in ALT, AST, GGT, and INR were observed more frequently with
donidalorsen compared to placebo. Low-level elevations in AST and ALT (<3× ULN) were
common, nonspecific, and not concerning for DILI. A total of three subjects had ALT ≥5× ULN.
Due to the known ASO class effect of hepatotoxicity, the accumulation of ASOs in the liver over
time, the small safety database, and the unknown consequences of lifetime treatment with ASOs,
a PMR will be issued to assess the potential for chronic drug-induced liver injury with long-term
treatment.

7.7.4. Hypersensitivity Reactions
Issue
During the NDA review process, an adverse reaction of anaphylaxis in a subject enrolled in the
ongoing trial (CS7) was reported as a Safety Report to IND 142564. The safety assessment relies
on the response to an Information Request that was sent to the Applicant to provide relevant
information to evaluate this safety signal.

93
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Background
Hypersensitivity reactions are a known, labeled AE for several FDA-approved ASO products.
Hypersensitivity reactions are listed in the Warning and Precautions section of labeling for at
least four of these products: defibrotide, inotersen, eteplirsen, and golodirsen. The observed
symptoms include rash, urticaria, skin exfoliation, chills, flushing, dysphagia, tachycardia, and
bronchospasm. Serious hypersensitivity reactions occurred in the development program for
volanesorsen, including suspected anaphylaxis in one subject.8
Assessment
For donidalorsen, the subject was a 20-year-old White female who received donidalorsen-4 in
Trial CS5 and Trial CS7. The SAE with PT Hypersensitivity (Verbatim: Allergic reaction)
occurred on Trial CS7 Day 816 and resulted in permanent treatment discontinuation. Per the case
narrative, the event started 5 minutes after donidalorsen injection. The subject developed a red
rash covering most of her body, dyspnea, perioral swelling, and chest pain. The investigator
administered oral diphenhydramine and subcutaneous epinephrine. Her baseline vital signs were
normal and she developed tachycardia to 145 bpm at the time of the event, but blood pressure
was not measured. Thirty minutes later, when symptoms had subsided, heart rate was 113 and
BP was 126/82 mm Hg. Tryptase was not drawn. The subject had also taken ibuprofen 200 mg to
prevent postinjection site pain; she reported having tolerated ibuprofen in the past. The narrative
states that a skin allergy test conducted with donidalorsen demonstrated a negative reaction,
without providing details on the quality/results of this test, so this cannot be interpreted as
meaningful. Given the fulfillment of Sampson’s criteria (Sampson et al. 2006), the temporal
relationship to donidalorsen, and the lack of an alternative diagnosis, this event is consistent with
anaphylaxis due to donidalorsen.
Using a cumulative cutoff date of February 24, 2025, a search of the clinical and safety databases
was conducted using the OCMQs of Hypersensitivity (broad) and Anaphylactic Reaction (broad)
to identify potential cases of hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis, from two completed trials (CS2
and CS5) and two ongoing clinical trials (CS3 and CS7) in the donidalorsen clinical development
program. The cumulative exposure across the four trials at the cutoff date was 177 subjects. Out
of 53 events meeting the Hypersensitivity (broad) OCMQ criteria, the Applicant identified five
events (PTs: four Hypersensitivity and one Rash) in three subjects (all in Trial CS7) that are
consistent with non-serious hypersensitivity to donidalorsen (i.e., the temporal association and
lack of alternate diagnosis make this the most likely diagnosis). One of these events led to
treatment discontinuation.
There was no clear correlation between hypersensitivity and antidrug antibody (ADA) titers or
systemic concentration.

8

See FDA Summary Review for Olezarsen (NDA 218614), dated December 19, 2024, available at
https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218614Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf.

94
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Conclusion
Overall, six AEs (one serious and five non-serious) in three (2%, 3/177) subjects who received
donidalorsen were assessed as hypersensitivity reactions from Trials ISIS 721744-CS2, ISIS
721744-CS3, ISIS 721744-CS5, and ISIS 721744-CS7. One subject (0.6%, 1/177) experienced a
serious event of Hypersensitivity which fulfills NIAID criteria for the diagnosis of anaphylaxis
was reported across all donidalorsen clinical trials. Two out of six AEs of hypersensitivity
reactions led to permanent treatment discontinuation in two (1%) subjects.
This risk of donidalorsen use is important to communicate in labeling and will be described in
Section 5 of the USPI.

8. Therapeutic Individualization
8.1. Intrinsic Factors
Population PK and PD analyses showed no clinically meaningful differences in the
pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen based on age, body weight, sex, race,
ethnicity, disease status (i.e., healthy subjects or HAE patients), mild renal impairment (eGFR
≥60 to <90 mL/min/1.73 m2), or mild hepatic impairment (total bilirubin ≤1× ULN and AST >1×
ULN, or total bilirubin >1 to 1.5× ULN and any AST). Donidalorsen has not been studied in
patients with moderate or severe renal impairment, end-stage renal disease, or moderate or
severe hepatic impairment.

8.1.1. Age
No dosage adjustments based on age are recommended.
The proposed indication for donidalorsen is for prophylaxis to prevent HAE attacks in adults and
adolescents aged 12 years and older. No dose adjustment was proposed for adolescent subjects.
Based on the Applicant’s population PK analysis, the steady-state exposures following
administration of the donidalorsen-4 regimen was similar across different age groups, as shown
in Figure 21. A higher mean exposure (area under the concentration-time curve [AUC]tau,ss and
maximum plasma concentration [Cmax],ss) was estimated for adolescents as compared to adults.
The difference in body weight may contribute to this exposure difference (refer to Section 8.1.2).
The mean body weight for adolescents (12 to 17 years) and adults enrolled in Trial CS5 were
67.98 kg and 81.78 kg, respectively.

8.1.2. Body Weight
No dosage adjustments based on body weight are recommended.
No dosage adjustments were proposed based on body weight. Based on the Applicant’s
population analysis, body weight was identified as a significant covariate on donidalorsen
pharmacokinetics. In general, donidalorsen exposure is higher in subjects with lower body
weight. As compared with a reference subject with a body weight of 70 kg, the median
donidalorsen exposure (AUCtau, ss, Cmax, ss, Ctrough, ss) for a subject at the 10th percentile of the
body weight distribution (i.e., 60 kg) is expected to increase by 26%, 39%, and 23%,
respectively. A subject at the 90th percentile of the body weight distribution (i.e., 100 kg) is
expected to have a 42% lower AUCtau, ss, 54% lower Cmax, ss, and 38% lower Ctrough, ss compared
with a reference subject with a weight of 70 kg, as shown in Figure 23.

8.1.3. Hepatic Impairment
No dosage adjustments are recommended for patients with mild hepatic impairment.
Donidalorsen has not been studied in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Use
of donidalorsen is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment.
The effect of hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of
donidalorsen was not assessed in a dedicated clinical pharmacology trial. No dose adjustment
was proposed for subjects with mild hepatic impairment. Donidalorsen has not been studied in
subjects with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. However, the Applicant has not proposed a
restriction on the use of donidalorsen in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment.

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Similar to other GalNAc-conjugated oligonucleotide products, donidalorsen is mainly distributed
to the liver after subcutaneous administration with an initial rapid distribution phase followed by
a much slower elimination phase. Therefore, the liver concentrations of donidalorsen and its
metabolites are expected to be higher than those in plasma. Hepatic impairment may thus impact
the accumulation of GalNAc-conjugated products in the liver. In addition, the production of
PKK may be impaired in patients with hepatic impairment, which indicates that a lower dose of
donidalorsen may also be effective in this patient population. As donidalorsen has not been
evaluated in subjects with moderate to severe hepatic impairment, the long-term safety and
efficacy of donidalorsen in subjects with moderate to severe hepatic impairment is not known.
Both subjects with mild HI enrolled in Trial CS5 and later rolled over into Trial CS7 and
continued on the same donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen. Both subjects had ALT levels trending
upwards in Trial CS7, although no ALT value exceeded >3× ULN as of the date of NDA data
cutoff. Neither of these two subjects presented with any new ALT elevations after NDA data
cutoff in the 120-day safety update. See Section 7.7 for more details regarding safety evaluation.
The small sample size of mild HI subjects (N=2) limits the evaluation of safety in this
population.
In subjects with normal hepatic function, although there was no clear exposure-response
relationship observed between LFT elevation and plasma donidalorsen concentration in Trial
CS5, subclinical elevations in LFTs were observed more frequently with donidalorsen compared
to placebo. Some subjects with normal ALT at baseline who were treated with donidalorsen for a
longer duration (>1 year) throughout Trial CS5 and Trial CS7 experienced clinically relevant
ALT elevations (≥5× ULN). This observation increases the uncertainty regarding the long-term
safety of donidalorsen in patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment who may be more
vulnerable to hepatic toxicity. Therefore, the use of donidalorsen is not recommended in patients
with moderate to severe hepatic impairment from a safety perspective.

8.1.4. Renal Impairment
No dosage adjustments are recommended for patients with mild renal impairment. Donidalorsen
has not been studied in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment or end-stage renal
disease.
The effect of renal impairment on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen
was not assessed in a dedicated clinical pharmacology trial. Donidalorsen is highly bound to
plasma proteins (>98%) and less than 1% of the administered dose is excreted as total full-length
oligonucleotide in urine within the first 24 hours after the fourth dose administered every 4
weeks. In addition, linker-related metabolites accounted for ≤6.4% of the administered dose in
urine. Renal impairment did not impact the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of
donidalorsen. In the pivotal trial (CS5), five subjects with mild renal impairment (eGFR 60 to
89 mL/min/1.73 m2) were enrolled. Three of these subjects received donidalorsen-4. The
remaining two received donidalorsen-8. Based on observed data from Trial CS5, the plasma
Ctrough of donidalorsen and change from baseline in plasma PKK were similar between subjects
with normal renal function and subjects with mild renal impairment, as shown in Figure 28.

8.2. Extrinsic Factors
8.2.1. Drug Product Presentation
The proposed to-be-marketed presentation is solution for injection (80 mg/0.8 mL) in a singledose autoinjector (AI). The clinical formulation used in the pivotal phase 3 trial (CS5) is
donidalorsen solution (100 mg/mL) for injection in stopper glass vial.
To bridge the proposed AI and vial product, the Applicant evaluated plasma PK profiles of
donidalorsen in healthy adult subjects following administration of a single dose of donidalorsen
using vial and AI in a phase 1 bioequivalence trial (CS9).
The results of the bioequivalence trial demonstrated comparable systemic exposure between AI
and vial presentations (geometric mean ratio [90% CI] for AI versus vial products were 113%
[105, 121] for Cmax and 107% [104, 111] for AUC0-336). PD results based on PKK concentrations
were also similar between both products. Refer to Section 14.2.1 for details. The AI and vial
products are adequately bridged. The results therefore support use of the AI product as the to-bemarketed drug product.

8.2.2. Injection Site
The Applicant proposes that donidalorsen can be administered SC into the abdomen, upper thigh,
or the back of the upper arm.
Based on the Applicant’s population PK analysis, injection into the arm is predicted to yield a
12% lower geometric mean Cmax,ss (440 ng/mL) as compared to injection into the abdomen
(495 ng/mL) but a similar Cmax,ss following injection into the thigh (451 ng/mL). Injection into
the arm is also predicted to yield a similar mean AUCtau, ss and Ctrough, ss compared to those
following injection into the abdomen or thigh. The range of post hoc estimates for steady-state
exposure of Cmax, AUCtau, ss, and Ctrough, ss were overlapping between subjects with injection into
the arm, abdomen, and thigh in the Applicant’s population PK analysis.
In the pivotal phase 3 trial (CS5), donidalorsen could be administered into any of three injection
sites (abdomen, arm, or thigh) and alternating injection sites were used in some individuals. The
range of donidalorsen concentrations collected 2 hours postdose at steady state (Week 21)
following donidalorsen-4 administration was overlapping across injections. Although, a slightly
higher median value was noted following injection into the arm as compared to the abdomen or
thigh injection, in contrast to population PK predictions (Figure 29).

8.2.3. Drug-Drug Interactions
No dose adjustment strategies with respect to drug-drug interactions are warranted for
donidalorsen.
In vitro studies indicate that donidalorsen and its main linker-related metabolite (i.e., M8) are not
inducers or inhibitors of CYP-mediated oxidative metabolism. Donidalorsen was not identified
to be a substrate of any CYP enzymes. Linker-related metabolite M8 was determined to be a
substrate of CYP3A4. With respect to transporters, donidalorsen was not found to be a substrate
or inhibitor of major drug transporters. Linker-related metabolite M8 was identified as a
substrate of the transporters organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B3 and bile salt export
pump (BSEP). Linker-related metabolite M8 was also determined to be an inhibitor of multidrug
and toxin extrusion protein (MATE) 1. Notably, although M8 was identified as the main linkerrelated metabolite, its abundance in human plasma is low (1.3% relative to parent). Lastly, no in
vitro DDIs were observed with regards to plasma protein binding displacement between
donidalorsen and other highly plasma protein-bound drugs, such as ibuprofen and warfarin. For
additional details, refer to Section 14.1.

8.3. Plans for Pediatric Drug Development
An initial pediatric study plan (iPSP) was submitted by the Applicant on June 3, 2022, and an
agreement letter for the agreed iPSP was issued on July 6, 2022. The Applicant requested a
waiver for pediatric patients under 2 years of age on the grounds that clinical manifestations of
the disease state (HAE attacks) do not exist in this age group. Ages 12 to less than 18 years were
included in Trial CS5 and Trials CS7. The Applicant requested a deferral for ages 2 to less than
12 years; this age group will be targeted in a future open-label clinical trial (CS8) that will target
enrolling 20 patients for a treatment duration of 25 weeks.
On September 19, 2023, donidalorsen received orphan designation for the treatment of HAE
exempting pediatric studies under PREA.

8.4. Pregnancy, Lactation, and Females/Males of
Reproductive Potential
The potential reproductive and developmental toxicity of donidalorsen was evaluated in GLPcompliant combined fertility and embryofetal (embryo-fetal development [EFD]) developmental
and PPND studies in mice. Donidalorsen does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK
gene sequence and mice are not considered a pharmacologically relevant species. As such, the
reproductive and developmental toxicity studies in mice also evaluated mouse surrogate
antisense oligonucleotide ISIS 722059, which targets mouse PKK, to assess potential toxicities
related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition.
The following nonclinical information was used in support of the drug’s labeling. Additional
details are available in Section 13.

Product
Donidalorsen injection product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution
containing an ASO in prefilled syringe within an AI device. The drug/device combination
product is intended for subcutaneous injection by the patient or caregiver at home and is
indicated for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and
older. Donidalorsen, an ASO, reduces the production of PKK protein. Each product unit contains
80 mg/0.8 mL of donidalorsen drug. The labeling recommends a starting dose for patients aged
(b) (4) (equivalent to 84 mg of donidalorsen
12 years and older of 80 mg donidalorsen

All excipients in the product are of USP/NF grade and in quantities that do not exceed the
maximum daily amounts approved for other injection drug products or products, according to the
Inactive Ingredient Report. None of the excipients are novel and none are derived from animal

12. Summary of Regulatory History
On July 15, 2019, Ionis Pharmaceuticals submitted IND 142564 with a proposed trial, ISIS
721744-CS2, entitled “A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2a Study to
Assess the Clinical Efficacy of ISIS 721744, a Second-Generation Ligand-Conjugated Antisense
Inhibitor of Prekallikrein, in Patients with Hereditary Angioedema,” which was allowed to
proceed on August 14, 2019. A phase 1 study, Protocol No. ISIS 721744-CS1, was previously
conducted in Canada to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics
of ISIS 721744 in healthy volunteers.
On August 30, 2021, an end-of-phase 2 meeting was held to discuss the adequacy of the
nonclinical and clinical development to support a marketing application. FDA recommended an
increase in the safety database size, evaluating an alternative lower dosing regimen, shared
concerns and requested additional information regarding regulatory acceptability of the proposed
PRO tools (AE-QoL and AECT), and recommended evaluating mild-to-moderate hepatic
impairment and/or pre-existing hepatic diseases for generalizability. FDA stated the acceptability
of a single pivotal trial to provide substantial evidence of effectiveness would be a review issue.
Regarding the nonclinical development, FDA recommended that prior to the start of phase 3
clinical trials, a characterization of the metabolism of ISIS 721744 and its THA linker should be
provided, as recommended by the Pharmacology and Toxicology and Clinical Pharmacology
Reviewers within the Agency. Further, a toxicologic assessment of the liver inflammation and
necrosis in female mice in the 26-week toxicity study should be provided. It was also agreed that
an EFD study of ISIS 721744 in rabbits is not needed. The meeting minutes were issued on
October 18, 2021.
On July 6, 2022, FDA provided initial agreement on the pediatric trial plan for a partial waiver
for <2 years old, assessment of 12 to less than 18 years old as part of the proposed phase 3 trial,
and a deferred trial of patients 2 to <12 years old postmarketing.
SPA 1 for the 2-year study in rats was submitted on August 5, 2022, and was subsequently
denied due to lack of the Standard for Exchange of Nonclinical Data datasets for the supporting
16-week dose range finding study in rats and resubmitted on September 30, 2022, with the
Standard for Exchange of Nonclinical Datasets. FDA agreed with the proposed 2-year
carcinogenicity study in rats on November 4, 2022. SPA 2, which proposed a 6-month
carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice, was submitted on October 12, 2022, and was agreed
upon for male mice but not for female mice (as no acceptable basis for dose selection could be
identified) on November 16, 2022.
Ionis requested a use-related risk analysis review on January 20, 2023, and included information
on the target disease and human factors (HF) development. In the June 17, 2024, response, FDA
did not identify any new or unique risks for the proposed product ISIS 721744 AI for intended
adults as compared to currently approved Wainua AI and noted prematurity in determining the
need for additional HF validation trials for adolescent users. FDA recommended submission of
the full results report for the HF validation trial with the marketing application.

Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)

13.1.1. Pharmacology
13.1.1.1. Primary Pharmacodynamics
Donidalorsen is a triantennary GalNAc3-conjugated ASO that causes ribonuclease H1 (RNase
H1)-mediated degradation of PKK messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) through binding to PKK
mRNA, which results in reduced production of PKK protein. PKK is a pro-enzyme for plasma
kallikrein, which results in the release of bradykinin, a potent vasodilator causing swelling and
pain in HAE. In patients with HAE, C1-INH deficiency or dysfunction leads to excessive plasma
kallikrein activity, bradykinin generation, and angioedema attacks. Donidalorsen lowers PKK
concentration, which is intended to prevent excessive bradykinin production in patients with
HAE.
The primary pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen have been evaluated in both in vitro and in vivo
primary pharmacology studies.
In Vitro Primary Pharmacology Studies
As described by the Applicant, over 1300 ASOs were designed to target various sites within the
human PKK gene and were evaluated for their ability to inhibit the level of PKK mRNA in vitro
in the human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line HepaRG. Of those ASOs, ISIS 546254, an
unconjugated 2'-O-methoxyethyl (2′-MOE) gapmer ASO with a uniform phosphorothioate (PS)
backbone was identified as a lead candidate. Donidalorsen was derived from ISIS 546254 as a 2′MOE gapmer ASO with the same nucleobase sequence as ISIS 546254 but with a mixed PS and
phosphodiester (PO) backbone and conjugated to a trivalent GalNAc3.
In Silico and In Vitro Characterization of Human PKK ASO ISIS 721744 Specificity
(Study No. ECID129370)
The specificity of donidalorsen to PKK mRNA was characterized in silico and in vitro with the
unconjugated human PKK ASO parent compound, ISIS 546254, which has the same nucleobase
sequence as donidalorsen. ISIS 546254 is perfectly matched to only PKK mRNA in the human
transcriptome (targets site free of meaningful sequence variation). Based on the in silico Basic
Local Alignment Search Tool analysis, there were no identified potential off-target genes with a
0-, 1-, or 2-base mismatch or a 3-base mismatch with 17 matched bases in a row. Alignment of
the ISIS 546254 sequence against the human transcriptome and mRNA reference sequences
predicted seven human genes (i.e., ACACA, CTAGE5, IFIH1, PRKN, ANKS1B, CDH4, and
LOC442028) with mismatched counts of two bases. Of these, one gene (i.e., LOC442028) had
no reported expression in human tissues and two genes (ANKS1B and CDH4) were reported to
be expressed only in the human brain, which is not a preferential tissue for GalNAc3 ASO
accumulation. The effect of ISIS 546254 on the expression of PKK mRNA and the remaining
four predicted off-target mRNAs (i.e., ACACA, CTAGE5, IFIH1, and PRKN), which are
ubiquitously expressed in human tissue, was evaluated in the human hepatocellular cell line
Hep3B. In this experiment, ISIS 546254 (doses up to 20μM ) potently reduced PKK mRNA
(IC50=0.35μM ) and in comparison, only minimally reduced ACACA, CTAGE5, IFIH1, and
PRKN mRNA (IC50=>20, >20, 9.1, and 8.8μM , respectively). These data show that ISIS 546254
is selective for PKK mRNA compared to potential off-target mRNAs.

In Vitro Characterization of Human Prekallikrein Antisense Oligonucleotide ISIS 721744
Activity (Study No. ECID129371)
The in vitro characterization of donidalorsen to reduce human PKK mRNA was based on an
experiment using two human hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines (HepaRG and Hep3b) treated
with ISIS 546254 (unconjugated human PKK ASO parent compound of donidalorsen with the
same nucleobase sequence) or ISIS 141923 (control oligonucleotide with no matches to any sites
within the human transcriptome). ISIS 546254 reduced human PKK mRNA levels in human
hepatocellular cell lines HepaRG and Hep3b by greater than 90% in a concentration-dependent
manner with IC50 of 0.31μM and 0.35μM, respectively (Figure 32). In comparison, the control
oligonucleotide ISIS 141923 did not reduce PKK mRNA in either cell line.

Recommendation for Designation of the Established Pharmacological Classification
The recommended EPC for donidalorsen is “prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide.”
Donidalorsen is an ASO that binds to PKK mRNA to cause degradation of PKK mRNA, which
reduces PKK protein production. The recommended EPC for donidalorsen is consistent with the
EPC of other approved ASO products (both with and without GalNAc).
13.1.1.2. Secondary Pharmacodynamics
The secondary pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were not evaluated in secondary
pharmacology studies as the off-target actions of ASOs are expected to be minimal.
13.1.1.3. Safety Pharmacology
The safety pharmacology of donidalorsen was evaluated in a GLP-compliant study in
Cynomolgus monkeys assessing cardiovascular, respiratory, and CNS parameters, and a GLPcompliant in vitro hERG assay.
Evaluation of Cardiovascular, Respiratory, and Central Nervous Systems Following
Subcutaneous Administration of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus Monkeys (Study Nos. 11752;
721744-AS03)
Male Cynomolgus monkeys (n=4/group) received single SC injections of either the vehicle
control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection) or escalating dose of donidalorsen (12 and
30 mg/kg) with a minimum 1-week washout period between administration of the vehicle control
and each dose level of donidalorsen. The cardiovascular and respiratory assessments were
performed in conscious telemetered monkeys and evaluated arterial blood pressure, heart rate,
respiratory rate, core body temperature, and lead II electrocardiogram (ECG) at timepoints that
were about 2 hours predose through 24 hours postdose (60, 120, 240, 300, 360, 720, and 1440
minutes); arterial blood gases were measured at predose and 2 hours postdose. The CNS
assessment included a Functional Observational Battery (FOB) performed in conscious
nontelemetered monkeys at predose and 1, 4, and 24 hours postdose.
Based on cardiovascular and respiratory assessments, there were no test article-related effects in
conscious telemetered monkeys on arterial blood pressure parameters (systolic, diastolic, and
mean arterial pressure), heart rate, respiratory rate, core body temperature, or ECG parameters
(PR interval, QRS duration, QT interval, and RR interval) for up to 24 hours after dosing, or
arterial blood gases for up to 2 hours after dosing, with 12 and 30 mg/kg donidalorsen.
Based on CNS assessments, there were no treatment-related effects in conscious nontelemetered
monkeys noted by FOB for up to 24 hours after dosing with 12 and 30 mg/kg donidalorsen.
Effect of ISIS 721744 on Cloned hERG Potassium Channels Expressed in Human
Embryonic Kidney Cells (Study Nos. 210830.JTJ; 721744-IS08)
HEK-293 cells were stably transfected with hERG cDNA and treated with donidalorsen (30 and
300μM) at near-physiological temperature to measure the effect on ionic currents by whole-cell
128
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
patch-clamp technique. Donidalorsen inhibited hERG current by 0.5% and 1.9% at 30μM and
300μM, respectively (not statistically significant) versus 2.4% for the vehicle control. The IC50
for the inhibitory effect of donidalorsen on hERG potassium current was not calculated but was
estimated to be greater than 300μM. The positive control article (60nM terfenadine) inhibited
hERG potassium current by 85.6%. In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to interact with
the hERG channel.

13.1.2. Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism,
Excretion/Pharmacokinetics
The absorption and distribution, PK, and toxicokinetic (TK) profiles of donidalorsen were
evaluated both in vitro and in vivo (mice and monkeys).
13.1.2.1. Absorption
The plasma TK profile of SC administration of donidalorsen was evaluated in a GLP-compliant
13-week interim/39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in Cynomolgus monkeys with a 26-week
treatment-free recovery period.
A 39-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus Monkeys With a 13Week Interim Necropsy and 26-Week Recovery (Study Nos. 727-081; 721744-AS02)
Cynomolgus monkeys received SC doses of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection)
or donidalorsen (2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose with loading doses on Days 1, 5, 9, and 14 and once
weekly thereafter) for 13-week interim (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the
interim sacrifice) or 39-weeks followed by a 26-week treatment-free recovery period. Validated
hybridization electrochemiluminescence (ECL) or high-performance liquid chromatographytandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) methodologies were used to measure total fulllength donidalorsen (including fully conjugated, partially conjugated, and unconjugated
donidalorsen) in plasma.
Donidalorsen was rapidly absorbed into systemic circulation with median time to maximum
concentration (Tmax) from 1 to 4 hours across dose levels after single-dose (Day 1) and repeatdose (Days 91 and 273) administration. Mean Cmax and AUC0-48hr increased between dose levels.
After the first dose (Day 1), the 15th dose (Day 91), and the 41st dose (Day 273), AUC0-48hr
increased in a greater than dose proportional manner between doses. There was some
accumulation of drug at the 12 mg/kg/dose, based on increased AUC0-48hr on Day 273 versus Day
91. There were no clear differences in donidalorsen plasma TK between males and females. The
majority of total fully conjugated full-length donidalorsen was cleared within hours from plasma,
with a mean residence time (MRT)0-48hr of about 3 to 10 hours.

129
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
13.1.2.2. Distribution
The distribution of donidalorsen was evaluated in vitro for plasma protein binding in human,
monkey, and mouse plasma, and in vivo into the kidney cortex and liver as part of the GLPcompliant 13-week interim/39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in Cynomolgus monkeys with a
26-week treatment-free recovery period.
In Vitro Evaluation of the Extent of Plasma Protein Binding of ISIS 721744 in Human,
Monkey, and Mouse Plasma by Ultrafiltration (Study Nos. IIS-M4-298; 721744-IS03)
The in vitro protein binding of donidalorsen at 0.5, 5, and 150 µg/mL was evaluated in the whole
plasma from human, Cynomolgus monkey, and mouse by ultrafiltration methods and a nucleasedependent hybridization ELISA detection method. Donidalorsen was highly bound (≥96.81%) to
whole plasma proteins in human, monkey, and mouse at all three concentrations evaluated. The
extent of plasma protein binding of donidalorsen was similar across all species.
A 39-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus Monkeys With a 13Week Interim Necropsy and 26-Week Recovery (Study Nos. 727-081; 721744-AS02)
Cynomolgus monkeys received SC doses of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection)
or donidalorsen (2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose with loading doses on Days 1, 5, 9, and 14, and once
weekly thereafter) for 13-week interim (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the
interim sacrifice) or 39-weeks followed by a 26-week treatment-free recovery period. Validated
hybridization ECL or HPLC-MS/MS methodologies were used to measure unconjugated
donidalorsen in kidney cortex and liver.
After SC administration, donidalorsen distributed to kidney cortex and liver in mostly similar
concentrations (less than 2-fold difference in concentrations between tissues). After the 15th dose
(Day 91) and the 41st dose (Day 273), the concentration of unconjugated donidalorsen in kidney
cortex and liver was dose-dependent across doses. The Applicant claims steady-state tissue
concentration (kidney cortex and liver) based on comparable mean tissue concentrations on Days
9, 93, and 275. There were no apparent differences in unconjugated donidalorsen tissue
concentrations (kidney cortex or liver) between males and females.

13.1.3. Toxicology
The potential toxicity of donidalorsen was evaluated in GLP-compliant repeat-dose toxicity (13week and 26-week in mice and 13-week interim/39-week in monkeys), genotoxicity (in vitro
Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration assay, and in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay
in mice), carcinogenicity (6-month in Tg.rasH2 mice), and reproductive and developmental
toxicity (combined fertility and development in mice and PPND in mice) studies. The main
nonclinical species used in the toxicology studies were monkeys and mice. Donidalorsen does
not align perfectly to the mouse PKK gene sequence and is not pharmacologically active in the
mouse. As such, the toxicity studies in mice evaluated donidalorsen and the conjugated PKK
ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (with the same GalNAc-conjugated 2′-MOE ASO chemical
backbone structure as donidalorsen) to assess both potential off-target and on-target effects,
respectively. The human sequence targeted by donidalorsen has a single-base sequence mismatch
130
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)
Reference ID: 5646426

NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
within the binding site of monkey PKK mRNA (position 19). Despite this mismatch,
donidalorsen demonstrated dose-dependent inhibition of liver target mRNA expression and
reductions in PKK protein and activity levels in peripheral circulation of Cynomolgus monkeys,
which supports the use of the monkey as a pharmacologically relevant species for evaluation of
on-target effects (i.e., effects related to PKK reduction). There were no single-dose toxicity
studies with donidalorsen.
13.1.3.1. Repeat-Dose Toxicity
The pivotal GLP-compliant repeat-dose toxicity studies of longest treatment duration with
donidalorsen included a 26-week study in mice and a 13-week interim/39-week study in
monkeys.
A 39-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus Monkeys With a 13Week Interim Necropsy and 26-Week Recovery (Study Nos. 727-081; 721744-AS02)
Key Study Findings


Cynomolgus monkeys received SC doses of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for
injection) or donidalorsen (2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose with loading doses on Days 1, 5, 9, and
14, and then once weekly thereafter) with a 13-week interim sacrifice (monkeys at
30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the interim sacrifice) or 39 weeks followed by a 26week treatment-free recovery period.



There were no deaths during the study.



Hematology changes included thrombocytopenia (defined as platelet counts
<150000 cells/mcL) that was considered test article-related and adverse in one male at
30 mg/kg/dose and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose. The male animal had marked decreases in
platelet counts compared to individual pretest 2 values on Days 80 and 87 (22 and 30
×103/mcL, respectively). The female animal had marked decreases in platelet counts relative
to individual pretest 2 values on Days 65, 70, 74, 79, and 87 (ranging from <10000 cells/mcL
to 66×103/mcL). Thrombocytopenia was not seen in these two animals during the respective
recovery periods. The platelet decreases in these animals were accompanied by mild to
marked decreases in red cell mass with mild to moderate increases in reticulocyte counts
and/or increased polychromasia (of note, the 12 mg/kg/dose female had mild SC tissue
necrosis with fibrin and hemorrhage at injection site 4 and both the 12 mg/kg/dose female
and the 30 mg/kg/dose male had red nasal discharge, red skin discoloration, bruising, and/or
petechial hemorrhage at various body sites, which may account for decrease in red cell mass
and increase in reticulocyte counts).



Coagulation changes included minimal prolongations in mean aPTT time in males and
females at 30 mg/kg/dose relative to pretest on Day 1 (4 hours postdose) and Day 91 (4 hours
postdose). These changes were not seen by 24 hours postdose on both Day 1 and Day 91.



Clinical chemistry changes included increases in C-reactive protein in females at
12 mg/kg/dose on Day 65 through Day 275 and females at 30 mg/kg/dose on Day 65 and
Day 93 (up to a greater than 600% change or more than 7-fold increase relative to control

Organ weight changes included effects on liver, kidney, and mesenteric lymph nodes.

There were dose-dependent decreases in liver PKK mRNA expression and dose-dependent
and time-dependent decreases in PKK plasma protein after treatment with donidalorsen
≥2 mg/kg/dose at the interim and/or terminal sacrifices. Both liver PKK mRNA expression
and PKK plasma protein increased by the end of the recovery periods. This showed

Donidalorsen was rapidly absorbed into the systemic circulation with median Tmax at 1 to 4

A 26-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Mice With a 13-Week Recovery
(Study Nos. 8405032; 721744-AS04)
Key Study Findings


Mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for
injection), donidalorsen (1, 4, or 12 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059
(4 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for 26 weeks with a 13-week treatment-free recovery period (vehicle
control and 12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen only).



There were no unscheduled deaths during the study that were considered related to treatment
with donidalorsen or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.



Changes in hematology parameters at the end of the 26-week Treatment Period included
increases in white blood cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and/or monocytes in males and/or
females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the
end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in hematology parameters were no longer seen
at the 12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen.



Changes in clinical chemistry parameters at the end of the 26-week Treatment Period
included increases in ALT, AST, and/or ALP in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or
12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen. Effects on clinical chemistry parameters (including ALT,
AST, and ALP) were less clear at 4 mg/kg/dose of ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week
recovery period, increases in ALT and/or AST were still seen in males and/or females at
12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen, while increases in ALP were no longer seen. The
toxicological significance of increases in ALT and AST were unclear as histopathology
findings in the liver appeared to be partially reversible and levels of unconjugated
donidalorsen had declined below the lower limit of quantitation.



Gross pathology findings after the 26-week Treatment Period with donidalorsen were seen in
the liver (discoloration in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen
and enlargement in males at 4 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen) and inguinal lymph nodes (enlarged
in males at 1 and 4 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen). There were no clear gross pathology findings
seen after the 26-week Treatment Period with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059. Gross pathology
findings after the 13-week recovery period at12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen were noted in the
liver (discoloration in males) and subcutaneous injection site (discoloration in males).

13.1.3.2. Genotoxicity

The genotoxicity of donidalorsen was evaluated in a complete battery of GLP-compliant
genotoxicity studies (i.e., in vitro Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration assay in CHL
cells, and in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice).
ISIS 721744: Bacterial Reverse Mutation Assay (Study Nos. G115138; 721744-IS01)
The in vitro Ames assay, using the plate incorporation method, evaluated vehicle, positive
controls, and donidalorsen (15 to 5000 µg/plate) in Salmonella typhimurium TA98, TA100,
TA1535, and TA1537, and Escherichia coli WP2uvrA tester strains (with or without 10% S9
mix for metabolic activation). There was no increase in the number of revertant colonies in any
tester strain, at any donidalorsen concentration, with or without metabolic activation. There was
no toxicity up to highest donidalorsen concentration, in any tester strain, with or without
metabolic activation. Donidalorsen was negative for mutagenicity up to 5000 µg/plate ± S9
metabolic activation.
ISIS 721744: In Vitro Chromosome Aberration Assay in CHL Cells (Study Nos. G115139;
721744-IS02)
The in vitro chromosome aberration assay evaluated vehicle, positive controls, and donidalorsen
at 62.5 to 500 µg/mL in CHL cells for 6 hours (with or without 2% S9 mix for metabolic
activation) and for 22 hours (without S9 mix). No cytotoxicity was noted at up to 500 µg/mL
after 6 hours with or without 2% S9 mix and 22 hours without S9 mix. There was no significant
increase in the number of metaphases with structural or numerical aberrations up to 500 µg/mL
135

Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
after 6 hours (with or without 2% S9 mix) and 22 hours (without S9 mix). Donidalorsen was

Mammalian Micronucleus Assay in Bone Marrow Erythrocytes Following Subcutaneous
Injection of ISIS 721744 to ICR Mice (Study Nos. G120005; 721744-AS05)
The in vivo mammalian micronucleus assay evaluated vehicle, positive control, and donidalorsen
(500, 1000, and 2000 mg/kg SC) administered on Days 1 and 3 (48 hours postdose on Day 1) to
ICR mice. Mice were sacrificed on Day 4 (24 hours postdose on Day 3) for bone marrow
collection. There was no statistically significant increase in the incidence of micronucleated
polychromatic erythrocytes at any dose of donidalorsen tested compared to the vehicle control
(negative control) group. Donidalorsen was negative in the in vivo bone marrow micronucleus
assay in mice.
13.1.3.3. Carcinogenicity
The SPAs for the proposed protocols for the 6-month carcinogenicity study in hemizygous
transgenic (Tg.rasH2) mice and the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats included
recommendations on dose selection based on a non GLP-compliant 14-week DRF study in
Tg.rasH2 mice and 16-week DRF study in Sprague Dawley rats, respectively.
A 14-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 and ISIS 722059 IN CBYB6F1TG(HRAS)2JIC Hemizygous Transgenic Mice (Study No. 721744-AS07P)
Tg.rasH2 mice received SC injections of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection),
donidalorsen (6, 18, or 36 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (6 mg/kg/dose) Q2W.
Animal numbers were noted to be low (n=6/sex/group) and the histopathology examination was
limited (i.e., sternum bone marrow and bone, heart, injection sites, kidneys, liver, lung, spleen,
testes, thymus, gross lesions, and tissue masses). Donidalorsen resulted in dose-dependent
increases in ALP (up to 1.6-fold over control), AST (up to 5.4-fold over control), and ALT (up to
5.1-fold over control) in males at all dose levels. These increases correlated with a dosedependent increase of minimal karyocytomegaly in the liver in males at ≥6 mg/kg Q2W. In
females, only minimal and non-dose-dependent increases in liver enzymes (up to 1.9-fold over
control) were seen and there were no microscopic correlates in the liver. For male mice, the high
dose selection of 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen was based upon incidences of karyocytomegaly
and increases of ALT, AST, and ALP at ≥18 mg/kg/dose in the 14-week DRF study. For female
mice, there were no histopathological findings in the liver and there were minimal non-doserelated elevations of ALT, AST, and ALP in the 14-week DRF study. No dose-limiting toxicity
was identified for female mice in the 14-week DRF study. To evaluate pharmacological effects
in the 6-month carcinogenicity study, male and female mice will receive the mouse surrogate,
ISIS 722059, at a dose of 10 mg/kg/dose, although only a single dose level of 6 mg/kg Q2W was
evaluated in the 14-week DRF study. A MTD for ISIS 722059 was not determined. At 10 mg/kg
Q2W, the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059, is expected to achieve ~>80% reduction in liver PKK
mRNA expression.
The Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee (ECAC) concurred with doses of 0 (0.9%
sodium chloride for injection), 5, 10, and 20 mg/kg Q2W via SC injection in male mice with the

high dose based on a MTD (i.e., incidences of karyocytomegaly and increases of ALT, AST, and

A 16-Week Repeat-Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Sprague Dawley Rats (Study
Nos. 721744-AS08P)
Sprague Dawley rats received SC injections of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for
injection) or donidalorsen (10, 30, or 90 mg/kg) Q2W with one additional loading dose on
Day 8. Animal numbers were noted to be low (vehicle control =3/sex/group; test article-treated
groups =5/sex/group) and the histopathology examination was limited (e.g., gross lesions,
adrenal glands, bone marrow, heart, injection sites, kidneys, liver, lung, lymph nodes, spleen, and
thymus). Decreased body weight gains (>10% from control) were seen in males at
≥30 mg/kg/dose and females at ≥10 mg/kg/dose. In the kidneys, histopathology findings in males
and females at ≥10 mg/kg/dose included minimal to marked basophilic granules in the proximal
convoluted tubule, minimal to mild accumulation of eosinophilic (hyaline) droplets in the
proximal convoluted tubule, and minimal to mild mononuclear interstitial infiltrates.
The Committee concurred with the Applicant’s proposed doses of 0 (0.9% sodium chloride for
injection), 1.5, and 5 mg/kg Q2W via SC injection for both male and female rats. The high dose
was identified as the MTD based on the decrease in body weight gain (i.e., >10% from control in
females at ≥10 mg/kg Q2W) and also class experience with ASO, which suggests that the
observed histopathology lesions in the kidneys (seen in male and female rats at ≥10 mg/kg Q2W)
can progress with longer treatment duration and adversely impact survival in a 2-year study. The
low dose for both male and female rats was approximately one-third of the high dose.
13.1.3.4. Reproductive and Developmental Toxicity
The potential reproductive and developmental toxicity of donidalorsen were evaluated in GLPcompliant combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice with donidalorsen and
mouse surrogate ISIS 722059, a combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice
with the unconjugated parent compound of donidalorsen (ISIS 546254) and the corresponding
unconjugated mouse surrogate (ISIS 482584), and an EFD study in rabbits with the unconjugated
parent compound of donidalorsen (ISIS 546254).
