15.3.4. Eligibility Criteria, Trial CS2
Key eligibility criteria for Part A are summarized below. The trial enrolled subjects ≥18 years of
age with clinically confirmed HAE and an attack frequency that would likely warrant
prophylactic HAE therapy. The inclusion and exclusion criteria are acceptable and consistent
with those used in previous trials of approved products for HAE prophylaxis.
Key Inclusion Criteria


Male or female ≥18 years of age at the time of informed consent.



Diagnosed with clinically confirmed C1-INH (Type I or Type II) HAE based on all of the
following:
– Documented clinical history consistent with HAE (SC or mucosal, nonpruritic swelling
episodes without accompanying urticaria).
– C1-INH functional level <40% normal level. Patients with a functional level of 40% to
50% of normal could be enrolled if their complement factor C4 level was below the LLN
or when a known pathogenic mutation in the SERPING1 gene had been demonstrated.
– At least one of the following: age at HAE onset ≤30 years; family history consistent with
Type I or II HAE; or complement component 1q within the normal range.



Experienced ≥2 HAE attacks during the Screening Period.



Female subjects: nonpregnant, nonlactating, and either surgically sterile, postmenopausal,
abstinent, or using acceptable contraceptive methods.



Male subjects: either surgically sterile or using an acceptable contraceptive method.

Key Exclusion Criteria


Concomitant diagnosis of another form of angioedema, such as idiopathic or acquired
angioedema, recurrent angioedema associated with urticaria, or Type III HAE.



Exposure to any of the following medications:
– ACE inhibitors or any estrogen containing medications with systemic absorption (such as
oral contraceptive or hormonal replacement therapy) within 4 weeks prior to Screening.
– Chronic prophylaxis with Takhzyro® (lanadelumab), Haegarda® (C1-esterase inhibitor
SQ), Cinryze® and Ruconest® (C1 esterase inhibitor) or Orladeyo® (berotralstat) within
5 half-lives prior to Screening (i.e., Takhzyro within 10 weeks prior to Screening,
Haegarda/Berinert 2000/3000® subcutaneously/Cinryze/Ruconest within 2 weeks prior
to Screening, Orladeyo within 3 weeks prior to Screening).
– Oligonucleotides within 4 months of Screening (if a single administration) or 12 months
of Screening (if multiple doses received); does not apply to vaccines.



History of acquired coagulopathies or bleeding diathesis (e.g., thrombocytopenia) and
inherited bleeding disorders (e.g., hemophilia).



Any clinically significant renal or hepatic diseases.

15.3.5. Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial CS2
The final SAP, version 1.0, is dated February 17, 2021.
For Trial CS2, the ITT population included all enrolled or randomized subjects. The per-protocol
(PP) population included all subjects in the ITT population who were treated according to the
protocol without any major deviations.
The primary efficacy endpoint, the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per month (defined
as 28 days) during the On-Treatment Period from Week 1 to Week 17 (28 days after last dose
administration), was compared between donidalorsen-4 and placebo in Part A using a Poisson
regression model and Pearson chi-square scaling of standard errors to account for potential
overdispersion. The model included a fixed effect for treatment group (categorical), the timenormalized Run-In Period attack rate (continuous) as a covariate, and the logarithm of time in
month (days from first dose date to 28 days after last dose administration divided by 28) that
each subject was observed during the period as an offset variable. The primary analysis of the
primary endpoint was conducted in the ITT population.
All secondary endpoints that concerned time-normalized varieties of HAE attacks were analyzed
using the same method as the primary endpoint.
The number of subjects with a clinical response (defined as ≥50%, ≥70%, or ≥90% reduction
from Baseline in HAE attack rate) by Week 17 was analyzed as a risk difference with a
corresponding exact 95% confidence interval and p-value from Fisher’s Exact test using the ITT
and per-protocol populations. For each subject, a Treatment Period HAE attack rate from Week 5
to Week 17 and Run-In Period HAE attack rate was calculated. The percentage reduction will be
calculated as the Treatment Period HAE attack rate from Week 5 to Week 17 minus the Run-In
Period HAE attack rate divided by the Run-In Period HAE attack rate. Subjects who
discontinued treatment early due to lack of efficacy or AEs were considered as nonresponders
and included in the denominator for the calculation of the proportion in the ITT population.
Subjects who discontinued due to other reason were excluded from analysis.
The number and percentage of subjects who achieved HAE attack free (no HAE attacks) by
Week 17 (end of the On-Treatment Period) were tabulated by treatment group and by Part.
Subjects who discontinued treatment early due to lack of efficacy or AEs were considered as
nonresponders and included in the denominator for the calculation of the proportion in the ITT
population. Subjects who discontinued due to other reason were excluded from analysis. The risk
difference between donidalorsen-4 group to the placebo group in Part A, and the corresponding
exact 95% confidence interval were provided along with the Fisher’s Exact test p-value. The
analysis was conducted in both ITT and per-protocol populations.

Reference ID: 5646426

15.3.6. Sample Size Considerations, Trial CS2
The primary endpoint was the time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per month) from
Week 1 to Week 17. From historical data, the placebo group was estimated to have 6.8 HAE
attacks per 4-month period. Assuming the donidalorsen-4 group has 2.8 HAE attacks per 4month period, then with a 0.05 significance level and using Poisson model, the sample size of 18
subjects (12 subjects administered donidalorsen-4, and 6 subjects administered placebo)
provided at least 90% power for the primary endpoint, considering a 10% missing data or
dropout rate for both active treatment and placebo.

15.3.7. Data and Safety Monitoring Committee, Trial
CS2
A Data and Safety Monitoring Committee reviewed safety, tolerability, and efficacy (as needed)
data collected during the trial.

15.3.8. Protocol Amendments, Trial CS2
The original protocol (dated May 3, 2019) was amended three times. Key changes in
Amendment #1 were the addition of several exclusion criteria (related to elevated PTT, history
of coagulopathy or bleeding diathesis, and renal and hepatic diseases); these were added prior to
the first subject’s enrollment. Amendment #2 allowed subjects who completed the Week 17 trial
visit to pursue enrollment in the OLE trial (CS3) at any time after that. Amendment #3 allowed
flexibility to conduct some trial procedures via home healthcare, in response to the COVID-2019
pandemic. These protocol amendments are not expected to have substantially impacted the trial
results.

15.4. Trial CS3
15.4.1. Trial Design, Trial CS3
Trial CS3 is an ongoing phase 2, randomized, open-label extension trial for adults with HAE
Type I or II who completed Trial CS2. The Trial CS3 CSR submitted with the NDA has a data
cutoff date of February 26, 2024. In Trial CS3, 20 subjects were treated with donidalorsen in two
dosing periods: the Fixed Dosing Period followed by the Flexible Dosing Period. In the Fixed
Dosing Period, every subject received donidalorsen-4 for 12 weeks. In the Flexible Dosing
Period, based on Investigator and Sponsor Medical Monitor recommendation, a subject was
treated with either: (1) continued donidalorsen 80 mg every 4 weeks; (2) donidalorsen 80 mg
once every 8 weeks (if attack free for the prior 12 weeks); or (3) donidalorsen 100 mg once every
4 weeks (if not attack free for the prior 12 weeks). At the end of the 52-week Treatment Period
(Fixed Dosing and Flexible Dosing), subjects had the option of: (1) receiving donidalorsen in an
Extended Treatment Period (during which flexible dosing was maintained) for up to an
additional 156 weeks (approximately 3 years), for a Total Treatment Period (Treatment +

the incidence and severity of TEAEs.
The secondary objectives of this trial were to evaluate the efficacy of extended dosing and
alternative dosing and/or dose frequency in patients with HAE. The secondary endpoints were:


The time-normalized HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) by treatment.



Consumption of on-demand medications.

The exploratory objectives of this trial were to characterize the effects of donidalorsen on PKK
levels, plasma proenzyme activation, and cHK levels; to evaluate the effects of donidalorsen on
the clinical and AE-QoL endpoints; and to evaluate PK exposure over time. The exploratory
endpoints were:


Prekallikrein levels, plasma proenzyme activation (only during Year 1), and cHK levels.



Angioedema Quality of Life questionnaire score.

15.4.4. Analysis Populations, Trial CS3
The following analysis populations were defined by the Applicant in the final SAP, version 3.0,
dated March 14, 2024:


The safety population was to include all enrolled subjects who received at least one dose of
donidalorsen.



The ITT population was to include all enrolled subjects.



The per protocol population was to include all subjects in the ITT population who were
treated according to the protocol with no major protocol deviations that could compromise
the interpretation of efficacy. Major protocol deviations that could compromise the
interpretation of efficacy were to be determined prior to the database lock.



The PK population was to include all subjects who enrolled and received at least one dose of
donidalorsen and had at least one evaluable PK sample.

15.4.5. Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial CS3
Per the final SAP, dated March 14, 2024, the primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized
number of HAE attacks. The HAE attack rates, as well as the changes and the percent changes
from baseline during the On-Treatment Period and Fixed Dosing Period, were summarized using
descriptive statistics by the Index Trial treatment group and overall for HAE Type I, II, and III.
The investigator-confirmed HAE attack rate was calculated for each subject as the number of
HAE attacks occurring during the On-Treatment Period divided by number of days the subject
contributed to the period multiplied by 28 days.
For the On-Treatment Period and Fixed Dosing Period, three sets of analysis were performed.
For the first set of analysis, the Trial CS2-on-treatment baseline was used to derive change and
percent change from baseline, regardless of which trial drug the subjects took in the Index Trial.
For the second set of analysis, subjects who took the active drug in the Index Trial used Trial
CS2-Run-In baseline and subjects who took placebo in the Index Trial used OLE baseline to
derive change and percent change from baseline. For the third set of analysis, all subjects used
Trial CS2-Run-In baseline.
Summaries for all analysis periods during the Flexible Dosing Period were only summarized by
dose options, using Trial CS2-Run-In baseline for subjects who took the active drug in the Index
Trial and OLE baseline for subjects who took placebo in the Index Trial. The analysis was
repeated using Trial CS2-Run-In baseline for all subjects. This analysis was also repeated using
the Fixed Dosing Period HAE attack rate as the baseline.
For subjects who received donidalorsen-4 in the Index Trial, an integrated analysis of HAE
attack rates was also done by including data in the Index Trial. Trial CS2-Run-In baseline was
used for derivation of change and percent change from baseline. The time-normalized HAE
attack rate for each subject was calculated as the number of HAE attacks occurring from first
dose of the Index Trial to the end of Treatment Period in the OLE trial divided by number of
days in the period multiplied by 28 days. The data were presented by HAE type.
266
Integrated Review Template, version 4.0 (11/1/23)

Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
Similar analyses were performed for the secondary efficacy endpoints of time-normalized
number of moderate or severe HAE attacks and time-normalized number of HAE attacks
requiring acute therapy. The secondary efficacy endpoints of response rate (subjects who achieve
50%, 70%, 90% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate) and HAE attack free response rate
were summarized by number and percentage of subjects.

15.4.6. Protocol Amendments, Trial CS3
The original protocol (dated January 17, 2020) was amended three times. Key changes in each
respective amendment were to provide the option for each subject to participate in an additional
year of trial participation (with relevant adjustments to the trial schedule of assessments),
lengthening the trial duration to 4 years of treatment with Amendment #3. Additionally,
Amendment #1 provided the option to reduce dosing to 80 mg every 8 weeks in the event of
tolerability or safety issues. Amendment #2 allowed continued flexible dosing of donidalorsen
after Week 41.

15.4.7. Interim Analyses, Trial CS3
The interim analyses presented in the Applicant’s CSR were performed after the data cutoff date
of February 26, 2024 (final database lock on March 26, 2024). The results of the interim analyses
were intended for regulatory submission, not to be used for stopping or adapting the trial or
adjusting the sample size.

15.4.8. Data and Safety Monitoring Committee, Trial
CS3
The safety of donidalorsen was continually monitored throughout the trial by the investigator or
designee and the Applicant or designee. No Data and Safety Monitoring Committee was utilized
for this OLE trial (CS3). Safety was evaluated by the collection and measurement of AEs,
clinical laboratory parameters (including hematology, serum chemistry, and urinalysis),
concomitant medication/procedure information, vital signs, physical examinations, and ECGs.

16.1.3. Primary Efficacy Results, Trial CS2
Table 92 summarizes the efficacy results for the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4
weeks from Week 1 to Week 17 for the primary efficacy endpoint comparison between
donidalorsen-4 and placebo. After adjusting for baseline attack rate and treatment group, the
estimated least square mean time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks was lower in
the donidalorsen-4 (LS mean =0.22, 95% CI =0.10, 0.50) group compared to placebo (LS
mean =2.29, 95% CI =1.54, 3.41). The estimated attack rate ratio for the donidalorsen-4 group
relative to placebo was 0.10 (95% CI =0.04, 0.24). Additionally, the percentage reduction in the
LS means for the donidalorsen-4 group was 90% (95% CI =76%, 96%) relative to placebo.

16.1.4. Type III HAE, Trial CS2
In Trial CS2 Part B, six subjects with HAE-nC1-INH (Type III HAE) were screened, and three
subjects were dosed and completed trial treatment. All three subjects were female, the mean age
was 34 years (range 25 to 40), all were White, and the mean body mass index was 38.4 kg/m2
(range 36 to 42). All three subjects had experienced prior peripheral and abdominal HAE attacks,
and one subject had used lanadelumab and discontinued because it was ineffective. The mean
number of attacks in the previous 12 months was 61.3 (range 36 to 100) and the mean HAE
attack rate in the Run-In Period was 4.23 (values: 2.3, 3, 7.4). The Treatment Period (Week 1 to
Week 17) mean HAE attack rate was 1.52 (values: 0, 0.5, 4.1). The mean reduction in monthly
HAE attack rate was 75% (values: 45, 83, 100).
Due to the open-label conduct and sample size of Trial CS2 Part B, no conclusive evidence about
efficacy can be drawn from this trial.

As summarized in Table 95, most subjects experienced at least one TEAE, the majority of which

The TEAE summary data do not reveal a new safety signal in Trial CS7.

721744-CS7.
For rollover subjects, each adverse event is counted under the dose regimen that the subject was assigned to at the onset of the
event.

17.1.7. Laboratory Findings and Vital Signs, Trial CS7
In the Treatment Period through Week 53, routine clinical testing, including vital signs and
coagulation studies, was performed every 3 months, while certain tests were performed on a
monthly basis: (1) hematology; (2) serum chemistry with hepatic function tests; and (3)
pregnancy testing. In the Extended Treatment Period, only pregnancy testing occurred monthly,
with the other laboratory tests and vital signs evaluated every 3 months. See Section 15.2.2 for
full details.
Noting the limitations of these data without a control group for comparison, no new safety signal
is identified based on the vital sign findings. A discussion of the platelet, coagulation, and
hepatic function laboratory values can be found in Section 7.7.2 and Section 7.7.3.

17.2. Safety Results, Trials CS2 and CS3
Overall, the safety results from Part A of Trial CS2 and for Trial CS3 were consistent with those
of Trial CS5; no new risks were identified. See Section 15.3 and Section 15.4 for details of these
trial designs. The key safety review issues included analysis of Trials C2 and CS3. See
Section 7.7 for details.

17.3. Subgroup Analyses, Trial CS5
The Agency conducted additional safety analyses by sex, age, race and geography using system
organ class and preferred terms to assess for potential safety imbalances. These post hoc
subgroup analyses conducted on a small population have limited interpretability. But overall, no
imbalance was identified.

17.4. 120-Day Safety Update
The Applicant submitted a 120-day safety update on December 19, 2024. The report included
data from ongoing open-label trials (CS3 and CS7) as of the cutoff dates of June 25, 2024, and
June 27, 2024, respectively. The report included updated pooled safety data from Trial CS2,
Trial CS3, Trial CS5, and Trial CS7; the 176 subjects exposed to donidalorsen in these trials had
a median donidalorsen exposure duration of 433 days, versus 168 days for placebo recipients.
Updated safety data from Trial CS3 and Trial CS7 included one fatal event of completed suicide,
recorded as a death, SAE, and permanent treatment discontinuation. This subject was a 48-yearold male with a past medical history of headache, on-trial TEAEs of headache and basilar
migraine, and no known history of depression or anxiety. One subject experienced an SAE of
cellulitis. One subject permanently discontinued trial treatment due to TEAEs of ALT increased
and AST increased (subject met the protocol-defined stopping rules for ALT >5× ULN).
Commonly reported TEAEs were generally consistent with the safety profile observed to date.
The safety update did not identify any new safety signals for donidalorsen.

17.5. Additional Safety Information
17.5.1. ASKCOV Trial
ASKCOV was an investigator-initiated, placebo-controlled clinical trial in Brazil, to evaluate
whether a single dose of 120 mg SC donidalorsen would lead to improved outcomes for patients
with COVID-19 prior to the availability of vaccines. The trial was funded by Ionis. The
investigators hypothesized that targeting and inhibiting prekallikrein would prevent abnormal
activation of the kallikrein-kinin system that leads to angioedema, lung inflammation, and
ultimately vessel blockage, which are complications of severe COVID-19 infections.
A total of 111 hospitalized patients with moderate to severe COVID-19 on supplemental oxygen
were enrolled. There was no statistically significant difference for the primary outcome (number
of days subjects were alive and free of oxygen support up to 15 days after randomization).
Incidences of mortality at Day 30 and the use of mechanical ventilation within 15 days were
approximately doubled in the donidalorsen group versus the placebo group.
The incidence and pattern of TEAEs in the trial did not reveal a concerning imbalance. No
TEAEs led to trial drug discontinuation (as it was a single dose). There were 78 SAEs reported in
32 subjects. The PT of respiratory failure occurred most frequently (26/78 [33%] events),
followed by septic shock (9/78 [12%] events), severe acute respiratory syndrome (5/78 [6%]
events), cardio-respiratory arrest and chronic kidney disease (4/78 [5%] events). None of these
SAEs were reported as related to the trial drug by the investigator. Because all these SAEs are
confounded by the background moderate-to-severe COVID-19 infection, applicability of these
results to the safety profile of donidalorsen in HAE is very limited.

1

Executive Summary

1.1

Introduction

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application
(NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg
(b) (4) (or 80 mg
(b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to
prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years
of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated
antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which binds to human prekallikrein (PKK) messenger
RNA (mRNA) to reduce PKK protein production. The GalNAc molecule preferentially
delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)
on liver cells.
This review focuses on the nonclinical safety assessment of extractables and
leachables for the donidalorsen drug product container closure system (CCS), which
(b) (4)
constitutes a staked needle glass prefilled syringe (PFS) closed with a
rubber plunger stopper that is assembled into an autoinjector to deliver a single dose of
80 mg donidalorsen in 0.8 mL (100 mg/mL). The extractables and leachables
information and study reports were submitted on 08/21/2024 (SDN 1) and 10/11/2024
(SDN 7).
Refer to Section 3.3 (Previous Reviews Referenced) for a list of the other nonclinical
reviews related to the nonclinical evaluation for NDA 219407.

1.2

Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings

The extractables and leachables studies for the donidalorsen drug product CCS
included a controlled extraction study, accelerated leachable study, and leachable study
as part of the stability assessment. As summarized below, there are no nonclinical
safety concerns based on results from these extractables and leachables studies.
In the controlled extraction study, the CCS was filled with aqueous buffer solution (pH 5
or pH 9.5) or water-isopropyl alcohol (50:50 v/v) and sealed with plunger stoppers
(b) (4) (in order to determine the potential impact of
sterilized by
(b) (4)
sterilization on the extractables profile). The detected extractables
are considered common extractables/leachables with the
materials of the CCS. These compounds were not detected in the leachable studies
(accelerated or stability). Further, it did not appear that the sterilization process
(b) (4) ) affected the extractable profile.

Structure or Biochemical Description
The structure of donidalorsen sodium is shown in Figure 1 (Applicant’s Figure).
ISIS 721744 is a 20-mer chimeric 2'-O-methoxymethyl (2’-MOE)-modified ASO with a
mixed backbone made up of phosphorothioate (PS) and phosphodiester (PO)
internucleotide linkages, which targets the mRNA of human PKK. The ASO is
conjugated to triantennary GalNAc via a trishexylamino (THA)-C6 linker, which
preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the ASGPR on liver cells.

Drug Formulation

The donidalorsen drug product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution
for SC administration. The drug product formulation is shown in Table 1 (Applicant’s
Table). The drug product is packaged in a staked needle glass PFS closed with a
(b) (4) rubber plunger stopper and assembled into an autoinjector to deliver
0.8 mL of solution containing 80 mg of donidalorsen (80 mg/0.8 mL = 100 mg/mL).

additional information on the CCS.

2.5

Comments on Extractables and Leachables Studies

The Applicant provided data from a controlled extraction study and an accelerated
leachable study with the donidalorsen drug product CCS. The Applicant also indicated
that a leachable study is ongoing as part of the registration stability protocol and
available data were provided to the NDA. The Applicant indicated that the extractables
and leachables assessment for the CCS was in line with the recommendations for
evaluation of primary packaging in USP <1661>, extractables/leachables testing per
USP <1663>, USP <1664>, and the Product Quality Research Institute (PQRI)
Leachables and Extractables Working Group Initiatives for Parenteral and Ophthalmic
Products.1,2,3
This section describes the donidalorsen drug product CCS as well as the study design
and results for the extractables and leachables studies with the CCS. The nonclinical
safety evaluation for potential leachables is included in Section 11 (Integrated
Summary and Safety Evaluation).
Refer to NDA 219407 Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Integrated Quality Assessment
dated 05/05/2025 for more details on the extractables and leachables assessment from
the quality perspective.

2.6

Proposed Clinical Population and Dosing Regimen

Provided below is regulatory background for the donidalorsen development program as
it relates to extractables and leachables.

The following comment was provided to the Applicant in IND 142564 Type C written
responses dated 12/19/2023:
“The clinical drug product is packaged with 0.8 mL deliverable volume in an ISO 2R
(b)
(b) (4)
Type (4) clear glass vial that is stoppered with a
rubber closure and sealed with an
aluminum overseal. During the phase 3 Open Label Extension study, the intended
commercial configuration will be introduced, which comprises a glass prefilled syringe
(PFS) fitted into an autoinjector (AI). A safety assessment of extractables and
leachables should be provided in the NDA for all primary container closure components
of the device that are in contact with the drug product during storage (i.e., AI and
potentially the vial if it is also used as a commercial configuration), as well as secondary
container closure components where there is a potential for migration of leachables into
the drug product. See USP Chapters for 1663 and 1664 for the design of extractables
and leachables studies, respectively.”
During the filing review of the original submission for this NDA 219407 (SDN 1,
08/21/2024), it appeared that the Applicant had not provided the study reports
associated with the extractables and leachables studies. The following information
request was sent to the Applicant on 09/27/2024:
“We are reviewing your August 21, 2024, NDA submission and have the following
requests for information:
The results of extractable and leachable studies conducted with the drug product
primary container closure system are summarized in Pharmaceutical Development
(Module 3.2.P.2) for the Container Closure System (Module 3.2.P.2.4). To facilitate the
review of your application, provide the finalized study reports associated with these
studies or provide their specific location in the submission.”
The Applicant provided the following response to the information request on 10/11/2024
(SDN 7):
“The product-specific study reports for donidalorsen drug product are provided with this
response.
Module 3.2.P.2.4 Section 7.2 provides a detailed extractables and leachables
assessment for the container closure system (CCS). The assessment is in line with the
recommendations for evaluation of primary packaging in USP <1661>,
extractables/leachables testing per USP <1663>, USP <1664>, and the Product Quality
Research Institute (PQRI) Leachables and Extractables Working Group Initiatives for
Parenteral and Ophthalmic Products.
To confirm the low risk of leachables from the CCS assessment, a product-specific
leachable study is ongoing as part of the registration stability protocol (Module
3.2.P.8.1). Three (3) registration stability batches of the donidalorsen drug product are
being monitored on stability. A tabular summary of leachable results obtained through
12 months storage at the long-term storage condition of 2–8 °C (with 6 weeks in use at
30 °C) and at T=0 and 6 months of storage at 25 °C/60% RH are summarized in Module
3.2.P.2.4 Table 20 and the reports associated with these studies are provided as

The Applicant is seeking approval for donidalorsen for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of
HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The recommended
(b) (4) . A dosing interval of
(b) (4)

(b) (4) may be considered in some patients. The donidalorsen drug product is a sterile,

(b) (4) rubber plunger
packaged in a staked needle glass PFS closed with a
stopper and assembled into an autoinjector to deliver a single dose of 0.8 mL of 80 mg
donidalorsen (80 mg/80 mL = 100 mg/mL).

assessment. In general, for the leachable evaluation, any organic (nonmetal) compound
with expected patient exposure below the PQRI thresholds of 5 μg/day (for compounds
lacking genotoxic potential and irritant potential) and 1.5 μg/day (for compounds with

1

Executive Summary

1.1

Introduction

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application
(NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg
(b) (4) (or 80 mg
(b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to
prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years
of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated
antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which binds to human prekallikrein (PKK) messenger
RNA (mRNA) to reduce PKK protein production. The GalNAc molecule preferentially
delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)
on liver cells.
This review focuses on the nonclinical safety assessment of ISIS 721744 impurities
through review of a 13-week repeat-dose SC toxicity and impurity qualification study of
ISIS 721744 and associated test article related mixtures (TAMs) in ICR mice and also
comparison of impurity levels in the ISIS 721744 clinical batch to the toxicology batch
used in the 39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in monkeys.
Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 03/25/2025 and
Investigational New Drug (IND) 142564 Nonclinical Primary review dated 08/13/2019 for
a review of the nonclinical pharmacology, safety pharmacology,
pharmacokinetics/absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (PK/ADME), and
general toxicology studies for the ISIS 721744 nonclinical program.
Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 03/05/2025 for a review of
the reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 (i.e., combined
fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and pre- and postnatal development
[PPND] study in mice).
Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 12/19/2024 for a review of
the 6-month carcinogenicity study of ISIS 721744, as well as the mouse surrogate, ISIS
722059, by SC injection in CByB6F1- Tg(HRAS)2Jic Hemizygous Transgenic mice
(Tg.rasH2 mice).

1.2

Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings

The Applicant submitted a 13-week repeat-dose SC toxicity and impurity qualification
study in which ICR mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9%
(b) (4) mg/kg total
sodium chloride for injection/solution [saline]) or
oligonucleotide dose level of ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and TAM 2 once every two weeks
(Q2W) for 13-weeks. The two TAMs that were evaluated in the study were made up of
(b) (4) impurities for
ISIS 721744 and associated impurities (i.e.,
(b) (4) impurity for TAM 2). The findings in TAM 1- and TAM 2-treated
TAM 1 and
groups were similar to those in ISIS 721744-treated groups, which included increases in
aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT), increases in
6
Reference ID: 5588258

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

liver weights, and histopathology findings of mononuclear cell infiltration and
karyocytomegaly in the liver and vacuolated granular macrophages at the injection site.
Overall, there were no meaningful differences between the findings in either of the TAM
groups (ISIS 721744 + associated impurities) compared to the ISIS 721744 group alone
and it did not appear that the added impurities affected the toxicity profile of ISIS
721744. Refer to Sections 2.5 and 6.2.
The Applicant conducted a pivotal Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant 39-week
repeat-dose toxicity study of ISIS 721744 (0, 2, 6, 12, and 30 mg/kg/week) in
Cynomolgus monkeys with a 13-week interim sacrifice and 26-week treatment-free
recovery period (Refer to IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary review dated 08/13/2019).
The impurity levels seen in the toxicology batch at the no observed adverse effect level
(NOAEL) of 6 mg/kg/week provide support for the proposed impurity limits for the
clinical batch. Refer to Section 2.5.
Conclusion: Taken together, the 13-week repeat-dose SC toxicity and impurity
qualification study in ICR mice and comparisons of impurity levels between the
39-week toxicology study in monkeys and clinical batches of the drug support the
proposed impurity limits. There are no outstanding nonclinical concerns.

1.3

Recommendations

1.3.1

Approvability

From the nonclinical perspective, NDA 219407 is recommended for approval. There are
no outstanding nonclinical issues.
1.3.2

Additional Non Clinical Recommendations

As described in the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 12/19/2024, the
Applicant should submit the final study report for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats
as a post marketing requirement (PMR) (Refer to IND 142564 pre-NDA Meeting
Preliminary Comments dated 04/10/2024).
1.3.3

Labeling

Nonclinical sections of the product label are evaluated separately.

Structure or Biochemical Description
The structure of donidalorsen sodium is shown in Figure 1 (Applicant’s Figure).
ISIS 721744 is a 20-mer chimeric 2’-MOE-modified ASO with a mixed backbone made
up of phosphorothioate (PS) and phosphodiester (PO) internucleotide linkages, which
targets the mRNA of human PKK. The ASO is conjugated to triantennary GalNAc via a
trishexylamino (THA)-C6 linker, which preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by
binding to the ASGPR on liver cells.

Drug Formulation

The donidalorsen drug product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution
for SC administration. The qualitative and quantitative drug product formulation is
shown in Table 1 (Applicant’s Table). The drug product is packaged in a staked needle
(b) (4) rubber plunger stopper. The
glass prefilled syringe (PFS) closed with a
PFS is assembled into an autoinjector for the final drug product presentation. The
autoinjector delivers a single dose of 80 mg donidalorsen in 0.8 mL (100 mg/mL).
A nonclinical safety evaluation of extractables and leachables of the container closure
system for the drug product is provided in a separate review.
Refer to NDA 219407 Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Integrated Quality Assessment
dated 05/05/2025 for more details on the drug formulation.

2.5

Comments on Impurities/Degradants of Concern

In an internal email dated 03/12/2025, the Quality Reviewer for the drug substance (Dr.
Brian Cawrse) solicited input from the Nonclinical Review Team on the impurity levels in
the donidalorsen drug substance.
The Quality Reviewer summarized the following information:
The Applicant provided the structures, origins, and fates for the oligonucleotide-related
impurities, including those derived from the starting materials and process-related
impurities. For the purposes of reporting, identifying, and qualifying impurities, the
Applicant grouped the impurities on the basis of structure and formation mechanism,
which is typical for oligonucleotide products. The release specification limits total
(b) (4) %, based on previous manufacturing
grouped impurities to between
experience and batch analysis. The Quality Reviewer considered the Applicant’s
approach consistent with other oligonucleotide products, but asked if there were any
nonclinical concerns regarding the impurity levels. For internal descriptive purposes
only, the Quality Reviewer referenced NDA 217779 (Rytelo [imetelstat] by Geron Corp.)

Nonclinical Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation on Impurities
As communicated to the Applicant in the IND 142564 Study May Proceed letter dated
09/30/2019 (Section 2.7): One approach for the determination of appropriate impurity
specifications could involve comparisons of impurity levels in toxicology and clinical
batches of the drug. If impurity levels at the no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL)
of the 39-week monkey study (or 13-week interim sacrifice) provide adequate safety
margins over impurity levels at the maximum proposed clinical dose, this could assist in
determination of appropriate specifications.
The safety margins for the donidalorsen specified oligonucleotide impurities based on
comparing the proposed acceptance criterion at the proposed clinical dose to the
impurity levels in the toxicology lot in the 39-week monkey study are shown in Table 3
or Table 4 based on body weight and body surface area, respectively.

Based on Capaldi et al 2017,1 one approach for evaluating toxicology coverage for
impurities is to multiply the amount of impurity present in the drug substance by the
NOAEL and divide the product by the clinical dose (i.e., 2.7 mg/kg Q4W [80 mg Q4W
considering an average patient weight of 29.5 kg for the adolescent patient population]).
Refer to Table 5 (Applicant’s Table) for toxicology coverage based on this approach.
Per communication with the Quality Reviewer, the Capaldi et al 2017 reference is well
known for oligonucleotide impurities and commonly referenced. The approach for
calculating toxicology coverage is standard and does not raise any concerns from the
quality perspective.

The following comment was provided in the IND 142564 Study May Proceed letter
dated 09/30/2019:
“Provide structures of any impurities and degradants of the drug substance and drug
product in your IND submission. Monitor impurities and degradation products of all
active ingredients and refer to ICH Guidance Q3A(R) and Q3B(R) for possible
qualification requirements. The specific impurity thresholds described in these
guidances do not apply to oligonucleotide-related impurities; however, the general
principles of these guidances do apply. It is expected that you would identify and
measure impurities as well as determine appropriate impurity specifications as IND
development proceeds. One approach for the determination of appropriate impurity
specifications could involve comparisons of impurity levels in toxicology and clinical
batches of the drug. If impurity levels at the no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL)
of the 39-week monkey study (or 13-week interim sacrifice) provide adequate safety
margins over impurity levels at the maximum proposed clinical dose, this could assist in
determination of appropriate specifications.”

Observations and Results
Mortality
Checks for mortality and morbidity were conducted twice per day (AM and PM) during
the treatment period.

22

Eleni Salicru, PhD

There were no unscheduled deaths during the study.
Clinical Signs
Clinical sign observations were made once per day during the pretreatment period,
twice per day during the treatment period, and once prior to necropsy. Detailed clinical
sign observations were made at least once per week during the treatment period.
Injection site observations were made prior to dosing on each dosing day.
There were no clinical sign or injection site findings during the study that were attributed
to treatment with ISIS 721744, TAM 1, or TAM 2.
Body Weights
Body weights were recorded at least once per week during the treatment period and
once prior to necropsy.
There were no body weight changes during the study that were attributed to treatment
with ISIS 721744, TAM 1, or TAM 2.
Feed Consumption
Food consumption was measured at least once per week during the treatment period.
There were no feed consumption changes during the study that were attributed to
treatment with ISIS 721744, TAM 1, or TAM 2.
Ophthalmoscopy
Ophthalmic examinations using binocular indirect ophthalmoscope after treatment with
mydriatic agent were conducted once during the pretreatment period and once during
Week 13 of the treatment period.
There were no ophthalmic findings during the study that were attributed to treatment
with ISIS 721744, TAM 1, or TAM 2.

Not evaluated

Blood samples were collected from the last 5 animals/sex/group for hematology

to treatment with ISIS 721744 or TAM 1. Red blood cell values were minimally

Peer Review
Yes. A peer review was conducted by an expert Peer Review Pathologist (facility not in

Peer Review Pathologists followed a robust scientific methodology, ensured that slides
were stored properly, and that records related to the chain of custody of the slides.
Histological Findings
Histopathology findings attributed to treatment with ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and/or TAM 2
were noted in the liver and injection site (Table 11).
Liver
Minimal to slight mononuclear cell infiltration was seen in males and/or females at (b) (4)
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and/or TAM 2.
Minimal karyocytomegaly was seen in males only at (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744,
TAM 1, and TAM 2. Hepatocellular karyocytomegaly correlated with minimally increased
ALT and AST and increased liver weight in males. This finding was attributed to uptake
and accumulation of ASOs into the liver.
Reviewer’s Note: Karyocytomegaly reflects hepatocyte polyploidy that occurs when
there is duplication of nuclear material in the absence of cytokinesis. Changes can
consist of increased numbers of diploid nuclei per hepatocyte or an increase in the
ploidy level of a single hepatocyte nucleus. Spontaneous occurrence of
karyocytomegaly is commonly seen in aging rodents and is not typically associated with
increased liver weight. This aging change, often referred to as polyploidy, is more
common in mice than in rats (NTP).2
Injection Site
Minimal to slight vacuolated granular macrophages were seen in males and females at
(b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744,
(b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 1, and
(b) (4)
mg/kg/dose TAM 2. This finding was attributed to uptake and accumulation of ASOs into
the macrophages.

2National Toxicology Program. US Department of Health and Human Services. Nonneoplastic Lesion

Atlas. https://ntp.niehs.nih.gov/atlas/nnl/hepatobiliary-system/liver/Hepatocyte-Karyomegaly

Dosing Solution Analysis
The dose formulations for ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and TAM 2 were provided ready-to-use
to the conducting laboratory by the Applicant. The Applicant verified concentrations of
ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and TAM 2 using a qualified UV spectroscopy or IP-HPLC-UV-MS
procedure. The Applicant verified stability of TAM 1 and TAM 2 using a qualified IPHPLC-UV-MS procedure.
The measured concentrations of the dosing solutions met the acceptance criterion of
(b) (4) of the label claim. There were no significant changes in the impurity
profiles of the test articles based on stability testing.

1

Executive Summary

1.1

Introduction

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application
(NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg
(b) (4) (or 80 mg
(b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to
prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years
of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated
antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which binds to human prekallikrein (PKK) messenger
RNA (mRNA) to reduce PKK protein production. The GalNAc molecule preferentially
delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)
on liver cells.
This review focuses on the nonclinical pharmacology, safety pharmacology,
pharmacokinetics/absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (PK/ADME), and
general toxicology studies for the ISIS 721744 nonclinical program that were not
previously reviewed. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary Review dated
08/13/2019 for the primary pharmacology, safety pharmacology, PK/ADME, and general
toxicology studies that were previously reviewed.
Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 12/19/2024 for a review of
the 6-month carcinogenicity study of ISIS 721744, as well as the mouse surrogate, ISIS
722059, by SC injection in CByB6F1- Tg(HRAS)2Jic Hemizygous Transgenic mice
(Tg.rasH2 mice) and to NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 03/05/2025 for a
review of the reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 (i.e.,
combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and pre- and postnatal
development [PPND] study in mice).
Together, these studies entail the nonclinical studies to support the safety of
donidalorsen for marketing approval.

1.2

Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings

Primary Pharmacology
Donidalorsen is a GalNAc-conjugated ASO that binds to PKK mRNA in the liver which
causes ribonuclease H1 (RNase H1)-mediated degradation of PKK mRNA to reduce
production of PKK protein by the liver. PKK is a pro enzyme for plasma kallikrein, which
results in the release of bradykinin, a potent vasodilator causing swelling and pain in
HAE. In patients with HAE, C1 inhibitor (C1 INH) deficiency or dysfunction leads to
excessive plasma kallikrein activity, bradykinin generation, and angioedema attacks.
Donidalorsen lowers PKK concentration, preventing excessive bradykinin production in
patients with HAE.
As described by the Applicant: Over 1300 ASOs were designed to target various sites
within the human PKK gene and were evaluated for their ability to inhibit the level of
PKK mRNA in vitro in the human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line HepaRG. Of those
7
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

ASOs, ISIS 546254, an unconjugated 2'-O-methoxyethyl (2′-MOE) gapmer ASO with a
uniform phosphorothioate (PS) backbone, was identified as a lead candidate.
Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) was derived from ISIS 546254 as a 2′-MOE gapmer ASO
with the same nucleobase sequence as ISIS 546254 but with a mixed PS and
phosphodiester (PO) backbone and conjugated to a trivalent GalNAc3.
Specificity analysis of ISIS 721744 to PKK mRNA was performed with the unconjugated
PKK ASO, ISIS 546254. ISIS 546254 is perfectly matched to only PKK mRNA in human
transcriptome (targets site free of meaningful sequence variation). Refer to the IND
142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
In an in vitro study, ISIS 721744 and unconjugated PKK ASO, ISIS 546254, induced a
dose-dependent reduction of PKK mRNA in human hepatocytes with supporting stromal
with IC50 values of 0.19 mcM vs. 8.73 mcM, respectively. Refer to the IND 142564
Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
In an in vitro study, unconjugated PKK ASO, ISIS 546254, reduced human PKK mRNA
levels by greater than 90% in a concentration-dependent manner in human
hepatocellular cell lines HepaRG and Hep3b with corresponding IC50 of 0.31 mcM and
0.35 mcM, respectively.
In an in vivo study in mice, SC administration of unconjugated PKK ASO mouse
surrogate, ISIS 482584, for 3 weeks caused a dose-dependent reduction of PKK liver
mRNA and PKK plasma protein. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated
08/13/2019.
In an in vivo study in mice, SC administration of unconjugated PKK ASO mouse
surrogate, ISIS 482584, for 3 weeks caused inhibition of basal vascular permeability,
captopril-induced vascular permeability, and C1 INH ASO-induced vascular permeability
in the colon of mice. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
In an in vivo study in mice, SC administration of unconjugated PKK ASO mouse
surrogate ISIS 482584 for 3 weeks reduced basal activated high molecular weight
kininogen cleavage in blood of male mice. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review
dated 08/13/2019.
In an in vivo study in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice, single SC administration of
ISIS 721744 on Day 0 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent reduction of plasma PKK
protein that approached 91% at the highest dose tested (10 mg/kg) on Day 14 after
treatment. PKK levels were still 20% below baseline levels by Day 56 (last time point
evaluated) at 10 mg/kg.
Safety Pharmacology
The safety pharmacology evaluations for the cardiovascular, respiratory, and central
nervous system (CNS) were combined into one study in Cynomolgus monkeys. There
were no test article-related effects on cardiovascular, respiratory, or CNS parameters in

8
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

male Cynomolgus monkeys evaluated for up to 24 hours after SC administration of 12
and 30 mg/kg ISIS 721744. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated
08/13/2019.
In the in vitro human ether-a-go-go-related gene (hERG) assay, ISIS 721744 did not
inhibit hERG potassium channel current in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK-293)
mammalian cells stably transfected with hERG complementary DNA (cDNA) compared
to the vehicle control. In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to interact with the
hERG channel.
PK/ADME
In an in vitro evaluation of plasma protein binding of ISIS 721744 (0.5, 5, and 150
mcg/mL) in human, monkey, and mouse plasma, ISIS 721744 was highly bound
(≥96.81%) to whole plasma proteins in all three species. The extent of plasma protein
binding of ISIS 721744 was similar across all species. Refer to IND 142564 Nonclinical
Review dated 08/13/2019.
The in vitro mean blood to plasma ratio of ISIS 721744 was between 0.630 and 0.824 in
human, 0.468 and 0.566 in monkey, and 0.501 and 0.661 in rat suggesting that ISIS
721744 distributes mostly in the plasma compartment across the concentrations tested
in all three species.
Based on metabolic profiling and identification of ISIS 721744 oligonucleotide-related
metabolites in urine from mice, monkeys, and humans, the Applicant described that the
primary route of elimination of donidalorsen is initial rapid hydrolysis of the GalNAc
conjugate in tissues (presumed to be primarily in the liver based on directed distribution
to the liver), followed by slow nuclease-mediated metabolism of the unconjugated
oligonucleotide, and subsequent excretion of chain-shortened metabolites, as well as
full-length oligonucleotides, albeit minor in urine and feces. There were no unique
metabolites identified in humans compared to animal species.
Based on metabolic profiling, identification, and quantitation of ISIS 721744 linkerrelated metabolites in plasma, urine, and/or fecal samples from mice, monkeys, and/or
humans, the Applicant described that the GalNAc moiety is hydrolyzed intracellularly
following uptake into tissues, and the trishexylamino (THA) linker undergoes extensive
oxidative metabolism, and is nearly completely eliminated via biliary excretion, and to a
lesser extent, renal excretion, within 24 hours after administration.
Toxicology
In the pivotal Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant chronic toxicity study in
Cynomolgus monkeys (pharmacologically relevant species), monkeys received SC
doses of ISIS 721744 at 0, 2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose. The monkeys were dosed for 39weeks (dosing on Days 1, 5, 9, and 14 [loading doses] and once weekly thereafter) with
a 13-week interim sacrifice (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the
interim sacrifice). A 26-week treatment-free recovery period was included after both the
13-week interim dosing interval (30 mg/kg/dose) and the 39-week dosing interval (0, 2,

9
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

6, 12 mg/kg/dose) to assess potential reversibility of any observed effects. Refer to
Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/13/2019 for details. In brief, the main test articlerelated findings included thrombocytopenia in two animals (12 and 30 mg/kg/dose) and
histopathology findings of basophilic granules in various organs/tissues (including
kidneys, liver, lymph nodes, and injection site) that in the absence of correlating
histopathology were considered consistent with oligonucleotide uptake and not
considered adverse. There were dose-dependent decreases in hepatic PKK mRNA
expression and dose-dependent and time-dependent decreases in PKK plasma protein
after treatment with ISIS 721744 at ≥2 mg/kg/dose at the interim and/or terminal
sacrifices. Both hepatic PKK mRNA expression and plasma protein increased by the
end of the recovery periods. Tissue concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 in liver
or kidney increased in a dose-dependent manner. The no observed adverse effect level
(NOAEL) was 6 mg/kg/week based on thrombocytopenia in two monkeys at the higher
dose levels of 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose. The NOAEL corresponded to a Cmax of 6.57
mcg/mL and an AUC0-48hr of 37.6 mcg*hr/mL on Day 273.
In the pivotal chronic toxicity study in mice (not a pharmacologically relevant species),
mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for
Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 12 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate, ISIS
722059, (4 mg/kg/dose) once every two weeks (Q2W) for 26 weeks with a 13-week
treatment-free recovery period (vehicle control and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 dose
groups only). This study, as designed, could assess potential off-target effects of ISIS
721744 and potential on-target effects using the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059.
Changes in clinical chemistry parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period
included increases in alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase
(AST), and/or alkaline phosphatase (ALP) in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Effects on clinical chemistry parameters (including ALT, AST,
and ALP) were less clear at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week
recovery period, increases in ALT and/or AST were still seen in males and/or females at
12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, while increases in ALP were no longer seen. The
toxicological significance of increases in ALT and AST were unclear as histopathology
findings in the liver appeared to be partially reversible and levels of unconjugated ISIS
721744 had declined below the lower limit of quantitation. Histopathology findings after
the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744 were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC
dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week
treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose
sites, spleen, and testis.
• Liver: Minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy was noted in
males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in one female (moderate) at
12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. This finding correlated with increased mean liver
weights at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and increased liver enzymes (AST,
ALT, and/or ALP). Despite a background incidence of hepatocyte vacuolation in
vehicle control males, there was an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of
hepatocyte vacuolation in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which
correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels.
These changes were attributed to uptake of ISIS 721744 into the liver.

Skin/Subcutis: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of mononuclear
cells, mixed cells, and/or vacuolated macrophages in the skin/subcutis were
noted in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Increased incidences and/or severity of vacuolated
fibrocytes in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Slight to moderate
inflammation in the skin was noted in females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744. These findings in the skin/subcutis correlated with increased leukocyte
counts.
SC dose sites: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of vacuolated
macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte
vacuolation at the SC injection sites were noted in males and/or females at 1, 4,
and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These
findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
Inguinal Lymph Nodes: Increased incidences and severities (minimal to marked)
of increased lymphocytes in males at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744
and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in the inguinal lymph
node. This finding in the inguinal lymph node correlated with increased leukocyte
counts. Amyloid in the inguinal lymph node was noted in one male at 4
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
Spleen: Increased incidence and/or severity of extramedullary hematopoiesis in
the spleen was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and correlated with increased mean
spleen weight in males administered 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
Testis: Moderate interstitial cell hyperplasia, minimal sperm stasis, and minimal
vacuolation were noted in the testis of males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.

Histopathology findings after the 13-week recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744 were still noted in the liver as hepatocellular vacuolation in males and females,
which correlated with increased liver weights. Histopathology findings in the
skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744 were not seen at the end of the recovery period.
Unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measurable in a dose-dependent manner in the kidney
(greater than dose proportional) and liver (dose proportional) after 26 weeks of
treatment with ISIS 721744. The mean concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744
were similar in the kidney and liver except at 12 mg/kg/dose where mean unconjugated
ISIS 721744 concentrations were greater in the kidney than in the liver. Mean
unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were higher in females than in males in the
kidney but similar in the liver. After the 13-week treatment-free recovery period at 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were below
or near the lower limit of quantitation of 0.107 mcg/g, suggesting complete clearance of
ISIS 721744.

Mouse PKK mRNA in mouse liver was reduced by 77% (statistically significant)
compared to vehicle control in mice treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4
mg/kg/dose for 26 weeks.
The NOAEL was 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, as test article-related findings were
considered related to the oligonucleotide uptake.
Conclusions
The nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology studies were adequate to support the
safety of donidalorsen for marketing. There are no outstanding concerns from the
nonclinical perspective.

1.3

Recommendations

1.3.1

Approvability

From the nonclinical perspective, NDA 219407 is recommended for approval. There are
no outstanding nonclinical issues.

Applicant should submit the final study report for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats
as a post marketing requirement (PMR) (Refer to IND 142564 pre-NDA Meeting
Preliminary Comments dated 04/10/2024).

Structure or Biochemical Description
The structure of donidalorsen sodium is shown in Figure 1 (Applicant’s Figure).
ISIS 721744 is a 20-mer chimeric 2’-MOE-modified ASO with a mixed backbone made
up of PS and PO internucleotide linkages, which targets the mRNA of human PKK. The
ASO is conjugated to triantennary GalNAc via a THA-C6 linker, which preferentially
delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the ASGPR on liver cells.

Regulatory Background

Provided below is a summary of the regulatory background for the donidalorsen
development program.
There was no pre-IND under the associated IND 142564. New IND 142564 was
received on 07/15/2019 for a phase 2a clinical study (Protocol No. ISIS 721744-CS2) to
assess the clinical efficacy of 80 mg ISIS 721744 (once monthly for 12-weeks) in
patients with HAE. The clinical study was allowed to proceed based on the 30-day
safety review and subsequently nonhold comments were provided in the Study May
Proceed later dated 09/30/2019.
A Type B End of Phase 2 (EOP2) meeting teleconference meeting between the
Sponsor and the FDA occurred on 08/30/2021 to discuss the adequacy of the existing
and proposed nonclinical and clinical development package to support a marketing
application for ISIS 721744 for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in patients 12
years of age and older. The Nonclinical Team indicated that the nonclinical evaluation of
the metabolism of ISIS 721744 and its THA linker was limited. As such, the Sponsor
was asked to provide data that characterizes the metabolism of ISIS 721744 and its
THA linker through literature (Sponsor’s work and/or non-proprietary literature) and
actual metabolism studies in monkey and mouse (as needed) prior to the start of phase
3 clinical studies to demonstrate reasonable comparability to human metabolism. In
addition, the FDA agreed that an embryofetal development (EFD) study of ISIS 721744
in rabbits was not needed. Refer to IND 142564 EOP2 Meeting Minutes dated
10/18/2021 for added details. Also, refer to NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review
dated 03/05/2025 for added details on the regulatory history related to the reproductive
and developmental toxicology program.
The initial Pediatric Study Plan (iPSP) for ISIS 721744 for HAE was submitted on
11/18/2021, with subsequent revisions submitted on 05/03/2022, and the agreed iPSP
submitted on 06/06/2022. As part of the iPSP, the Sponsor indicated that they planned
to conduct a 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study of ISIS 721744 in juvenile CD-1 mice
with a 6-week recovery period to support the inclusion of patients with HAE between 2
to <12 years of age. FDA communicated that a draft unaudited report of the juvenile
toxicity study in mice should be available prior to the start of the pediatric clinical trial
and a final report would be expected within 120 days after providing the draft unaudited
report. As such, the Sponsor submitted the draft protocol for the juvenile toxicity study in
mice on 07/11/2023 (see IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/28/2023).
The FDA communicated comments on the draft protocol to the Sponsor on 08/31/2023.
A Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) 1 for the 2-year study in rats was submitted on
08/05/2022 and denied on 08/17/2022 due to the lack of SEND datasets for the
supporting 16-week dose range finding study in rats. SPA 1 was resubmitted on
09/30/2022 with the SEND datasets. FDA agreed with the proposed 2-year
carcinogenicity study in rats on 11/04/2022. SPA 2, which proposed a 6-month
carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice, was submitted on 10/12/2022, and was agreed

16
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

upon on 11/16/2022 for male mice but not for female mice (as no acceptable basis for
dose selection could be identified).
In pre-NDA meeting preliminary comments (Refer to IND 142564 pre-NDA Meeting
Preliminary Comments dated 04/10/2024), the FDA agreed that it would be acceptable
to submit the report of the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and a
summary of the in-life data for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the
NDA submission and to submit the final report as a PMR.
Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 12/19/2024 for added
details on the regulatory history related to the genetic toxicology and carcinogenicity
programs.
NDA 219407 for donidalorsen was submitted on 08/21/2024, and the application was

4.1

Primary Pharmacology

As described in Section 3.1, most of the primary pharmacology studies for the
nonclinical development of ISIS 721744 were previously reviewed (refer to the IND
142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019). Included below is a review of two
primary pharmacology studies not previously reviewed.
In Vitro Characterization of Human Prekallikrein Antisense Oligonucleotide ISIS 721744
Activity (Study No. ECID129371)
Two human hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines (HepaRG and Hep3b) were
electroporated with ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744 with
the same sequence) or ISIS 141923 (control oligonucleotide with no matches to any
sites within the human transcriptome) and incubated for 24 hours under the
experimental conditions of the study, lysed for RNA isolation, and analyzed for human
PKK mRNA. As described in the study report, the sequence of ISIS 546254 was
identified from screens and dose-response confirmations of over 1300 unconjugated
ASOs that were designed throughout the human PKK primary transcript and then
determined to be a lead compound for its ability to inhibit the level of PKK mRNA at a
single concentration in the human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line, HepaRG.
As shown in Figure 2 (Applicant’s Figure), ISIS 546254 reduced human PKK mRNA
levels by greater than 90% in a concentration-dependent manner in human
hepatocellular cell lines HepaRG and Hep3b with corresponding IC50 of 0.31 mcM and
0.35 mcM, respectively. The control oligonucleotide ISIS 141923 did not reduce PKK
mRNA in either cell line.

In Vivo Evaluation of ISIS 721744 Activity in Human KLKBl/PKK Transgenic Mice
(Study No. ELN 23-100d)
Transgenic mice expressing the human KLKB1/PKK gene (n = 2 males/group + 2
females/group) were treated with single SC dose levels of ISIS 721744 at 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3,
and 10 mg/kg. Blood was collected on Days -1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 42 and 56 and human PKK
plasma protein levels were evaluated by ELISA.
As shown in Figure 3 (Applicant’s Figure), ISIS 721744 reduced plasma human PKK
protein in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice in a dose- and time-dependent manner.
Human PKK protein was reduced up to a maximum of about 91% on Day 14 after
treatment with 10 mg/kg ISIS 721744. After Day 14, plasma PKK protein levels
gradually increased to baseline levels and were restored by Day 42 or Day 56 at 1
mg/kg or 3 mg/kg ISIS 721744, respectively. At Day 56, PKK levels plasma PKK protein
levels at 10 mg/kg were still 20% below baseline levels.
As shown in Figure 4 (Applicant’s Figure), based on non-linear curve fit analysis, ED50
at Days 7 and 14 after treatment with ISIS 721744 was 0.67 and 0.75 mg/kg,
respectively.

Secondary Pharmacology

There were no secondary pharmacology studies conducted.

4.3

Safety Pharmacology

As described in Section 3.1, the GLP-compliant safety pharmacology study for the
evaluation of cardiovascular, respiratory, and CNS parameters following SC
administration of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus monkeys was previously reviewed (refer
to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019). Included below is a review of
the GLP-compliant hERG assay with ISIS 721744.
Effect of ISIS 721744 on Cloned hERG Potassium Channels Expressed in Human
Embryonic Kidney Cells (Study No. 210830.JTJ; 721744-IS08)
HEK-293 cells were stably transfected with hERG cDNA and treated with ISIS 721744
(30 and 300 mcM) at near-physiological temperature to measure the effect on ionic
currents by whole-cell patch-clamp technique.
ISIS 721744 inhibited hERG current by 0.5% and 1.9% at 30 mcM and 300 mcM,
respectively (not statistically significant) versus 2.4% for the vehicle control. The IC50 for

27
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

the inhibitory effect of ISIS 721744 on hERG potassium current was not calculated but
was estimated to be greater than 300 mcM. The positive control article (60 nM
terfenadine) inhibited hERG potassium current by 85.6%. In general, oligonucleotides
are not thought to interact with the hERG channel.

5

Pharmacokinetics/ADME/Toxicokinetics

5.1

PK/ADME

As described in Section 3.1, the in vitro evaluation of the extent of plasma protein
binding of ISIS 721744 in human, monkey, and mouse plasma by ultrafiltration was
previously reviewed (refer to IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019).
Included below are the PK/ADME studies not previously reviewed.
Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion of [3H]ISIS 721744 following a
Single Subcutaneous Dose Administration to Sprague Dawley Rats (Study No. IPI/06;
721744-APK02)
This study determined the ADME properties of [3H]ISIS 721744 (2 or 10 mg/kg) after
single SC administration to non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats.
• PK parameters and tissue distribution of total radioactivity were evaluated in
blood, plasma, and tissues after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 2
mg/kg and a radioactive dose level of 200 μCi/kg to male non-pigmented
Sprague Dawley rats.
• Mass balance and routes and extent of excretion of total radioactivity were
evaluated after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 2 mg/kg and a
radioactive dose level of 200 μCi/kg to male non-pigmented Sprague Dawley
rats.
• Tissue distribution of radioactivity was evaluated using Quantitative Whole Body
Autoradiography (QWBA) after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10
mg/kg and a radioactive dose level of 500 μCi/kg to male and female nonpigmented Sprague Dawley rats.
• Metabolite identification and profiling was evaluated after single SC
administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10 mg/kg and a radioactive dose level of
500 μCi/kg to male and female non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats.
• One male non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rat served as a control (i.e., received
a single SC dose of sterile isotonic saline).
Following a single SC dose of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 2 mg/kg to male non-pigmented
Sprague Dawley rats, Cmax of 0.375 and 0.538 μg equiv./mL were reached in the blood
and plasma, respectively, at 1 hour for both, after which radioactivity declined in a
biphasic manner. The blood:plasma ratio calculated from AUC0-∞ was 0.76. Cmax (μg
equiv./g) of 24.40 at 24 hours and 14.89 at 168 hours were reached in the liver and
kidney, respectively. Most tissues achieved concentrations similar to or slightly above
the blood radioactivity concentrations. Tissue:blood ratios at 24 hours were highest in
the liver and kidney (1877 and 850, respectively) consistent with uptake of ISIS 721744.
The thyroid gland, pancreas, large and small intestine, spleen, lymph node, and bone
marrow had tissue:blood ratios between 24.2 to 69.2 at 24 hours.
28
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Following a single SC dose of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 2 mg/kg to male non-pigmented
Sprague Dawley rats, the mean cumulative recovery (0 to Day 56) of radioactivity in
excreta was 76.8% (17.14% from urine + 57.46% from feces + 2.16% from cage wash).
Residual radioactivity in the carcass on Day 56 accounted for 5.84% of the administered
dose resulting in an overall recovery of 82.6%.
Following a single SC dose of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10 mg/kg to male and female nonpigmented rats, radioactivity was distributed to tissues by the first sampling time at 2
hours and reached maximal concentrations within 2 to 48 hours postdose with highest
concentrations of radioactivity in the kidney, liver, intestinal mucosa, salivary gland,
bone marrow, lymph nodes and splenic red pulp. Concentrations of radioactivity in most
organs/tissues decreased by the end of the sampling period at 336 hours, except for the
kidney where radioactivity levels remained at similar levels throughout the sampling
period.
Recovery of radioactivity in urine and feces from non-pigmented rats following a single
SC dose of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10 mg/kg was 0.35% and 1.37% of dose, respectively
for males and 0.30% and 1.31% of dose, respectively for females. See also below.
Metabolite Profiling and Identification Studies following a Single Subcutaneous Dose
Administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 to Male and Female Rats (Study No. IPI/07; 721744APK02)
This study evaluated the metabolic profile of ISIS 721744 in rat whole blood and
plasma, liver and kidney tissues, and in the excreta (urine and feces) by liquid
chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS
721744 at 10 mg/kg to male and female non-pigmented rats.
A summary of metabolites is shown in Table 2 (Applicant’s Table).
ISIS 721744 was seen in the liver, kidney, plasma and whole blood. ISIS 721744 was
the major component at 2 hours in plasma and blood but was not detected at 24 hours
in plasma and blood. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 (i.e. ISIS 780124) was the major
component in liver (2 and 24 hours) and kidney (24 hours). Two major components
were present in the kidney at 2 hours: unconjugated ISIS 721744 (i.e. ISIS 780124) and
ISIS 721744 minus 3 GalNAc sugars (i.e. ISIS 721744 -3 GalNAc). Two major
components were detected in feces samples at 0 to 24 hours: ISIS 780124 3’N-18 and
ISIS 780124 3’N-17. Several ISIS 780124 shortmers were identified as major
components in urine at 0 to 24 hours, from ISIS 780124 3’N-10 to ISIS 780124 3’N-14.
As described in the study report, all identified metabolites were consistent with
nuclease-mediated metabolism to chain shortened oligonucleotides with full, partial, or
without GalNAc or linker-conjugation.

A 6-Week Subcutaneous Repeat-Dose Pharmacokinetic Study of ISIS 721744 in CD-1
Mice (Study No. G122111; 721744-APK03)
In this study, male ICR mice were treated by SC administration with ISIS 721744 (10 or
20 mg/kg/week once weekly) for 6 weeks (Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, 36 and 43) to
determine the PK profile and distribution of ISIS 721744 to kidney and liver. As
described in the study report, concentrations of total full-length ISIS 721744, including
fully-conjugated, partially-conjugated (minus 1-, 2-, and 3-GalNAc sugars), and
unconjugated ISIS 721744 (ISIS 780124), were determined in mouse plasma by a
validated hybridization electrochemiluminescence (ECL) assay, while concentrations of
unconjugated ISIS 721744 in kidney and liver samples were analyzed by a validated
high-performance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry mass spectrometry
(HPLC-MS/MS) bioanalytical method.
As shown in Table 3 (Applicant’s Table), Tmax values were 0.5 hours on Days 1 and 43
at 10 and 20 mg/kg ISIS 721744. Cmax and AUC increased in a slightly greater than
dose proportional manner on Days 1 and 43. There was lack of accumulation after
repeat dosing.
Table 3

Plasma Pharmacokinetics from 6-Week Subcutaneous Repeat-Dose
Study of ISIS 721744 in CD-1 Mice (Applicant’s Table)

As shown in Table 4 (Applicant’s Table) unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measured in
the liver and kidney after repeat-dose treatment with ISIS 721744. Concentrations of
unconjugated ISIS 721744 were higher in the kidney than in the liver. Concentrations of
unconjugated ISIS 721744 in the liver were similar at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week possibly
due to saturation of tissue uptake at these dose levels.

In Vitro Evaluation of Whole Blood and Plasma Concentration Ratio of ISIS 721744
(Donidalorsen) in Human, Monkey and Rat (Study No. IIS-P2-008; 721744-IS11)
This study determined the in vitro blood to plasma ratio of ISIS 721744 in human whole
blood (neat, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, and 2 mcg/mL) and monkey and rat whole blood
(neat, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100, and 200 mcg/mL) using a hybridization ECL detection
method.
As shown in Table 5 (Applicant’s Table), the in vitro mean blood to plasma ratio of ISIS
721744 was between 0.630 and 0.824 in human, 0.468 and 0.566 in monkey, and 0.501
and 0.661 in rat suggesting that ISIS 721744 distributes primarily in the plasma
compartment across the concentrations tested in all three species.

Metabolic Profiling and Identification of ISIS 721744 Oligonucleotide-Related
Metabolites by HPLC-HRMS in Select Urine Samples from Mice, Monkeys, and
Humans (Study No. 727-085, 727-081, ISIS 721744-CS1; 721744-IS10)
This study identified ISIS 721744 oligonucleotide containing metabolites (full-length or
chain-shortened) from urine samples at steady state from mice, monkeys, and humans
treated with multiple SC doses of ISIS 721744 (i.e., 10 mg/kg dose group from 13-week
repeat-dose toxicity study in mice [Study No. 721744-AS01]; 30 mg/kg dose group from
39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in monkeys [Study No. 721744-AS02]; and 80 mg
dose group from phase 1 study in humans with dosing every four weeks for four total
doses [Study No. ISIS 721744-CS1]) using liquid chromatography with a tandem
ultraviolet (UV) detector and high-resolution mass spectrometer (HPLC/UV/HRMS)
method.
As described in the study report:
The oligonucleotide portions of conjugated ASO molecules are metabolized by
hydrolysis of the phosphodiester bonds via endo-nuclease and/or exo-nuclease (either
5' and/or 3') enzymes. Metabolism of the GalNAc-conjugation component of ISIS
721744 typically occurs by a sequential loss of the three GalNAc sugar moieties (-1, -2,
and -3 GalNAc), followed by the loss of a portion, or all the remaining THA linker.1,2
Complete loss of the THA linker results in the formation of ISIS 780124, the
unconjugated version of ISIS 721744. The metabolism of the two portions of ISIS
721744 (oligonucleotide and GalNAc) may occur simultaneously resulting in many
potential metabolites with multiple potential metabolic pathways responsible for a single
metabolite compound.
The study report grouped the likely metabolites of ISIS 721744 as follows:

Distribution and biotransformation of therapeutic antisense oligonucleotides and conjugates. Drug Discov
Today. 2021 Oct;26(10):2244-2258.
2Shemesh CS, Yu RZ, Gaus HJ, Greenlee S, Post N, Schmidt K, Migawa MT, Seth PP, Zanardi TA,
Prakash TP, Swayze EE, Henry SP, Wang Y. Elucidation of the Biotransformation Pathways of a
Galnac3-conjugated Antisense Oligonucleotide in Rats and Monkeys. Mol Ther Nucleic Acids. 2016 May
10;5(5):e319.
