Eleni Salicru, PhD

1. Families I through IV arise from multiple routes of sequential hydrolysis of the
GalNAc and THA linker portion of ISIS 721744:
a. Family I: Intact GalNAc and linker attached, and loss of the nucleotides at
the 3'-end to produce 3′ n-X metabolites.
b. Family II: Loss of one GalNAc sugar to become ISIS 721744(GalNAc)2THA-20-mer, and loss of nucleotides at the 3′-end to produce 3′
n-X metabolites.
c. Family III: Loss of two GalNAc sugars to become ISIS 721744(GalNAc)1THA-20-mer, followed by sequential loss of the nucleotides at
the 3′-end to produce 3′ n-X metabolites.
d. Family IV: Loss of three GalNAc sugars to become ISIS 721744
(GalNAc)0THA-20-mer, followed by sequential loss of the nucleotides at
the 3′-end to produce 3′ n-X metabolites.
2. Family V: Hydrolysis of the entire linker of ISIS 721744 to form ISIS 780124 (fully
unconjugated ISIS 721744) followed by subsequent endo- and exo-nuclease
hydrolysis (3'-deletion and 5'-deletion) to produce 3′- and 5′ n-X metabolites.
3. Family VI: Hydrolysis of the entire linker of ISIS 721744 to form ISIS 780124
(fully unconjugated ISIS 721744), while retaining the 5′ phosphate group (5′PO
ISIS 780124). This metabolite then undergoes endo- and exo-nuclease
hydrolysis (5'-deletion) to produce 5′ n-X metabolites.
X represents the number of nucleotides that have been removed from the full length
ASO.
A diagram of the proposed putative metabolism of donidalorsen is shown in Figure 5
(Applicant’s Figure).
Mouse Urine: ISIS 721744 was the major component (about 53% of total
oligonucleotide signal) in mouse urine samples when administered at 10 mg/kg. As
described by the Applicant, other oligonucleotide metabolites included the full-length
ASO with partial conjugations, fully and partially conjugated donidalorsen with loss of
nucleotides from the 3′-end (referred to as 3′-deletion chain-shortened metabolites), and
unconjugated donidalorsen with loss of nucleotides from the 5′-end (referred to as 5′deletion chain-shortened metabolites).
Monkey Urine: ISIS 721744 was the major component (about 41% of total
oligonucleotide signal), followed by ISIS 780124 (unconjugated version of ISIS 721744;
about 14% of total oligonucleotide signal) in the monkey urine samples when
administered at 30 mg/kg. As described by the Applicant, other identified metabolites
were 3′-deletion chain-shortened metabolites of donidalorsen (with GalNAc sugar
moieties and THA linker attached), as well as metabolites of unconjugated donidalorsen
with loss of nucleotides from the 5′-end.
Human Urine: ISIS 780124 (unconjugated version of ISIS 721744) was the major
component (about 38% of total oligonucleotide signal) in human urine samples when
administered at 80 mg/kg. ISIS 721744 was not detected. As described by the
Applicant, the other most abundant metabolites were from unconjugated donidalorsen

with loss of nucleotides from the 5′-end. However, 3′-deletion chain-shortened
metabolites of donidalorsen (with GalNAc sugar moieties and THA linker attached) were
also seen.
There were no unique metabolites found in humans compared to mice or monkeys.

Profiling, Identification, and Quantitation of ISIS 721744 Linker-Related Metabolites by
HPLC-MS/MS in Select Plasma, Urine, and Fecal Samples from Mice, Monkeys, and
Humans (Study No. 721744-IS12)
This study identified linker-only-related metabolites of ISIS 721744 (no full-length or
chain-shortened oligonucleotide components) from plasma (monkey and human), urine
(mouse, monkey, and human), and feces (monkey) after SC dosing of ISIS 721744 (i.e.,
2 and/or 10 mg/kg dose groups from 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study in mice [Study
No. 721744-AS01]; 2 and/or 30 mg/kg dose group from 39-week repeat-dose toxicity
study in monkeys [Study No. 721744-AS02]; and 80 mg dose group from phase 1 study
in humans with dosing every four weeks for four total doses [Study No. ISIS 721744CS1]) by a HPLC-MS/MS method. Eleven total linker metabolites (putative linker
metabolites M4 to M14) were monitored in these studies.

37
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Six linker metabolites were detected in monkey plasma (M5 and M8 to M12) and three
linker metabolites were detected in human plasma (M5, M8, and M12).
Ten linker metabolites (M5 to M14) were similarly detected in mouse, monkey, and
human urine. The linker metabolites with the highest peak area ratios were M8, M5, and
M12, which were consistent across the three species.
Ten linker metabolites (M5 to M14) were detected in monkey feces. The linker
metabolites with the highest peak area ratios were M8, M10, M11, and M5.
As described by the Applicant: The THA-linker-related metabolism is generally similar
across species with oxidative metabolites being formed and eliminated through urine
and bile. The overall metabolic pathways for the THA-linker-related metabolites of
donidalorsen involve hydrolysis of GalNAc sugars and oligonucleotide moieties to form
M4 metabolite, followed by internal cyclization of M4 to form cyclized linker M5
metabolite which would then undergo mono- and di-oxidation to form M6 and M7
metabolites. Dephosphorylation of M4 metabolite resulted in the formation of M8
metabolite followed by sequential oxidation at each branching arm of M8 metabolite to
form mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra-oxidation metabolites (M9- M12 metabolites). Additional
metabolites resulting from dealkylation (M13 metabolite), or deamination (M14
metabolite) were also detected. The proposed pathway for the metabolism of linkerrelated moieties of donidalorsen is shown in Figure 6 (Applicant’s Figure).3

General Toxicology

As described in Section 3.1, the pivotal GLP-compliant 39-week repeat-dose toxicity
study of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus monkeys with a 13-week interim necropsy and a
26-week recovery period was previously reviewed (refer to IND 142564 Nonclinical
Review dated 08/13/2019). The monkey is considered a pharmacologically relevant
species for ISIS 721744 nonclinical evaluations.
Reviewed below is the pivotal GLP-compliant 26-week repeat-dose toxicity study of ISIS
721744 and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 in mice with a 13-week recovery period. The
mouse is not a pharmacologically relevant species for ISIS 721744 nonclinical
evaluations. This study, as designed, could assess potential off-target effects of ISIS
721744 and potential on-target effects using the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059.

Key Study Findings
•

•
•

•

In a repeat-dose toxicity study, mice were treated by SC administration with
vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or
12 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for 26
weeks with a 13-week treatment-free recovery period (vehicle control and 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 dose groups only).
There were no unscheduled deaths during the study that were considered related
to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
Changes in hematology parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period
included increases in white blood cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and/or
monocytes in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744
and at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period,
increases in hematology parameters were no longer seen at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744.
Changes in clinical chemistry parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment
period included increases in ALT, AST, and/or ALP in males and/or females at 1,
4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Effects on clinical chemistry parameters
(including ALT, AST, and ALP) were less clear at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At
the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in ALT and/or AST were still
seen in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, while increases in
ALP were no longer seen. The toxicological significance of increases in ALT and
AST were unclear as histopathology findings in the liver appeared to be partially
reversible and levels of unconjugated ISIS 721744 had declined below the lower
limit of quantitation.

40
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407
•

•

•

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Gross pathology findings after the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744
were seen in the liver (discoloration in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and enlargement in males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744) and inguinal lymph nodes (enlarged in males at 1 and 4 mg/kg/dose
ISIS 721744). There were no clear gross pathology findings seen after the 26week treatment period with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059. Gross pathology
findings after the 13-week recovery period for 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were
noted in the liver (discoloration in males) and subcutaneous injection site
(discoloration in males).
Organ weight changes after the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744
included increases in liver weights in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12
mg/kg/dose and increases in spleen weights in males at 12 mg/kg/dose. There
were no organ weight changes after the 26-week treatment period with 4
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period for 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, liver weights were still increased in males and/or
females.
Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744
were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and
spleen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment with mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059 were seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, spleen,
and testis.
o Liver: Minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy was noted
in males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in one female
(moderate) at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. This finding correlated with
increased mean liver weights at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and
increased liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). Despite a background
incidence of hepatocyte vacuolation in vehicle control males, there was an
increase in the severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in
males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which correlated with gross
pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels. These findings
were consistent with uptake of ISIS721744.
o Skin/Subcutis: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of
mononuclear cells, mixed cells, and/or vacuolated macrophages in the
skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose. Increased
incidences and/or severity of vacuolated fibrocytes in the skin/subcutis
were noted in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and
ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose. Slight to moderate inflammation in the skin
was noted in females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. These findings
in the skin/subcutis correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
o SC Dose Sites: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of
vacuolated macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as
fibrocyte vacuolation at the SC injection sites were noted in males and/or
females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose
ISIS 722059. These findings at the SC injection sites correlated with
increased leukocyte counts.

41
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

•

•

•
•

Eleni Salicru, PhD

o Inguinal Lymph Nodes: Increased incidences and severities (minimal to
marked) of increased lymphocytes in males at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose
ISIS 721744 and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in
the inguinal lymph node. This finding in the inguinal lymph node correlated
with increased leukocyte counts. Amyloid in the inguinal lymph node was
noted in one male at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
o Spleen: Increased incidence and/or severity of extramedullary
hematopoiesis in the spleen was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4
and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and
correlated with increased mean spleen weight in males administered 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
o Testis: Moderate interstitial cell hyperplasia, minimal sperm stasis, and
minimal vacuolation were noted in the testis of males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS
722059.
Histopathology findings after the 13-week recovery period for 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744 were still noted in the liver as hepatocellular vacuolation in males and
females, which correlated with increased liver weights. Histopathology findings in
the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen at 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were not seen at the end of the recovery period.
Unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measurable in a dose-dependent manner in the
kidney (greater than dose proportional) and liver (dose proportional) after 26
weeks of treatment with ISIS 721744. The mean concentrations of unconjugated
ISIS 721744 were similar in the kidney and liver except at 12 mg/kg/dose where
mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were greater in the kidney than
in the liver. Mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were higher in
females than in males in the kidney but similar in the liver. After the 13-week
treatment-free recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, mean
unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were below or near the lower limit of
quantitation of 0.107 mcg/g, suggesting complete clearance of ISIS 721744.
Mouse PKK mRNA in mouse liver was reduced by 77% (statistically significant)
compared to vehicle control in mice treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at
4 mg/kg/dose for 26 weeks.
The NOAEL was 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, as test article-related findings
were considered related to the oligonucleotide uptake.

Observations and Results
Mortality
Animals were checked twice daily (AM and PM) for mortality.
There were no unscheduled deaths during the study that were considered related to
treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
One male in the vehicle control group (No. M0006) was sacrificed in moribund condition
on Day 94 of the treatment period due to a skin lesion in the dorsal cervical area that did
not response to initial treatment with topical antibiotic cream on Day 57 and became
worse by Day 93.
One female at 1 mg/kg/dose (No. M0610) was sacrificed in moribund condition on Day
155 of the treatment period due to an injury that was potentially cage-related.
Clinical Signs
Cageside observations were conducted once daily during the treatment and recovery
periods. Detailed observations were conducted once during the predose period, once
weekly during the treatment period, and once weekly during the recovery period. Dose
site(s) were evaluated prior to dosing on each day of dosing, beginning on Day 15.
There were no clinical observations during the study that were considered related to
treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.

44
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Body Weights
Body weights were recorded once during the predose period, weekly during the
treatment period, and weekly during the recovery period.
There were no changes in body weight or body weight gain during the study that were
considered related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
Feed Consumption
Quantitative food consumption (grams/animal/day) for each cage was determined
weekly during the treatment period and recovery period.
There were no changes in feed consumption during the study that were considered
related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
Ophthalmoscopy
Ophthalmic examinations of dilated eyes using an indirect ophthalmoscope were
conducted by an ophthalmologist once during the predose period, once during Week 26
of the treatment period, and during the final week of the recovery period.
There were no ophthalmic findings during the study that were considered related to
treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
ECG
Not evaluated

parameters was evaluated.

were increased at the end of the treatment period (Day 185) in males and/or females at
1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.

Neutrophils were increased in males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and
in females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in males and females at 4
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
Lymphocytes were increased in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and
in females at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in males and females at
4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
Monocytes were increased in males and females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS

Gross Pathology
Scheduled sacrifices for treatment period and recovery period animals were Day 185
and Recovery Day 91 (Day 275), respectively. A complete gross pathology examination
occurred at the time of schedule necropsies.
As shown in Table 11, gross pathology findings at the end of treatment with ISIS
721744 were seen in the liver and inguinal lymph nodes. There were no clear gross
pathology findings seen at the end of treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
•
•
•

Discoloration of the liver was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and correlated with increased incidence and/or severity
of hepatocyte vacuolation in males.
Enlargement of the liver was noted in males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and
correlated with increased liver weights and moderate hepatocyte vacuolation.
Enlarged inguinal lymph nodes were seen in males at 1 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744 and correlated with increased lymphocytes.

As shown in Table 12, gross pathology findings at the recovery period sacrifice at 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in the liver and subcutaneous injection site.

Organ Weights
Adrenal, brain, gall bladder, heart, kidney, liver with gallbladder, lung with large bronchi,
ovary with oviduct, prostate, seminal vesicle, spleen, testis, thymus, and uterus with
cervix were weighed on Day 185 of the treatment period and on Recovery Day 91 (Day
275) of the recovery period. Paired organs were weighed together.
Notable organ weight changes at the end of the treatment period sacrifice are shown in
Table 13. Liver weights (absolute, relative to body weight, and/or relative to brain
weight) were increased in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744. Increased liver weights correlated with gross pathology finding of enlarged liver
in two males and histopathology finding of hepatocellular hypertrophy in some males

50
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

and one female. Spleen weights (absolute, relative to body weight, and/or relative to
brain weight) were increased in males at 12 mg/kg/dose. Increased spleen weight
correlated with histopathology finding of increased extramedullary hematopoiesis. There
were no organ weight changes at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
Notable organ weight changes at the end of the recovery period sacrifice at 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 are shown in Table 14. Liver weights (absolute, relative to
body weight, and/or relative to brain weight) were still increased in males and/or
females and correlated with histopathology finding of hepatocyte vacuolation.

Peer Review
Yes. The Applicant conducted an independent peer review of the primary
histopathology evaluation. As stated in the study report, a retrospective peer review of
the liver and testes was conducted by a different Ionis pathologist than the original
contemporaneous peer review.
Histological Findings
As shown in Table 16, histopathology findings at the end of treatment with ISIS 721744
were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen.
Histopathology findings at the end of treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were
seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, spleen, and testis.
•

•

•

•

•

Liver: Minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy was noted in
males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in one female (moderate) at
12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. This finding correlated with increased mean liver
weights at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and increased liver enzymes (AST,
ALT, and/or ALP). Despite a background incidence of hepatocyte vacuolation in
vehicle control males, there was an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of
hepatocyte vacuolation in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which
correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels.
These findings correlated with uptake of ISIS 721744 into the liver.
Skin/Subcutis: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of mononuclear
cells, mixed cells, and/or vacuolated macrophages in the skin/subcutis were
noted in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Increased incidences and/or severity of vacuolated
fibrocytes in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Slight to moderate
inflammation in the skin was noted in females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744. These findings in the skin/subcutis correlated with increased leukocyte
counts.
SC Dose Sites: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of vacuolated
macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte
vacuolation at the SC injection sites were noted in males and/or females at 1, 4,
and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These
findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
Inguinal Lymph Nodes: Increased incidences and severities (minimal to marked)
of increased lymphocytes in males at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744
and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in the inguinal lymph
node. This finding in the inguinal lymph node correlated with increased leukocyte
counts. Amyloid in the inguinal lymph node was noted in one male at 4
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
Spleen: Increased incidence and/or severity of extramedullary hematopoiesis in
the spleen was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and correlated with increased mean
spleen weight in males administered 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.

54
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407
•

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Testis: Moderate interstitial cell hyperplasia, minimal sperm stasis, and minimal
vacuolation were noted in the testis of males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.

As shown in Table 17, histopathology findings at the recovery period sacrifice at 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were still noted in the liver as hepatocellular vacuolation in
males and females, which correlated with increased liver weights. Histopathology
findings in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and/or spleen were
either not seen or less evident at the end of the recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744.

Special Evaluation
Exploratory Cytokine/Chemokine Analysis
Blood was collected for cytokine/chemokine analysis (IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL10, IL-13, TNF-α, and MCP-1A) using a multiplex assay kit on Day 185 of the treatment
period and Recovery Day 91 of the recovery period.
There were no clear effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on
concentrations of IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-10, IL-13, TNF-α, and MCP-1A.
IL-10, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-4, and IL-5 concentrations were below the limit of quantitation for
samples tested from the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated
groups.
IL-6 concentrations were at or below the limit of quantitation (<29.5 pg/mL) for all
samples tested in the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated
groups except for male No. M0006 in the vehicle control group with an elevated IL-6
concentration (202 pg/mL) on Day 94 (animal was terminated for a non-treatment
related injury).
IFN-γ concentrations were low or below the limit of quantitation (<2.87 pg/mL) for most
samples tested in the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated
groups except for female No. M0606 at 1 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 with a slight increase
in IFN-γ concentration (56.4 pg/mL).
TNF-α concentrations were below the limit of quantitation (<6.60 pg/mL) or just above
the limit of quantitation for all samples tested in the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated,
and ISIS 722059-treated groups.

62
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

MCP-1 was measurable at low concentrations in most samples in the vehicle control,
ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated groups with no clear effect of treatment.
Toxicokinetics
Tissue Analysis
Liver samples from vehicle control and ISIS 721744-treated groups and kidney samples
from ISIS 721744-treated groups were analyzed for unconjugated ISIS 721744 by a
validated UPLC-MS/MS analytical method.
There was no detectable unconjugated ISIS 721744 in the vehicle control liver samples.
As shown in Table 18 (Applicant’s Table), unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measurable
in a dose-dependent manner in the kidney (greater than dose proportional) and liver
(dose proportional) after 26 weeks of treatment with ISIS 721744. The mean
concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 were similar in the kidney and liver except
at 12 mg/kg/dose where mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were greater
in the kidney than in the liver. Mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were
higher in females than in males in the kidney but similar in the liver. After the 13-week
treatment-free recovery period, mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations at 12
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were below or near the lower limit of quantitation of 0.107
mcg/g, suggesting complete clearance of ISIS 721744 at this dose level.

PKK mRNA Analysis
Liver samples from vehicle control and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were collected on
Day 185 of the treatment period for PKK mRNA analysis by RT-PCR.
As shown in Figure 7 (Applicant’s Figure), mouse PKK mRNA in mouse liver was
reduced by 77% (statistically significant) compared to vehicle control in mice treated
with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose for 26 weeks.

Dosing Solution Analysis
The test articles were provided preformulated by the Applicant. The Applicant
conducted stability analyses on representative ISIS 721744 test articles within the
bracketed concentrations of 0.1 and 200 mg/mL (lot # RP721744-009 and lot #
RP721744-012, respectively) by a qualified ion-pair high-performance liquid
chromatography with ultraviolet detection and mass spectrometry (IP-HPLC-UV-MS)
method.
In the stability analysis for ISIS 721744 at 0.1 mg/mL, degradation impurities were
increased >50% in comparison to the ISIS 721744 release results, during the mass
spectrum overlay assessment. Upon a more detailed evaluation, the level of
degradation impurities was within the bulk drug substance specification limit and the
(b) (4) % so the test article was
label claim was within the acceptable range of
considered suitable for use. There was no change in the impurity profile or stability for
ISIS 721744 at 200 mg/mL.
All formulations were within ±15% of the target concentrations, ranging from 94.8% to
109.5% of theoretical, and met the acceptance criteria for study use.

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation

The Applicant is developing donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as a prophylaxis to prevent
attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. ISIS 721744 is
a GalNAc-conjugated ASO, which binds to human PKK mRNA to reduce PKK protein
production. The GalNAc molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by
binding to the ASGPR on liver cells.
The nonclinical development program included primary pharmacology (in vitro and in
vivo), safety pharmacology (in vivo cardiovascular, respiratory, and CNS in monkeys
and in vitro hERG) PK/ADME, repeat-dose toxicity (39-week in monkeys and 13- and
26-week in mice), genotoxicity (in vitro Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration
assay, and in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice), carcinogenicity (6-month
Tg.rasH2 mice), and reproductive and developmental toxicology (combined fertility and
development in mice and PPND in mice) studies. The main nonclinical species used in
the pharmacology and toxicology studies were monkeys and mice. The sequence
targeted by ISIS 721744 has one mismatch to the binding site in Cynomolgus monkey
PKK mRNA (position 19). Despite this mismatch, ISIS 721744 showed dose-dependent
inhibition of hepatic target mRNA expression and reductions in PKK protein and activity
levels in peripheral circulation of Cynomolgus monkeys. ISIS 721744 does not align
perfectly to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As such, in vivo studies in mice evaluated
mouse-specific PKK ASOs (either unconjugated ISIS 482584 in the pharmacology
studies or conjugated ISIS 722059 in the toxicology studies).
Primary Pharmacology
Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) is an ASO GalNAc conjugate that causes RNase H1
mediated degradation of PKK mRNA through selective binding to PKK mRNA, which
results in reduced production of PKK protein. There is high concordance of the
nonclinical pharmacology and clinical efficacy data for inhibition of PKK. PKK is a target
of several approved HAE therapies (small molecules and monoclonal antibodies).
In Vitro Pharmacology
Specificity analysis of ISIS 721744 was performed with unconjugated PKK ASO, ISIS
546254, which has the same sequence. ISIS 546254 is perfectly matched to only PKK
RNA in human transcriptome (targets site free of meaningful sequence variation). Refer
to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
Treatment of HepatoPac® (co-culture system of primary human hepatocytes and
stromal cells [mouse fibroblasts]) with ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254 (unconjugated
parent compound of ISIS 721744) resulted in a dose-dependent reduction of PKK
mRNA. The IC50 for ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254 were 0.19 mcM and 8.73 mcM,
respectively, indicating that ISIS 721744 is about 46-fold more potent than ISIS 546254
(likely due to cellular uptake through hepatocyte-specific ASGPR). Refer to the IND
142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
ISIS 546254 reduced human PKK mRNA levels by greater than 90% in a concentrationdependent manner in human hepatocellular cell lines HepaRG and Hep3b with
65
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

corresponding IC50 of 0.31 mcM and 0.35 mcM, respectively. The control
oligonucleotide ISIS 141923 did not reduce PKK mRNA in either cell line.
In Vivo Pharmacology
ISIS 721744 does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As
such, an unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate (i.e., ISIS 482584) was used for in
vivo pharmacology studies in mice. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated
08/13/2019.
Male C57Bl/6 albino mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle or
unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, or 160
mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. ISIS 482584 inhibited PKK liver mRNA and PKK plasma
protein expression in a dose-dependent manner. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical
Review dated 08/13/2019.
Permeability assays were performed in male C57Bl/6 albino mice treated with
unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (80 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks.
Evans Blue tracer was injected into the tail vein of mice and analyzed for its
accumulation in the colon tissue. Some mice were also treated intraperitoneally with the
angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitor captopril (1 mg/kg) at the time of Evans
Blue tracer injection or with a C1 INH ASO (40 mg/kg/week for 3 weeks) to enhance
vascular permeability. ISIS 482584 inhibited basal vascular permeability. Further ISIS
482584 inhibited vascular permeability induced by either captopril or C1 INH ASO.
Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
Male C57Bl/6 albino mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle or
unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, or 160
mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. ISIS 482584 (10 to 160 mg/kg for 3 weeks) reduced basal
activated high molecular weight kininogen cleavage in blood of male mice. Refer to the
IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
Human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice were treated by SC administration with ISIS
721744 (0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, or 10 mg/kg) on Day 0 and plasma was collected on Day -1, 3, 7,
14, 28, 42 and 56. A single dose of ISIS 721744 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent
reduction of plasma PKK protein that approached 91% at 10 mg/kg on Day 14 after
treatment. After reaching the lowest point at Days 7 to 14, plasma PKK levels were fully
restored by Day 42 for 1 mg/kg or Day 56 for 3 mg/kg dose. PKK levels were still 20%
below baseline levels by Day 56 for 10 mg/kg.
Safety Pharmacology
The safety pharmacology evaluations for the cardiovascular, respiratory, and CNS were
combined into one study in Cynomolgus monkeys. Based on cardiovascular and
respiratory assessments, there were no test article-related effects on arterial blood
pressure parameters (systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure), heart rate,
respiratory rate, core body temperature, or ECG parameters (PR interval, QRS duration,
QT interval, and RR interval) for up to 24 hours after dosing, or arterial blood gases for

66
Reference ID: 5557033

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

up to 2 hours after dosing, with 12 and 30 mg/kg ISIS 721744. Based on CNS
assessments, there were generally no treatment-related effects noted by functional
observational battery (FOB) for up to 24 hours after dosing with 12 and 30 mg/kg ISIS
721744. Although, one animal (No. 072104) receiving 12 mg/kg had signs of hunched
posture and tremors at 1 hour and 4 hours postdose, which were not evident at 24
hours postdose. Clinical chemistry and hematology parameters for this animal were
normal. These findings were not seen in any other animals at this dose (12 mg/kg) or
the higher dose (30 mg/kg). Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated
08/13/2019.
In the in vitro hERG assay, ISIS 721744 inhibited hERG current in HEK-293 cells by
0.5% and 1.9% at 30 mcM and 300 mcM, respectively (not statistically significant)
versus 2.4% for the vehicle control. The IC50 for the inhibitory effect of ISIS 721744 on
hERG potassium current was not calculated but was estimated to be greater than 300
mcM. In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to inhibit the hERG channel.
PK/ADME
The in vitro protein binding of ISIS 721744 at concentrations of 0.5, 5, and 150 mcg/mL
was evaluated in the whole plasma from human, Cynomolgus monkey, and mouse by
ultrafiltration methodology and a nuclease-dependent hybridization ELISA detection
method. ISIS 721744 was highly bound (≥96.81%) to whole plasma proteins in human,
monkey, and mouse at all three concentrations evaluated. The extent of plasma protein
binding of ISIS 721744 was similar across all species. Refer to the IND 142564
Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
The in vitro mean blood to plasma ratio of ISIS 721744 was between 0.630 and 0.824 in
human, 0.468 and 0.566 in monkey, and 0.501 and 0.661 in rat suggesting that ISIS
721744 distributes mostly in the plasma compartment across the concentrations tested
in all three species.
Based on metabolic profiling and identification of ISIS 721744 oligonucleotide-related
metabolites in urine from mice, monkeys, and humans, the Applicant described that the
primary route of elimination of donidalorsen is initial rapid hydrolysis of the GalNAc
conjugate in tissues, followed by slow nuclease-mediated metabolism of the
unconjugated oligonucleotide, and subsequent excretion of chain-shortened
metabolites, as well as full-length oligonucleotides, albeit minor in urine and feces.
There were no unique metabolites found in humans compared to animal species.
Based on metabolic profiling, identification, and quantitation of ISIS 721744 linkerrelated metabolites in plasma, urine, and/or fecal samples from mice, monkeys, and/or
humans, the Applicant determined that the GalNAc moiety is hydrolyzed intracellularly
following uptake into tissues, and the THA linker undergoes extensive oxidative
metabolism, and is nearly completely eliminated via biliary excretion, and to a lesser
extent, renal excretion, within 24 hours after administration.

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Repeat-Dose Toxicity
In the pivotal GLP-compliant chronic toxicity study in Cynomolgus monkeys
(pharmacologically relevant species), monkeys received SC doses of ISIS 721744 at 0,
2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose. The monkeys were dosed for 39-weeks (dosing on Days 1,
5, 9, and 14 [loading doses] and once weekly thereafter) with a 13-week interim
sacrifice (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the interim sacrifice). A 26week treatment-free recovery period was included after both the 13-week interim dosing
interval (30 mg/kg/dose) and the 39-week dosing interval (0, 2, 6, 12 mg/kg/dose) to
assess potential reversibility of any observed effects. Refer to Nonclinical Primary
Review dated 08/13/2019 for details. In brief, the main test article-related findings
included thrombocytopenia in two animals (12 and 30 mg/kg/dose) and histopathology
findings of basophilic granules in various organs/tissues (including kidneys, liver, lymph
nodes, and injection site) that in the absence of correlating histopathology were
considered consistent with oligonucleotide uptake and not considered adverse. There
were dose-dependent decreases in hepatic PKK mRNA expression and dosedependent and time-dependent decreases in PKK plasma protein after treatment with
ISIS 721744 at ≥2 mg/kg/dose at the interim and/or terminal sacrifices. Both hepatic
PKK mRNA expression and plasma protein increased by the end of the recovery
periods. Tissue concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 in liver or kidney increased
in a dose-dependent manner. The NOAEL was 6 mg/kg/week based on
thrombocytopenia in two monkeys at the higher dose levels of 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose.
The NOAEL corresponded to a Cmax of 6.57 mcg/mL and an AUC0-48hr of 37.6
mcg*hr/mL on Day 273.
In the pivotal chronic toxicity study in mice (not a pharmacologically relevant species),
mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for
Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 12 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059
(4 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for 26 weeks with a 13-week treatment-free recovery period
(vehicle control and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 dose groups only). Changes in
hematology parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period included increases
in white blood cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and/or monocytes in males and/or
females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in hematology parameters were
no longer seen at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Changes in clinical chemistry
parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period included increases in ALT, AST,
and/or ALP in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Effects
on clinical chemistry parameters (including ALT, AST, and ALP) were less clear at 4
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in ALT
and/or AST were still seen in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744,
while increases in ALP were no longer seen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week
treatment period with ISIS 721744 were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC dose sites,
inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment
with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites,
spleen, and testis.

males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in one female (moderate) at

Unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measurable in a dose-dependent manner in the kidney

were similar in the kidney and liver except at 12 mg/kg/dose where mean unconjugated

Conclusions
The nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology studies were judged to be adequate to
support the safety of donidalorsen for marketing. There are no outstanding concerns
from the nonclinical perspective.

approval.

1

Executive Summary

1.1

Introduction

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application
(NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg
(b) (4) (or 80 mg
(b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to
prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years
of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated
antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which targets human prekallikrein (PKK). The GalNAc
molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the
asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) on liver cells.
This review focuses on the evaluation of the GLP-compliant reproductive and
developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 (i.e., combined fertility and
developmental toxicity study in mice and pre- and postnatal development [PPND] study
in mice). ISIS 721744 does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene
sequence. As such, ISIS 721744 is not pharmacologically active in mice and the mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059, which targets mouse PKK, was included in both studies in mice
to assess potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition.
This review also provides a summary of the GLP-compliant reproductive and
developmental toxicology studies (i.e., combined fertility and developmental toxicity
study in mice and embryofetal development [EFD] study in rabbits) with the
unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744 (i.e., ISIS 546254) and/or its
unconjugated mouse surrogate (ISIS 482584) which targets mouse PKK to assess
potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition.

1.2

Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings

In the combined fertility and developmental toxicity study, mice were treated by SC
administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS
721744 (1, 4, or 10 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week).
Males were dosed once weekly during the premating, mating, and postmating phases
until euthanasia (about 10 weeks total). Females were dosed weekly during the
premating and mating phases and then every other day during the gestation period from
Gestation Day (GD) 0 to GD 16 (encompassing the periods of implantation and
organogenesis). Since ISIS 722059 statistically decreased PKK mRNA expression in
the liver of male and female mice by 80% and 75%, respectively. Unconjugated ISIS
721744 concentrations in the placenta (up to 0.31 mcg/g) were >10% lower than in the
liver (i.e., 3 to 43 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in females on GD 18). SC
administration of ISIS 721744 (up to 10 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059
(4 mg/kg/week) did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development in mice.
In a combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice, SC administration of the
unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744 (i.e., ISIS 546254) at dose levels up to
84 mg/kg/week or unconjugated mouse surrogate (i.e., ISIS 482584) at 84 mg/kg/week
did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development.
7
Reference ID: 5543389

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

In an EFD study in rabbits, SC administration of the unconjugated parent compound of
ISIS 721744 (i.e., ISIS 546254) at dose levels up to 75 mg/kg/week every other day
from GD 6 to GD 18 did not result in any fetal external findings, visceral variations or
malformations, or skeletal variations or malformations attributed to treatment.
In the PPND toxicity study, F0 female mice were treated by SC administration with
vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5, 10, or 20
mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) every other day from
GD 6 to GD 18 and weekly from Lactation Day (LD) 1 to LD 20 (the treatment period
encompassed organogenesis through weaning). Since ISIS 721744 is not active in
mice, the mouse-surrogate, ISIS 722059, was included in the study to assess the
potential effects related to the target inhibition. ISIS 722059 statistically decreased PKK
mRNA expression in the liver of F0 female mice by 82% on LD 22. ISIS 721744 was
present in milk of lactating F0 females at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week, although the drug is
unlikely to be adsorbed systemically in F1 pups. SC administration of ISIS 721744 (up to
20 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) did not affect
pregnancy in F0 females or prenatal and postnatal development (including behavioral,
fertility, and reproduction function) in F1 offspring.
Conclusion: The reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744
(and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059) were adequate to support the safety of ISIS
721744 for marketing. There are no outstanding concerns from the nonclinical
perspective related to reproductive and developmental toxicology.

1.3

Recommendations

1.3.1

Approvability

Refer to main Pharmacology/Toxicology NDA Review and Evaluation.
1.3.2

Additional Nonclinical Recommendations

There are no additional nonclinical recommendations related to the evaluation of
reproductive and developmental toxicity.
1.3.3

Labeling

Nonclinical sections of the product label are evaluated in a separate review.

for SC administration. The qualitative and quantitative drug product formulation is
shown in Table 1 (Applicant’s Table). The drug product is packaged in a staked needle
(b) (4) rubber plunger stopper. The
glass prefilled syringe (PFS) closed with a

autoinjector delivers a single dose of 80 mg donidalorsen.

Comments on Novel Excipients

There are no novel excipients in the drug product formulation. All the excipients are
within levels found in other FDA-approved SC drug products.

2.6

Proposed Clinical Population and Dosing Regimen

Donidalorsen is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and
pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The recommended dosage is 80 mg
(b) (4) . A dosing interval of

2.7

Regulatory Background

Provided below is the regulatory background for the ISIS 721744 reproductive and
developmental toxicology program. In brief, the Agency agreed that an EFD study of
ISIS 721744 in rabbits was not needed. The following is excerpted from the Type B End
of Phase 2 (EOP2) Meeting Minutes dated 10/18/2021 capturing discussions from the
teleconference between the Applicant and the Agency on 08/30/2021.
Question 2
Does the Agency agree to a waiver from the requirement to conduct an embryo-fetal
development study of ISIS 721744 in rabbits?
11
Reference ID: 5543389

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

FDA Response:
Pending review of the available, ongoing, and planned reproductive and developmental
toxicity studies with ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254, unconjugated parent compound of
ISIS 721744, (and the mouse surrogates ISIS 722059 and ISIS 482584 [unconjugated]),
we agree that an embryo-fetal development study of ISIS 721744 in rabbits is not
needed.
Refer to the ICH M3(R2) Guidance regarding the timing of reproductive toxicology
studies and the inclusion of women of childbearing potential in clinical studies.
The ongoing fertility and early embryonic development toxicity study in CD-1 mice
should be available prior to the initiation of the phase 3 clinical trials with ISIS 721744.
The planned pre and postnatal development study in CD-1 mice can be conducted in
parallel with phase 3 trials and provided with a potential NDA.
Discussion for FDA Response to Question 2:
There was no discussion held for FDA Response to Question 2.

Key Study Findings
•

•
•

In a combined fertility and developmental toxicity study, mice were treated by SC
administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP),
ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 10 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4
mg/kg/week). Males were dosed once weekly during the premating (beginning 28
days prior to mating), mating, and postmating phases (10 weeks total). Females
were dosed beginning 14 days prior to mating. Females were dosed weekly
(Days 1, 8, 15, and 22, as needed) during the premating phase and through the
mating phase until positive evidence of copulation was observed, and every other
day during the gestation period from GD 0 to GD 16 (i.e., GDs 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10,
12, 14, and 16). Unmated females continued to be dosed weekly until termination
(following the last GD 18 necropsies).
There were no estrous cycle changes (i.e., mean number of cycles and mean
cycle length) related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS
722059.
Percent abnormal sperm was increased at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (15.6%,
statistically significant) and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059 (13.4%), compared to the
vehicle control (10.1%), and outside of the conducting laboratory historical
control ranges of 3.4% to 10.2%. It did not appear that an increase in percent

13
Reference ID: 5543389

NDA 219407

•
•
•
•
•

•
•

Eleni Salicru, PhD

abnormal sperm affected pregnancy indices at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 or 4
mg/kg/week ISIS 722059.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on male
or female mating performance.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on the
number of corpora lutea, implantations, preimplantation and postimplantation
losses, or live fetuses.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on fetal
body weights.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on fetal
external, visceral, or skeletal variations or malformations (i.e., no fetal anomalies)
in mice.
Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the parental liver of males and
females increased with increasing dose of drug. Unconjugated ISIS 721744
concentrations in the fetal liver were below the limit of quantitation in all ISIS
721744-treated groups. Notably, unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the
placenta (up to 0.31 mcg/g) and testes (up to 1.61 mcg/g) were much lower than
in the liver (i.e., 3 to 43 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in F0 females
on GD 18 and 7 to 47 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week for males on Day 73). It was
unclear if ISIS 721744 or the unconjugated version of ISIS 721744 crossed the
placenta to reach fetal tissues.
Treatment of F0 male and female mice with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4
mg/kg/week statistically decreased hepatic mRNA expression of Klkb1/Pkk by
80% and 75%, respectively.
The NOAEL for ISIS 721744 on male and female fertility and mating
performance, as well as developmental toxicity, was the high dose of 10
mg/kg/week.

Observations and Results
Mortality
Mortality/cageside observations were made at least twice daily (morning and afternoon)
beginning upon arrival through termination/release.
There were two unscheduled deaths during the study. One male (No. 2021) at 1
mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 was euthanized on Day 61 due to severe penile prolapse and
decreased urine output. One toxicokinetic (TK) female (No. 7505) at 1 mg/kg/week ISIS
721744 was euthanized on GD 12 due to pregnancy complications (red discharge from
the vagina and red material present in the cage bedding). These unscheduled deaths
were considered incidental and unrelated to treatment with ISIS 721744 as there were
no deaths in higher dose groups.
All other animals survived to scheduled termination.
Clinical Signs
Detailed clinical observations were made prior to randomization and daily during
treatment (predose and about 1.5 hours postdose on dosing days).

16
Reference ID: 5543389

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

There were no clinical sign observations attributed to treatment with ISIS 721744 or
mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
Body Weight
Males
Males were weighed at receipt, prior to randomization, and twice weekly during the
premating and postmating phases.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on body weight
in males during the study.
Females
Females were weighed at receipt, prior to randomization, and twice weekly prior to
mating. Upon the beginning of the mating phase, females were weighed once weekly or
until mating was confirmed (body weight data for the mating phase was not included in
the study report). Upon verification of mating, females were weighed on the presumed
GDs 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on body weight
in females during the premating phase of the study.
As shown in Table 3, mean gestational body weight was increased beginning on GD 10
through GD 18 in females treated with 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (+5% to
+15% difference from vehicle control). Mean gestational body weight was increased
beginning on GD 16 through GD 18 in females treated with 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059
(+8% to +9% difference from vehicle control). These increases in mean gestational
body weight corresponded with increases in mean gestational body weight gain. The
increases in mean gestational body weight gain were not considered adverse. A
comparison of the body weight changes between GD 0 and GD 16 (drug treatment
period) is shown in Table 4.

Feed Consumption
Qualitative food consumption was recorded weekly prior to mating. Food consumption
was not recorded during the mating phase. Following the mating phase, qualitative food
consumption for males was recorded on a weekly basis until euthanasia. Qualitative
food consumption for females was recorded on the corresponding gestation body
weight days.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on food
consumption during the study.

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Estrous Cyclicity
Females were examined daily for estrous cyclicity at least 10 days prior to initiation of
treatment and until evidence of copulation was observed or the cohabitation period
ended.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on estrous
cyclicity (i.e., mean number of cycles and mean cycle length).
Sperm Analysis
At the time of euthanasia, the right testis and epididymis were used for sperm analysis
(i.e., sperm motility, sperm count/concentration, and sperm morphology).
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on sperm
motility or sperm count/concentration.
As shown in Table 5 (Applicant’s Table), percent abnormal sperm was increased at 10
mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (15.6%, statistically significant) and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS
722059 (13.4%) compared to the vehicle control (10.1%). These percent abnormal
sperm mean values were outside the conducting laboratory historical control ranges of
3.4% to 10.2%. As described in the study report: These differences were mostly driven
by a few animals at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (up to 36%) and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS
722059 (up to 27.7%) that had individual percent abnormal sperm slightly higher than
the concurrent control (up to 24.5%). It did not appear that an increase in percent
abnormal sperm affected pregnancy indices at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 or 4
mg/kg/week ISIS 722059.

in males suggestive of an effect on the liver. Other changes included a decrease in
albumin at 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in males, an increase in cholesterol at 1,

Toxicokinetics
Tissue Bioanalysis

21
Reference ID: 5543389

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Parental (liver, testis, and placenta) and fetal (liver) tissue were analyzed using a
validated ultra-high performance liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry
(UHPLC-MS/MS) procedure to determine unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations.
Parental and fetal tissue concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 are shown in
Table 8 (Applicant’s Table). Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the parental
liver of vehicle control males and females were below the limit of quantitation except for
one female which had a liver exposure of 1.72 mcg/g. Unconjugated ISIS 721744
concentrations in the parental liver of males and females increased with increase in ISIS
721744 dose. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the fetal liver were below
the limit of quantitation in all ISIS 721744-treated groups. Unconjugated ISIS 721744
concentrations in the placenta were below the limit of quantitation at 1 mg/kg/week ISIS
721744 and at 0.03 and 0.31 mcg/g at 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744, respectively.
Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the testes were below the limit of
quantitation at 1 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 and at 0.25 and 1.61 mcg/g at 4 and 10
mg/kg/week ISIS 721744, respectively. Notably, unconjugated ISIS 721744
concentrations in the placenta and testes were much lower than in the liver (3 to 43
mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in females on GD 18 and 7 to 47 mcg/g for 1
to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in males on Day 73). The uptake of ISIS 721744 by the
liver was promoted by the GalNAc conjugate, which is subsequently cleaved.

Necropsy
Scheduled euthanasia and necropsy for males was on Day 73 (about 48 hours after the
last dose). Scheduled euthanasia and necropsy for mated females was on presumed
GD 18 (about 48 hours following the last dose) and for unmated females was on Day 47
following completion of all GD 18 necropsies.
The tissues/organs that were weighed, collected, processed, and evaluated at the time
of necropsy are shown in Table 9 (Applicant’s Table).

Organ Weights
Organ weights were collected for testis (left and right separately), epididymis (left and
right separately), kidneys (paired), liver, seminal vesicles, spleen, and prostate gland for
males. Gravid uterine weight and organ weights for kidneys, liver, ovaries with oviduct
(paired), and spleen were recorded for females.
As shown in Table 10, there were increases in mean liver, kidney, and/or spleen
weights in males and/or females after treatment with ISIS 721744 and/or mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059. Mean liver weight was increased in males and females at 4 and
10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059. Mean kidney weight was
increased in females at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059.
Mean spleen weight was increased in males at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744. Increased
liver and kidney weights were attributed to uptake of ISIS 721744 and ISIS 722059.

Fertility Parameters (Mating/Fertility Index, Corpora Lutea, Preimplantation Loss, etc.)
Mating
As described in the study report:
Mating began on Day 29 for males and Day 15 for females. One female was housed
with one male from the same treatment group in the cage of the male. Positive evidence
of copulation was established by daily inspection for a copulatory plug in situ or vaginal
lavage for sperm. The day in which positive evidence of copulation was observed was
considered GD 0. After mating, each female was returned to an individual cage. The
maximum mating phase was 14 days.
As shown in Table 11 and Table 12 (Applicant’s Tables), the male and female mating
index was 100% for the vehicle control group as well as for the ISIS 721744 and mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059 groups. Further, the male and female fertility and pregnancy
indices were 92% in ISIS 721744 and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 groups compared
to 88% for the vehicle control group. As shown in Table 12 (Applicant’s Table), there
were 23 pregnancies in each of the ISIS 721744 groups and the mouse surrogate ISIS
722059 group compared to 22 pregnancies in the vehicle control group.

Each fetus was sexed, weighed, and evaluated for external, visceral, and skeletal

differences were not considered related to ISIS 721744.

Key Study Findings
•

•
•
•
•
•

•
•

In a PPND toxicity study, F0 female mice were treated by SC administration with
vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5, 10, or
20 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) every other
day from GD 6 to GD 18 (GDs 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18) and weekly from LD 1
to LD 20 (LDs 1, 7, 13, and 20).
There were no deaths in any of the F0 females attributed to treatment with ISIS
721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
AST (3x and 2x of control, respectively) and ALT (5x and 4x of control,
respectively) were increased in F0 females on LD 22 at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week
ISIS 721744 that was consistent with uptake into the liver.
Mean ISIS 721744 concentrations in milk from F0 females was below the limit of
quantitation for the vehicle control and 5 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 groups and
7.63 and 24.63 ng/mL at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744, respectively.
There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on
parturition parameters (gestation index, live newborn pups/litter, live birth index,
uterine implantation sites, and gestation length).
Kidney, liver, and/or spleen weights (absolute and/or relative to terminal body

and/or 20 mg/kg/week. Increases of kidney and liver weights were consistent
with uptake of ISIS 721744.
Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the kidney and liver of F0 females
on LD 22 increased with ISIS 721744 dose, which was consistent with uptake of
ISIS 721744.
Treatment of F0 females with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 5 mg/kg/week
statistically decreased hepatic mRNA expression of Klkb1/Pkk by 82% on LD 22.

Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation

ISIS 721744 is a GalNAc-conjugated ASO, which targets human PKK. The GalNAc
molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the ASGPR on
(b) (4) (or 80
liver cells. SC administration of ISIS 721744 is proposed as 80 mg
(b)
(4)
mg
in some patients) prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in
adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.
This review evaluates the GLP-compliant reproductive and developmental toxicology
studies with ISIS 721744 (i.e., combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in
mice and PPND study in mice) to support the safety of ISIS 721744 for marketing
approval. ISIS 721744 does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene
sequence. As such, ISIS 721744 is not pharmacologically active in mice and the mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059, which targets mouse PKK, was included in both studies in mice
to assess potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition.
This review also provides a summary of the GLP-compliant reproductive and
developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 546254 (i.e., combined fertility and
developmental toxicity study in mice and embryofetal development [EFD] study in
rabbits). ISIS 546254 is the unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744, which has
the same sequence as ISIS 721744 (i.e., 5′-TGCAAGTCTCTTGGCAAACA-3′), but with
a uniform backbone of phosphorothioate diester internucleotide linkages instead of a
mixed backbone like ISIS 721744. Based on specificity analysis against the human
transcriptome, ISIS 546254 is completely aligned to only PKK RNA. ISIS 546254 does
not have perfect alignment with the mouse PKK mRNA . Since ISIS 546254 is not
pharmacologically active in mice, the unconjugated mouse surrogate ISIS 482584,
which targets mouse PKK, was included in the combined fertility and developmental
toxicity study in mice to assess potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology
of PKK inhibition. Refer to summaries below.
Fertility and Early Embryonic Development
In the combined fertility and developmental toxicity study, mice were treated by SC
administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS
721744 (1, 4, or 10 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week).
Males were dosed once weekly during the premating, mating, and postmating phases
until euthanasia (about 10 weeks total). Females were dosed weekly during the
premating and mating phases and then every other day during the gestation period from
GD 0 to GD 16 (encompassing the periods of implantation and organogenesis). Since
ISIS 721744 is not active in mice, the mouse-surrogate ISIS 722059 was included in the

44
Reference ID: 5543389

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

study to assess the potential effects related to the target inhibition. ISIS 722059
statistically decreased PKK mRNA expression in the liver of male and female mice by
80% and 75%, respectively. Notably, unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the
placenta (up to 0.31 mcg/g) were >10% lower than in the liver (i.e., 3 to 43 mcg/g for 1
to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in females on GD 18). SC administration of ISIS 721744
(up to 10 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week) did not affect
fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development. It was unclear if ISIS 721744 or the
unconjugated version of ISIS 721744 crossed the placenta to reach fetal tissues.
A summary of the GLP-compliant combined fertility and developmental toxicity study
with ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744, which has the same
sequence as ISIS 721744) and unconjugated mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (Study No.
(b) (4) 090.60; Applicant No. 546254-AS04) is provided here.
• CD-1 mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium
Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 546254 (10.5, 42, or 84 mg/kg/week), or mouse
surrogate ISIS 482584 (84 mg/kg/week). As described in the study report,
animals were dosed every other day and received three or four doses per week;
thus, the weekly dose (mg/kg/week) was equivalent to 3.5 times the single
mg/kg/dose. Males were dosed every other day during the premating (beginning
4 weeks prior to mating), mating, and postmating phases (10 weeks total).
Females were dosed every other day for two weeks prior to mating, during the
mating phase, and throughout GD 15 (encompassing the period of
organogenesis).
• There was one unscheduled death during the study. One male at 84 mg/kg/week
ISIS 482584 was euthanized on Day 49 due to declining clinical condition (lack of
skin turgor and progressive face swelling). The animal was noted with a SC
hemorrhagic mass on top of the skull, which was considered incidental, likely of
traumatic origin. There were no remarkable gross findings in the other tissues
and organs that were examined. The unscheduled death was considered
incidental and unrelated to treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 482584. All
other animals survived to scheduled termination.
• Body weight decreases were noted in females on GD 18 at 10.5 and 84
mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (less than 10%
difference from vehicle control). The decreases were not considered adverse.
• Decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) in hematology parameters
were noted at 42 and/or 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males on Day 71 for
RBC (up to -14%), hemoglobin (up to -23%), hematocrit (up to -21%), mean
corpuscular volume (MCV) (up to -9%), mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) (up
to -11%), and platelets (up to -26%) and females on GD 18 for platelets (up to 21%).
• Decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) in hematology parameters
were noted at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 in males on Day 71 for hemoglobin (18%), hematocrit (-14%), MCV (-14%), MCH (-18%), and platelets (-54%) and in
females on GD 18 for platelets (-54%).
• Increases (percent difference from vehicle control) in hematology parameters
were noted at 42 and/or 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males on Day 71 for

Prenatal and Postnatal Development
In the PPND toxicity study, F0 female mice were treated by SC administration with
vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5, 10, or 20
mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) every other day from
GD 6 to GD 18 and weekly from Lactation Day (LD) 1 to LD 20 (the treatment period
encompassed organogenesis through weaning). Since ISIS 721744 is not active in
mice, the mouse-surrogate ISIS 722059 was included in the study to assess the
potential effects related to the target inhibition. ISIS 722059 statistically decreased PKK
mRNA expression in the liver of F0 female mice by 82% on LD 22. SC administration of
ISIS 721744 (up to 20 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week)
did not affect pregnancy in F0 females or prenatal and postnatal development (including
behavioral, fertility, and reproduction function) in F1 offspring. ISIS 721744 was present
in milk of lactating F0 females at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week.
Safety Evaluation:
In the combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice, SC administration of
ISIS 721744 (up to 10 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week)
did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development. In the PPND toxicity
study in mice, SC administration of ISIS 721744 (up to 20 mg/kg/week) or mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) did not affect pregnancy in F0 females or
prenatal and postnatal development (including behavioral, fertility, and reproduction

49

Eleni Salicru, PhD

function) in F1 offspring. The reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with
ISIS 721744 did not provide TK of ISIS 721744 from blood (e.g., AUC and Cmax

In a combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice, SC administration of

Conclusion: The reproductive and developmental toxicology studies were judged to be

1

Executive Summary

1.1

Introduction

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application
(NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg
(b) (4) (or 80 mg
(b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to
prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years
of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated
antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which targets prekallikrein (PKK). The GalNAc
molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver.
This review focuses on the evaluation of the 6-month carcinogenicity study of ISIS
721744, as well as the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, by SC injection in CByB6F1Tg(HRAS)2Jic Hemizygous Transgenic mice (Tg.rasH2 mice). The mouse is not a
pharmacologically relevant species with ISIS 721744 and this study primarily assessed
off-target toxicity. As such, the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, was included to assess
the effect of the intended pharmacology to inhibit synthesis of PKK. The Executive
Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee (ECAC) concurred with the doses for the study
in male mice but could not recommend doses for female mice (refer to Carcinogenicity
Special Protocol Assessment-2 [SPA-2] agreement dated 11/16/2022).
Of note, a two-year carcinogenicity study in Sprague Dawley (SD) rats is in progress.
The Division previously agreed that it would be acceptable to submit a summary of the
in-life data for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the NDA submission
and to submit the final report as a post marketing requirement (PMR) (Refer to IND
142564 pre-NDA Meeting Preliminary Comments dated 04/10/2024). Per the Applicant,
at the time of the NDA submission, the 2-year rat study was at >Week 74 of treatment.
The final study report is expected to be available around Quarter 4 (Q4) of 2025.
This review also provides an evaluation of the genotoxicity studies with ISIS 721744.

1.2

Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings

The genotoxic potential of ISIS 721744 was evaluated in the Good Laboratory Practice
(GLP)-compliant in vitro Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration assay, and in vivo
mammalian micronucleus assay in mice. The carcinogenic potential of ISIS 721744 (offtarget) and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (intended pharmacology to inhibit PKK
synthesis) was evaluated in the GLP-compliant 6-month carcinogenicity study in
Tg.rasH2 mice.
The in vitro Ames assay, using the plate incorporation method, was conducted to
evaluate the potential mutagenicity of ISIS 721744 (15 to 5000 mcg/plate) in S.
typhimurium TA98, TA100, TA1535 and TA1537, and E. coli WP2uvrA tester strains
(with or without 10% S9 mix for metabolic activation). There was no increase in the
number of revertant colonies in any tester strain, at any ISIS 721744 concentration up to
5000 µg/plate, with or without metabolic activation. ISIS 721744 was negative for
6
Reference ID: 5498659

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

mutagenicity up to 5000 µg/plate with or without metabolic activation. Refer to the IND
142564 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/13/2019 for further information.
The in vitro chromosome aberration assay was conducted to evaluate the clastogenic
potential of ISIS 721744 (62.5 to 500 mcg/mL) in Chinese hamster lung (CHL) cells for
6 hours (with or without 2% S9 mix for metabolic activation) and for 22 hours (without
S9 mix). No cytotoxicity was noted at up to 500 mcg/mL ISIS 721744 after 6 hours with
or without 2% S9 mix and 22 hours without S9 mix. There was no significant increase in
the number of metaphases with structural aberrations up to 500 mcg/mL ISIS 721744
after 6 hours (with or without 2% S9 mix) and 22 hours (without S9 mix). ISIS 721744
was negative for clastogenicity up to 500 mcg/mL with or without S9 in cultured CHL
cells. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/13/2019 for further
information.
The in vivo mammalian micronucleus assay was conducted to evaluate the potential
clastogenicity of ISIS 721744 (500, 1000, and 2000 mg/kg SC) administered on Days 1
and 3 (48 hours postdose on Day 1) to ICR mice. Mice were sacrificed on Day 4 (24
hours postdose on Day 3) for bone marrow collection. There was no statistically
significant increase in the incidence of micronucleated polychromatic erythrocytes
(MNPCEs) at any dose of ISIS 721744 tested compared to the vehicle control (negative
control) group. ISIS 721744 was negative in the in vivo bone marrow micronucleus
assay in mice. Refer to Section 7 for further information.
Conclusion: Overall, ISIS 721744 was not genotoxic in a complete battery of
genotoxicity assays.
The 6-month study in Tg.rasH2 mice was conducted to evaluate the carcinogenic
potential of ISIS 721744 (off-target) and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (intended
pharmacology to inhibit PKK synthesis). Tg.rasH2 mice (n = 25/sex/group) were
administered vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5,
10, or 20 mg/kg/dose for males and 10, 20, or 60 mg/kg/dose for females), or mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059 (10 mg/kg/dose) every two weeks (Q2W) for up to 6 months by
SC injection. A positive control group was also included in which Tg.rashH2 mice
(10/sex) were administered urethane (500 mg/kg/dose) via intraperitoneal (IP) injection
on Days 1, 3, and 5. A maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was achieved at the high dose
of 20 mg/kg Q2W in males based on histopathology findings in the liver and elevations
of glutamate dehydrogenase [GLDH]. The high dose of 60 mg/kg Q2W in females did
not meet the criteria for a MTD.
There was no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality dose response
across the vehicle control and ISIS 721744-treated groups, in either male or female
mice. There was a statistically significant decrease in mortality in the male 5 mg/kg/dose
group (low dose) compared to the vehicle control group.
Effects on clinical chemistry included increases in aspartate aminotransferase (AST),
alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and GLDH in males at 10 and 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS

7
Reference ID: 5498659

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

721744 and females at 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which correlated with
histopathology findings in the liver.
Neoplastic histopathology findings of hepatocellular adenoma in the liver were seen in
1/25 males at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, 2/25 males at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744,
and 1/25 males at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. The adenomas at 20 mg/kg/dose were
accompanied by several non-neoplastic findings in the liver (see below). Based on the
FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, there was no statistically significant dose
response relationship across the vehicle control and the ISIS 721744-treated groups in
any tumor types in either male or female mice. The pairwise comparisons also showed
no tumor types with a statistically significant increase in tumor incidences in ISIS
721744- or ISIS 722059-treated groups, when compared to the vehicle control group in
either male or female mice.
Non-neoplastic histopathology findings in ISIS-721744-treated and/or ISIS-722059 mice
were noted in the liver (microvesicular hepatocellular vacuolation, basophilic pigmented
macrophages, hepatocellular single cell necrosis, karyocytomegaly, and/or basophilic
focus of cellular alteration); kidney (epithelial vacuolation and epithelial basophilic
granules); injection site (macrophage granular vacuolation); urinary bladder
(urothelial vacuolation); and the axillary and/or mesenteric lymph nodes
(macrophage vacuolation). All histopathological findings were attributed to or a
consequence of oligonucleotide uptake.
The positive control (urethane) group resulted in neoplastic findings consistent with
known effects of urethane administration1 and confirmed the carcinogenic
responsiveness of the Tg.rasH2 model.
The mouse is not a pharmacologically relevant species for ISIS 721744, so the study
included one dose group treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059. Hepatic PKK
mRNA expression was statistically reduced in male and female mice treated with 10
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 Q2W for 26 weeks by 94% and 79%, respectively, compared
to controls.
Conclusion: Treatment with ISIS 721744 resulted in hepatocellular adenoma in
2/25 males at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which was not statistically significant
based on FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation. The ECAC concluded that the
carcinogenicity study was adequate for male mice and negative for drug-related
tumors. However, the carcinogenicity study was inadequate for female mice
because a MTD was not achieved and no other valid basis to support the high
dose was discernable.

1.3

Eleni Salicru, PhD

Recommendations

The final study results for the 6-month carcinogenicity study of ISIS 721744, as well as
the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 in Tg.rasH2 mice were presented to the ECAC on
12/10/2024. The ECAC concluded that the carcinogenicity study was adequate for male
mice and negative for drug-related tumors. However, the carcinogenicity study was
inadequate for female mice because a MTD was not achieved and no other valid basis
