Regulatory Background

At the pre-NDA meeting, the Division agreed that it would be acceptable to submit the
report of the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and a summary of the inlife data for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the NDA submission
and to submit the final report as a PMR (Refer to IND 142564 pre-NDA Meeting
Preliminary Comments dated 04/10/2024). This replaced comments conveyed from the
End of Phase 2 (EOP2) meeting in which the Applicant was requested to provide
reports for the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and the 2-year
carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of an NDA (Refer to IND 142564 EOP2 Meeting
Minutes dated 10/18/2021).
In the EOP2 meeting package, the Applicant had indicated their plan to conduct a 6month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and to seek a waiver for a 2-year rat
carcinogenicity study for ISIS 721744. Based on input from the ECAC, the conduct of a
2-year carcinogenicity study in rats could not be waived. As such, it was recommended
that the protocols for the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and the 2-year
carcinogenicity study in rats, along with supporting dose range-finding (DRF) studies, be
submitted for evaluation by the ECAC (Refer to IND 142564 EOP2 Meeting Minutes
dated 10/18/2021).
The carcinogenicity SPA-2 for a 6-month study in Tg.rasH2 mice with ISIS 721744 and
mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 was submitted on 10/12/2022 (SDN 36). The 14-week
DRF study in Tg.rasH2 and proposed protocol were reviewed (refer to Nonclinical
Primary Review dated 12/12/2022) and presented to the ECAC on 11/15/2022.
ECAC Recommendations and Conclusions for 6-Month Study in Tg.rasH2 Mice
• The Committee concurred with doses of 0 (0.9% sodium chloride for injection,
USP), 5, 10, and 20 mg/kg Q2W via SC injection in male mice with the high dose
based on a MTD (i.e., incidences of karyocytomegaly and increases of ALT,
AST, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) in male mice at higher doses in the 14week DRF study). The mid and low doses are based on adequate dose spacing.
• For female mice, the Committee could not recommend doses for the proposed
study, as no acceptable basis for dose selection could be identified. If the
Sponsor would like ECAC concurrence for dose selection, a new DRF study
should be conducted to identify an acceptable high dose as outlined in ICH
S1C(R2) or ICH S1B(R1).
• The Committee noted that the 6-month carcinogenicity study will be performed in
a different facility than used in the 14-week DRF study. The carcinogenicity study
may not be acceptable if toxicity is significantly different due to this change such
that dose selection would have been altered.
• The Committee noted that the planned ophthalmic examinations in the proposed
carcinogenicity study are not needed by FDA.
• If there are survival issues during the study, the Sponsor should contact the
Review Division before any changes are made.
Refer to IND 142564 ECAC Protocol Minutes dated 11/16/2022 for more details.

Key Study Findings
The in vivo mammalian micronucleus assay was conducted to evaluate potential
clastogenicity of ISIS 721744 (500, 1000, and 2000 mg/kg SC) administered on Days 1
and 3 (48 hours postdose on Day 1) to ICR male mice. Mice were sacrificed on Day 4
(24 hours postdose on Day 3) for bone marrow collection. There was no statistically
significant increase in the frequencies of MNPCEs at any dose of ISIS 721744 tested
compared to the vehicle control (negative control) group. ISIS 721744 was negative for
clastogenic potential in the in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice.

Study Validity
The high dose of 2000 mg/kg ISIS 721744 was based on a DRF study in mice and
considered a limit dose according to OECD TG No. 474 and ICH S2(R1). As such,
dosing of ISIS 721744 was considered adequate for the micronucleus assessment.
Adequate numbers of polychromatic erythrocytes (PCEs) per animal (i.e., 4000) were
scored for the presence of micronuclei.
The incidence of MNPCEs in the vehicle control (negative control) was within the range
of historical control data.
A positive control group (cyclophosphamide monohydrate) was included in the definitive
study. The incidence of MNPCEs in the positive control was significantly increased
compared to the negative control.
Results
There was no mortality during the study.
There were no abnormal clinical signs during the study.
There were no body weight changes during the study.
The mean incidence of MNPCEs based on examining 4000 PCEs per animal were 4.80,
6.00, 6.80, 5.00, and 92.80 for vehicle control, 500 mg/kg ISIS 721744, 1000 mg/kg
ISIS 721744, 2000 mg/kg ISIS 721744, and positive control, respectively. There was no
statistically significant increase in the incidence of MNPCEs at any dose of ISIS 721744
compared to the vehicle control. The increase in the incidence of MNPCEs for the
positive control was statistically significant compared to the vehicle control.
The mean ratio of PCEs to total erythrocytes (i.e., PCEs/[PCEs + normochromatic
erythrocytes (NCEs)]) based on examining 500 erythrocytes per animal were 0.53, 0.59,
0.52, 0.65, and 0.54 for vehicle control, 500 mg/kg ISIS 721744, 1000 mg/kg ISIS
721744, 2000 mg/kg ISIS 721744, and positive control, respectively. There was no
statistically significant difference in the mean PCEs/(PCEs + NCEs) at any dose of ISIS
721744 or the positive control compared to the vehicle control, used as an indicator of
cytotoxicity.
Liver samples from three mice/group were analyzed for tissue concentrations of
unconjugated ISIS 721744 on Day 4 (24 hours postdose on Day 3). As shown in Table
3 (Applicant’s Table), unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were increased in the
ISIS 721744-treated groups compared to the vehicle control group with group mean
ranging from 502 mcg/g to 774 mcg/g for ISIS 721744 doses ranging from 500 to 2000
mg/kg.

Key Study Findings
•

Tg.rasH2 mice (n = 25/sex/group) were administered vehicle control (0.9%
sodium chloride for injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/dose for
males and 10, 20, or 60 mg/kg/dose for females), or mouse surrogate ISIS
722059 (10 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for up to 6 months by SC injection. A positive
control group was also included in which Tg.rashH2 mice (10/sex) were
administered urethane (500 mg/kg/dose) via IP injection on Days 1, 3, and 5. The
mouse was not a pharmacologically relevant species wit ISIS 721744 and this
study evaluated off-target effects. The mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 was
included to assess inhibition of PKK and potential on-target effects.

•

There was no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality dose
response across the vehicle control and ISIS 721744-treated groups, in either
male or female mice. The pairwise comparisons showed a statistically significant
decrease in mortality in the male 5 mg/kg/dose group (low dose) compared to the
vehicle control group (p = 0.0160). The pairwise comparisons showed no
statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality between the mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059 group and the vehicle control group, in either male or
female mice.

•

There were no ISIS 721744-related or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059-related
effects on body weights.

•

Effects on clinical chemistry included increases in AST, ALT, and GLDH in males
at 10 and 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females at 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744, which correlated with histopathology findings in the liver.

•

A MTD was achieved at the high dose of 20 mg/kg Q2W in males based on
histopathology findings in the liver and elevations of GLDH. The high dose of 60
mg/kg Q2W in females did not meet the criteria for a MTD.

•

Gross pathology findings included liver mass in one male at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744 and one male at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which correlated with
neoplastic histopathology findings of hepatocellular adenoma in the liver of both
mice.

•

Neoplastic histopathology findings included hepatocellular adenoma in the liver in
1/25 males at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, 2/25 males at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744, and 1/25 males at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. The hepatocellular
adenoma seen in the males at 5 and 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were
accompanied by increases in AST and ALT, gross pathology findings in the liver,
and non-neoplastic histopathology findings in the liver of microvesicular
hepatocellular vacuolation, basophilic focus of cellular alteration, hepatocellular
single cell necrosis, and/or basophilic pigmented macrophage. There were no
correlating gross pathology or non-neoplastic histopathology findings for the male
at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
20

Reference ID: 5498659

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

•

Non-neoplastic histopathology findings were noted in the liver (microvesicular
hepatocellular vacuolation, basophilic pigmented macrophages, hepatocellular
single cell necrosis, karyocytomegaly, and/or basophilic focus of cellular
alteration in males at 5, 10, and/or 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, and/or females
at 10, 20, and/or 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, and/or males and/or females at 10
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059); kidney (epithelial vacuolation in females at 60
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and epithelial basophilic granules in males at 20
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females at 20 and 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744);
injection site (macrophage granular vacuolation in males and females at all ISIS
721744 doses and in males and females at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059); urinary
bladder (urothelial vacuolation in males at 10 and 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744
and females at 20 and 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744); and the axillary and/or
mesenteric lymph nodes (macrophage vacuolation in females at 60
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744). The histopathology findings were attributed to or a
consequence of oligonucleotide uptake.

•

The positive control (urethane) group confirmed the carcinogenic responsiveness
of the Tg.rasH2 model. Urethane treatment resulted in a decrease in body weight
in both male and female mice and a statistically significant increase in
unscheduled deaths (i.e., decrease in survival) compared to the vehicle control
group in both male and female mice. Neoplastic findings included
hemangiosarcoma (whole body in male and female mice), malignant lymphoma
(hemolymphoreticular tissue in male mice), and bronchioloalveolar adenoma and
carcinoma (lungs in male and female mice). These findings are consistent with
known effects of urethane administration.1

•

Toxicokinetics were not evaluated.

•

ISIS 721744 concentrations in the kidney and liver of males and females were
generally increased with increasing ISIS 721744 dose following 6-months of
treatment with ISIS 721744.

•

Hepatic PKK mRNA expression was statistically reduced in male and female
mice treated with 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 Q2W for 26 weeks by 94% and
79%, respectively, compared to controls.

Adequacy of Carcinogenicity Study
•

As described above, the ECAC concurred with the doses for the study in male
mice but could not recommend doses for female mice (refer to Carcinogenicity
SPA-2 agreement dated 11/16/2022). The Applicant did not conduct a new DRF
study to identify an acceptable high dose or seek ECAC concurrence for their
final dose selection in female mice. The ECAC concluded that the carcinogenicity
study was adequate for male mice but inadequate for female mice because a

NDA 219407

•

•

Eleni Salicru, PhD

MTD was not achieved and no other valid basis to support the high dose was
discernable.
There were no test article-related body weight changes or other adverse effects
that limited the duration of the study that were suggestive of the MTD being
exceeded in males receiving up to 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females
receiving up to 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
The duration of treatment was adequate (i.e., up to 6 months for males and
females).

Appropriateness of Test Models
The Tg.rasH2 mouse is considered an appropriate test model for evaluating the
carcinogenic potential of pharmaceuticals per ICH Guidance for Industry S1B Testing
for Carcinogenicity of Pharmaceuticals.
Evaluation of Tumor Findings
Test Articles
There was no statistically significant increase in tumor incidences in ISIS 721744- or
ISIS 722059-treated groups, when compared to the vehicle control group in either male
or female mice. Neoplastic histopathology findings included hepatocellular adenoma in
the liver in 1/25 males at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, 2/25 males at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744, and 1/25 males at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. The hepatocellular adenoma

laboratory Tg.rasH2 mouse historical control incidence (0/643 grand total male mice
examined [0%]; 1/643 grand total female mice examined [0.2%] or up to 4% per study
[1/25 female mice]).
Positive Control
There were statistically significant increases in tumor incidences of hemangiosarcoma
(whole body), malignant lymphoma in the hemolymphoreticular tissue, and
bronchioloalveolar adenoma and/or carcinoma in the lungs for the positive control group
(urethane), when compared to the vehicle control group, in either male or female mice,
which were expected findings for this known carcinogen.1

statistically
significant
at
≥18
mg/kg/dose) and females at 6, 18, and 36
mg/kg/dose (1.8x, 1.3x, and 1.6x over
control,
respectively;
not
dosedependent; not statistically significant).

•

As described in the study report, dosedependent increases in ALP, AST, and
ALT
in
males
correlated
with
histopathology findings of minimal
hepatocyte karyocytomegaly in the liver.
In the females, mild increases in ALP,
AST, and ALT were generally not dosedependent and did not correlate with
histopathology findings in the liver. ALP
was significantly increased for females at
36 mg/kg/day, although the increase
(1.2-fold)
was
not
toxicologically
significant.

ISIS 721744-related histopathology findings
were noted in the kidney, liver, and injection
site(s) as follows:
•

In the kidneys, histopathology findings in
males and females at ≥18 mg/kg/dose
included minimal accumulation of small
basophilic granules in the tubular
epithelium.

•

In the liver, histopathology findings in
males at ≥6 mg/kg/dose included minimal
karyocytomegaly (described as an
increase in hepatocyte nuclear size and
cytoplasmic volume). Karyocytomegaly
reflects hepatocyte polyploidy that occurs
when there is duplication of nuclear
material in the absence of cytokinesis.
Changes can consist of increased
numbers of diploid nuclei per hepatocyte

25
Reference ID: 5498659

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD
or an increase in the ploidy level of a
single hepatocyte nucleus. Spontaneous
occurrence of karyocytomegaly is
commonly seen in aging rodents and is
not typically associated with increased
liver weight. This aging change, often
referred to as polyploidy, is more
common in mice than in rats (NTP). As
described in the study report, this finding
correlated with increases in AST, ALT,
and ALP. There were no comparable
histopathological findings in the liver for
female drug-treated groups, although
ALP activity was increased for high dose
females. Increases of ALT, AST, and/or
ALP in male drug-treated groups and the
high dose female group, as well as
karyocytomegaly in male drug-treated
groups, were attributed to the uptake and
accumulation of the test article in
hepatocytes. There were no comparable
histopathological findings in the liver for
female drug-treated groups, although
higher concentrations of unconjugated
ISIS 721744 were measured in the livers
of females compared to males.
•

At the skin injection site, histopathology
findings in males at ≥6 mg/kg/dose and
females at ≥18 mg/kg/dose included
minimal to mild numbers of macrophages
with vacuolated or granular cytoplasm.
As described in the study report, when
comparing males and females of similar
dose groups, the injection site finding in
males was more distinct and easily
observed on microscopic examination
while in females vacuolated/granular
macrophages were more difficult to
detect.

•

As described in the study report, the
findings within the liver, kidneys, and
macrophages at the injection site were
likely secondary to uptake and
accumulation of the ASO. Because they

26
Reference ID: 5498659

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD
were not associated with evidence of
cellular degeneration or necrosis, these
findings were not considered adverse.
For male and female mice that received the
mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, at 6
mg/kg/dose, there were no changes of body
weight and clinical pathology parameters.
Further, there were no notable histopathological
findings.
The high dose selection with ISIS 721744 at 20
mg/kg/dose in male mice was based upon
observations of karyocytomegaly and increases
of ALT, AST, and ALP in male mice at 18
mg/kg/dose in the 14-week DRF study.
For female mice there were no histopathological
findings in the liver and there were minimal
generally non-dose-related elevations of ALT,
AST, and ALP. There were higher
concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 in
the liver of females compared to males. A MTD
was not identified for females.
The testing laboratory was different between
the 14-week dose range finding study and
26-week carcinogenicity study.
Vehicle, frequency of dosing, and route of
administration were identical between the
14-week dose range finding study and 26week carcinogenicity study.

Observations and Results
Mortality
Observations for mortality/morbidity occurred at least twice daily (morning and
afternoon) beginning upon arrival through termination.
The number of male and female mice that experienced early deaths (i.e., unscheduled
euthanasia or found dead) versus those that survived to terminal necropsy is shown in
Table 5.
An FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation by Malick Mbodj, PhD dated 12/16/2024
analyzed intercurrent mortality data using the Kaplan-Meier product limit method.
Further, the dose response relationship and homogeneity of survival distributions were
tested for the treatment groups using the Likelihood ratio test and the Log-Rank test.
Based on the FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation:
• There was no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality dose
response across the vehicle control and ISIS 721744-treated groups, in either
male or female mice. The pairwise comparisons showed a statistically significant
decrease in mortality in the male 5 mg/kg/dose group (low dose) compared to the
vehicle control group (p = 0.0160).
• The pairwise comparisons showed no statistically significant increase or
decrease in mortality between the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 group and the
vehicle control group, in either male or female mice.
• The positive control group had a statistically significant increase in unscheduled
deaths compared to the vehicle control group (p < 0.0001) in both male and
female mice.

In cases of early deaths for ISIS-721744-treated and ISIS-722059-treated mice, where
the cause of death could be determined, causes of death were malignant
mesothelioma, hemangiosarcoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and testicular
hemorrhage. These causes of death were either of low incidence, similar in incidence
between vehicle control and drug-treated groups, or did not exhibit a dose-response
relationship across groups (Table 6, Applicant’s Table).
As described in the study report, bronchioloalveolar carcinoma was the most common
cause of early death in positive control (urethane) mice; other causes of early death
included hemangiosarcoma and lymphoma.

Clinical Signs
Cageside observations occurred at least twice daily (morning and afternoon) beginning
upon arrival through termination. Detailed clinical observations (including but not limited
to evaluation of the skin, fur, eyes, ears, nose, oral cavity, thorax, abdomen, external
genitalia, limbs and feet, respiratory and circulatory effects, autonomic effects such as
salivation, nervous system effects including tremors, convulsions, reactivity to handling,
unusual behavior) occurred at predose and at about 4 hours postdose on dosing days
and once weekly on non-dosing weeks. The injection site(s) was evaluated prior to
dosing on each day of dosing beginning on Day 29 for any signs of irritation,
discoloration, and/or swelling. Palpation of tissue masses occurred weekly throughout
the study.
There were no ISIS 721744-related or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059-related clinical
signs or palpable masses.
Body Weights
Individual body weights were collected once after arrival, Day -1, and once weekly
during the study.
As shown in Table 7, there were no ISIS 721744-related or mouse surrogate ISIS
722059-related effects on absolute body weights compared to concurrent controls. The

Feed Consumption
Food consumption was quantitatively measured once weekly for the first 14 weeks and
every 2 weeks thereafter.
There were no ISIS 721744-related or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059-related effects on
food consumption.
Clinical Chemistry
Blood was taken for clinical chemistry evaluations at termination (Day 185). A
representative panel of clinical chemistry parameters was evaluated.
There were five vehicle control male mice (Nos. 1004, 1006, 1008, 1011, and 1018) and
three vehicle control female mice (Nos. 1511, 1516, and 1523) with large AST and ALT
values compared to the other mice in the vehicle control groups, which skewed the
group means higher. Taking this into account, there were still several males at 10 and
20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females at 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 with minimal to
mild increases in AST and ALT compared to the vehicle control groups. Males at 10 and

35
Reference ID: 5498659

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females at 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 also had
statistically significant increases in GLDH compared to vehicle control animals.
Increases in AST, ALT, and GLDH were indicative of effects on the liver. As described
in the study report, these increases correlated with histopathology findings related to
uptake of oligonucleotide that included hepatocellular vacuolation/basophilic granule
accumulation in macrophages and evidence of ongoing degeneration/hepatocyte
turnover (single cell necrosis and karyocytomegaly) in males, as well as with
histopathology findings of single cell necrosis (60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744) and
basophilic pigmented macrophages (20 and 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744) in the liver in
females that were attributed to uptake of oligonucleotide. The clinical chemistry changes
may also correlate to neoplastic findings of hepatocellular adenomas in two males at 20
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 (Nos. 4006 and 4016).
Triglycerides were statistically decreased in males and females at all ISIS 721744
doses and in females at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Cholesterol was increased in
males at all ISIS 721744 doses and at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and in females at 20
and 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
Total protein and albumin were decreased in males at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and
females at 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.

Gross Pathology
Mice were euthanized on Day 185 (about 48 hours after the Day 183 dose) and
subjected to a complete necropsy evaluation, including an external evaluation of
palpable masses.
Liver mass was noted in one male at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 (No. 2019) and one
male at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 (No. 4016), which correlated with neoplastic
histopathology finding of hepatocellular adenoma in both mice. Spleen mass was noted
in one male at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Refer to Table 9.
Gross pathology findings in the positive control (urethane) group included masses,
nodules, pale discoloration, and pale foci in the lungs, masses and nodules in the
spleen, and mass and enlargement in the thymus. Refer to Table 9.

Historical Control Provided for Tumor Incidence:
(b) (4)
The final study report (SDN 1, 08/21/2024) referenced the testing facility’s (i.e.,
historical control data for cause of death, neoplastic
lesions, and non-neoplastic lesions from 6 month studies in Tg.rasH2 mice (from
(b) (4) ) but it did not appear that these data were included in the final
study report. As such, in an information request (IR) dated 10/28/2024, the Applicant
was asked to submit these historical control data to the NDA (or indicate their location in
the NDA if they were already submitted). In their response to the IR (SDN 10,
11/04/2024), the Applicant indicated that the historical control data had not been
previously submitted and therefore provided the testing facility’s historical control data
for Tg.rasH2 mice, as requested.
Neoplastic
An FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation by Malick Mbodj, PhD dated 12/16/2024
analyzed the tumor data for dose response relationship across the vehicle control group
and the treated groups, as well as the pairwise comparisons of vehicle control group
with each of the treated groups. Following the recommendations by FDA statisticians for
the carcinogenicity study design and data analysis, the FDA Statistician applied multiple
41
Reference ID: 5498659

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

testing adjustments and used significance levels of 0.005 and 0.025 for common and
rare tumors, respectively in dose response relationship (trend) tests and significance
levels of 0.01 and 0.05 for common and rare tumors, respectively in pairwise
comparisons. A tumor is defined as a rare tumor if the published spontaneous rate or
the spontaneous rate of the vehicle control of the tumor is less than 1%, and a common
tumor is defined as one with tumor rate greater than or equal to 1%.
Test Articles
As shown in Table 12, the incidence of combined multicentric hemangiosarcoma was
greater in all male ISIS 721744-treated groups (up to 3/25 or 12% at 20 mg/kg/dose)
compared to the male vehicle control group (1/25 or 4%). However, based on the FDA
Statistical Review and Evaluation, this increase in hemangiosarcoma incidence was not
statistically significant. Based on the testing laboratory Tg.rasH2 mouse historical
control data, male and female mice developed multicentric hemangiosarcoma (38/643
grand total male mice examined [6%] or up to 16.7% per study; 39/643 grand total
female mice examined [6%] or up to 12% per study). The highest incidence of
hemangiosarcoma noted as 3/25 males (12%) at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 was
within range of the testing laboratory historical control data.
As shown in Table 12, hepatocellular adenoma in the liver was not observed in the
male (or female) vehicle control group(s), but was seen in males at 5 and 20
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059, as follows:
•

Male No. 2019 at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 (1/25; 4%).
Male No. 2019 had correlating gross pathology finding of liver mass and nonneoplastic histopathology finding in the liver of minimal microvesicular
hepatocellular vacuolation. Male No. 2019 also had elevated AST (i.e., 112 U/L)
and ALT (i.e., 272 U/L) compared to other males at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744
and males in the vehicle control group.

•

Male Nos. 4006 and 4016 at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 (2/25; 8%).
Male No. 4006 had correlating gross pathology finding of pale focus in the liver
and non-neoplastic histopathology findings in the liver of moderate basophilic
focus of cellular alteration, minimal hepatocellular single cell necrosis, and
minimal basophilic pigmented macrophage. Male No. 4006 also had elevated
AST (i.e., 120 U/L) and ALT (i.e., 126 U/L).
Male No. 4016 had correlating gross pathology finding of liver mass and nonneoplastic histopathology findings in the liver of moderate microvesicular
hepatocellular vacuolation, minimal hepatocellular single cell necrosis, and
minimal basophilic pigmented macrophage. Male No. 4016 also had elevated
AST (i.e., 183 U/L) and ALT (i.e., 257 U/L).

•

Male No. 6016 at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 (1/25; 4%).
Male No. 6016 had no correlating gross pathology or non-neoplastic
histopathology findings in the liver.

Non-neoplastic
Non-neoplastic histopathology findings at the time of the terminal sacrifice were noted in
the liver, kidney, injection site, urinary bladder, and lymph nodes (axillary and
mesenteric). Refer to Table 13.
Liver
Microvesicular hepatocellular vacuolation (minimal to moderate) in the liver was noted in
males at all ISIS 721744 doses and in one female at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. The
finding (minimal to mild) was seen in males at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. This finding
was attributed to oligonucleotide uptake.
Basophilic pigmented macrophages (minimal to moderate) in the liver were noted in
males at 10 and 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females at 20 and 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS
721744. The finding (minimal) was noted in males and females at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS
722059. This finding was attributed to oligonucleotide uptake.
Hepatocellular single cell necrosis (minimal) in the liver was seen in males at 10 and 20
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females at 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. The finding
(minimal) was seen in one male at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
Karyocytomegaly (minimal to mild) in the liver was seen in males at 10 and 20
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. The finding (minimal) was seen in one male at 10 mg/kg/dose
ISIS 722059.
Basophilic focus of cellular alteration (minimal to moderate) in the liver was seen in
males at 10 and 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. The finding (minimal) was seen in one
female at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
Kidney (Right)
Epithelial vacuolation (minimal to mild) in the kidney was noted in females at 60
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. The finding was not seen at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. This
finding was attributed to oligonucleotide uptake.
Epithelial basophilic granules (minimal to moderate) in the kidney were noted in males
at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females at 20 and 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. The
finding was not noted at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. This finding was attributed to
oligonucleotide uptake.
Injection Site
Macrophage granular vacuolation (minimal to mild) at the injection site was noted in
males and females at all ISIS 721744 doses. The finding (minimal to mild) was seen in
males and females at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. This finding was attributed to
oligonucleotide uptake.

Urothelial vacuolation (minimal to moderate) in the urinary bladder was noted in males

Toxicokinetics
The toxicokinetics of ISIS 721744 was not evaluated in this study.
Tissue Concentration Analysis
Portions of the kidney (left) and liver (left lobe) from 10 animals/sex/group were used for
tissue concentration analysis since these organs are the major organs of distribution for
oligonucleotides.
As shown in Table 14 (Applicant’s Table), ISIS 721744 concentrations in the kidney and
liver of males and females were generally increased with increasing ISIS 721744 dose
following 6-months of treatment with ISIS 721744.

Target mRNA Analysis
Liver tissue from the first 10 surviving animals/sex from the vehicle control group and all
surviving animals from the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059-treated group were used for
target mRNA analysis.
As shown in Figure 6 (Applicant’s Figure), hepatic PKK mRNA expression was
statistically reduced in male and female mice treated with 10 mg/kg/dose mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059 Q2W for 26 weeks by 94% and 79%, respectively, compared to
controls.

Dosing Solution Analysis
As described and included in the study report: Concentration verification of each ISIS
721744 and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 dose formulation was documented by the
Applicant and communicated to the Testing Facility in the form of a GLP Analytical
Summary Report. Representative samples which bracketed the range of ISIS 721744
and mouse surrogate 722059 concentrations were assessed for stability. No
homogeneity analysis of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 was performed
as they form a true solution in aqueous buffers.
The concentrations of the ISIS 721744 formulations (0.5, 1, 2, and 6 mg/mL) and mouse
surrogate ISIS 722059 formulation (1 mg/mL) were within acceptable ranges (94.4% to
99.3% of label claim and 106.6% of label claim, respectively) at test article release.
Further, ISIS 721744 formulations which bracketed those used on study (0.1 and 200
mg/mL) were stable for 42 months (results within 98.2 to 99.8% of the label claim) and
mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 formulations which bracketed that used on study (0.1 to

49

15 mg/mL) were stable for 12 months (results within 101.6 to 107.3% of label claim),
which confirmed the stability of the formulated test articles during the dosing period.

Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation

The Applicant submitted a 505(b)(1) NDA for SC administration of donidalorsen (ISIS
(b) (4) (or 80 mg
(b) (4)
721744), an ASO which targets PKK, as 80 mg
in some patients) prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric
patients 12 years of age and older.
ISIS 721744 was not genotoxic in a complete battery of genotoxicity assays (in vitro
Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration assay, in vivo mammalian micronucleus
assay).
The Applicant conducted a 6-month study in Tg.rasH2 mice to evaluate the
carcinogenic potential of ISIS 721744 (off-target) and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059
(intended pharmacology to inhibit PKK synthesis). Tg.rasH2 mice (n = 25/sex/group)
were administered vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection, USP), ISIS
721744 (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/dose for males and 10, 20, or 60 mg/kg/dose for females),
or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (10 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for up to 6 months by SC
injection. A positive control group was also included in which Tg.rashH2 mice (10/sex)
were administered urethane (500 mg/kg/dose) via intraperitoneal (IP) injection on Days
1, 3, and 5. Based on the 14-week DRF study in Tg.rasH2 (refer to Nonclinical Primary
Review dated 12/12/2022), the ECAC concurred with doses in male mice (high dose
based on a MTD) but could not recommend doses in female mice (no acceptable basis
for dose selection could be identified) (Refer to IND 142564 ECAC Protocol Minutes
dated 11/16/2022 for additional details).
There was no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality dose response
across the vehicle control and ISIS 721744-treated groups, in either male or female
mice. There was a statistically significant decrease in mortality in the male 5 mg/kg/dose
group (low dose) compared to the vehicle control group.
Effects on clinical chemistry included increases in AST, ALT, and GLDH in males at 10
and 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and females at 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which
correlated with histopathology findings in the liver.
A MTD was achieved at the high dose of 20 mg/kg Q2W in males based on
histopathology findings in the liver and elevations of GLDH. The high dose of 60 mg/kg
Q2W in females did not meet the criteria for a MTD.
Neoplastic histopathology findings included hepatocellular adenoma in the liver in 1/25
males at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, 2/25 males at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, and
1/25 males at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Although the tumor incidence was not
statistically significant, the hepatocellular adenoma noted in 2/25 males (8%) at 20
mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 exceeded the testing laboratory historical control incidence
(0/643 grand total male mice examined [0%]; 1/643 grand total female mice examined

50
Reference ID: 5498659

NDA 219407

Eleni Salicru, PhD

[0.2%] or up to 4% per study). Based on the FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation,
there was no statistically significant dose response relationship across the vehicle
control and the ISIS 721744-treated groups in any tumor types in either male or female
mice. The pairwise comparisons also showed no tumor types with a statistically
significant increase in tumor incidences in ISIS 721744- or ISIS 722059-treated groups,
when compared to the vehicle control group in either male or female mice.
Non-neoplastic histopathology findings were noted in the liver (microvesicular
hepatocellular vacuolation, basophilic pigmented macrophages, hepatocellular single
cell necrosis, karyocytomegaly, and/or basophilic focus of cellular alteration); kidney
(epithelial vacuolation and epithelial basophilic granules); injection site (macrophage
granular vacuolation); urinary bladder (urothelial vacuolation); and the axillary and/or
mesenteric lymph nodes (macrophage vacuolation). All histopathology findings were
attributed to or a consequence of oligonucleotide uptake.
The positive control (urethane) group resulted in findings consistent with known effects
of urethane administration1 and confirmed the carcinogenic responsiveness of the
Tg.rasH2 model.
Toxicokinetics were not evaluated in the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2.
Drug concentrations in the liver and kidneys generally increased with increasing dose.
The mouse is not a pharmacologically relevant species for ISIS 721744, so the study
included one dose group treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059. Hepatic PKK
mRNA expression was statistically reduced in male and female mice treated with 10
mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 Q2W for 26 weeks by 94% and 79%, respectively, compared
to controls.
The results of the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice carcinogenicity study
were presented to the ECAC (refer to meeting minutes dated 12/12/2024). The ECAC
concluded that the carcinogenicity study was adequate for male mice and negative for
drug-related tumors. However, the carcinogenicity study was inadequate for female
mice because an MTD was not achieved and no other valid basis to support the HD
was discernable.
Reviewer’s Note: Based on this nonclinical review, and the pending results of the 2-year
carcinogenicity study in male and female rats as a post marketing requirement, another
6-month study in female mice will not be requested at this time.

1. Background
In this submission the sponsor included a carcinogenicity study report in transgenic mice. This study was
intended to assess the carcinogenic potential of the test article donidalorsen (ISIS 721744), when given once
every other week via subcutaneous injection for up to 6-months in CByB6F1-Tg (HRAS)2Jic mice. In
addition, since ISIS 721744 was not homologous to mouse PKK mRNA, a mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059,
was included to evaluate carcinogenicity potential related to PKK inhibition. Results of this review have been
discussed with the reviewing pharmacologist Dr. Salicru.
In this review the phrase "dose response relationship" (trend) refers to the linear component of the effect of
treatment, and not necessarily to a strictly increasing or decreasing mortality or tumor incidence rate as dose
increases.
2. Mouse Study
In this study two separate experiments were conducted, one in male mice and one in female mice. In each
of these two experiments, one hundred and ten Tg rasH2 transgenic mice were assigned randomly to one
of the five groups which included three treated groups, one vehicle control group and one positive control
group in equal size of 25 animals except the positive control group which had 10 animals. The dose levels
for the treated groups were 5, 10, and 20 mg/kg/dose, for males and, 10, 20, and 60 mg/kg/dose, for
females as indicated in Table 1. In this review these dose groups would be referred to as the low, medium,
and high dose group, respectively. In addition, since ISIS 721744 was not homologous to mouse PKK
mRNA, a group of 25 mice (mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059), was included to evaluate carcinogenicity
potential related to PKK inhibition. The vehicle control group received the vehicle 0.9% Sodium Chloride
for Injection, USP (also known as Saline) administered subcutaneously once every two weeks in the same
manner as the treated groups. The positive control was administered with an intraperitoneal injection
(Urethane) at 500 mg/kg/dose on Days 1, 3, and 5. This group was included to verify sensitivity of the
test system to detect carcinogenicity effect.

The positive control was administered with intraperitoneal injection on Days 1, 3, and 5.
All animals were euthanized during week 27, (Groups 1-6)

During the study period, all animals were observed for morbidity, mortality, injury, and the availability of
food and water at least twice daily (morning and afternoon) beginning upon arrival throughout the study,
and all animals were given a detailed clinical examination within 3 days of the first dose administration
and 4 ± 0.5 hours postdose on dosing days, once weekly on non-dosing weeks. Any animal showing signs
of severe debility or intoxication, and if determined to be moribund or suffering excessively was
euthanized. The observations included, but were not limited to, evaluation of the skin, fur, eyes, ears,
nose, oral cavity, thorax, abdomen, external genitalia, limbs and feet, respiratory and circulatory effects,
autonomic effects such as salivation, and nervous system effects including tremors, convulsions,
reactivity to handling, unusual behavior, and palpation of tissue masses were done weekly throughout the

Reference ID: 5496510

NDA 219407 Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744)

Page 4 of 14

study. Histopathological examinations were performed on all animals found dead or killed moribund or
sacrificed at the end of the experiment. Body weights for all animals were measured and recorded once
after arrival, Day-1 and once weekly during the study. The food consumption recorded once weekly for
the first 14 weeks, every 2 weeks thereafter.
2.1.

Sponsor's analyses

2.1.1. Survival analysis
Intercurrent mortality data were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier product-limit method. An overall test
comparing all groups was conducted using the log-rank test. If this overall test was significant (p<0.05), a
follow up analysis was performed where each treated group was compared to the vehicle control group
using the log-rank test. Results of all pair-wise comparisons are reported at the 0.05 and 0.01 significance
levels. All endpoints were analyzed using two-tailed tests.
Sponsor’s findings:
Sponsor’s analysis showed the numbers of mice surviving to their terminal necropsy were 21 (84%), 25
(100%), 23 (92%), 21 (84%), and 22 (88%) in the vehicle control group, low, medium, high, and ISIS
722059 groups, respectively in male mice, and 25 (100%), 23 (92%), 24 (96%), 25 (100%), and 23(92%),
respectively, in female mice. The sponsor’s report concluded that, there was no statistically significant
increase or decrease in mortality dose response across the vehicle control group and the three treated
groups, in either male or female mice. The pairwise comparisons, also showed no statistically significant
increase or decrease in mortality between the individual treated groups, the ISIS 722059 group, and the
vehicle control group in either male or female mice.
2.1.2. Tumor data analysis (Peto and Poly-k Method)
Tumor incidence data were analyzed using both survival-adjusted and unadjusted tests. The unadjusted
tests were based on the incidences and numbers of sites examined for each tumor type. The CochranArmitage test was used to test dose response, and Fisher’s exact test was used to compare each treated
group with the control group. Trend test was applied for all control and treated groups able to be arranged
in a strictly increasing dose level. The survival-adjusted test was conducted according to the
prevalence/mortality methods described by Peto et al.
Survival adjusted analysis was also performed using the Poly-k method to assess prevalence of tumors
(Bailer and Portier, 1988) (Bieler and Williams, 1993). The survival-adjusted rates based on the risk
weights were displayed. The tests included both overall trend and pair-wise comparisons of each treated
group with the vehicle control. All p-values are reported using upper-tailed tests.
Adjustment for the multiplicity:
For multiplicity adjustment, the sponsor used significance levels of 0.005 and 0.025 for common and rare
tumors, respectively in dose response relationship (trend) tests and significance levels of 0.01 and 0.05 for
common and rare tumors, respectively in pairwise comparisons.
Sponsor’s findings:
The sponsor’s report concluded that, the donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) or ISIS 722059 does not have
carcinogenic activity or potential when administered daily for 26 weeks subcutaneously at doses up to
20 mg/kg/dose for males and up to 60 mg/kg/dose for females.

2.2

Reviewer's analyses

This reviewer independently performed the survival data analyses, tumor data analyses and additional
analyses suggested by the reviewing pharmacologist. Data used in this reviewer's analyses were provided by
the sponsor electronically on October 25, 2024, via SDN 0008.
2.2.1

Survival analysis

In the reviewer’s analysis, intercurrent mortality data were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier product limit
method. The Kaplan-Meier’s curve was presented graphically. The dose response relationship and
homogeneity of survival distributions were tested for the treatment groups using the Likelihood ratio test
and the Log-Rank test. The intercurrent mortality data are given in Tables 1A and 1B in the appendix.
The Kaplan-Meier curve for survival rate is given in Figures 1A and 1B in the appendix. Results of the
tests for dose response relationship and homogeneity of survivals are given in Tables 2A and 2B in the
appendix.
Reviewer’s findings:
This reviewer’s analysis showed the numbers of male mice surviving to their terminal necropsy were 21
(84%), 25 (100%), 23 (92%), 21 (84%), and 22 (88%) in the vehicle control group, low, medium, high,
and ISIS 722059 groups, respectively in male mice, and 25 (100%), 23 (92%), 24 (96%), 25 (100%), and
23(92%), in vehicle control, low, medium, high, and ISIS 722059 groups, respectively, in female mice.
This reviewer’s analysis showed no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality dose
response across the vehicle control group and the three ISIS 721744 treated groups, in either male or
female mice. The pairwise comparisons, showed a statistically significant decrease in mortality in the
male’s low dose group when compared to the vehicle control group, (p=0.0160).
Also, the pairwise comparisons, showed no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality
between the ISIS 722059 group, and the vehicle control group, in either male or female mice.
This reviewer’s analysis also, showed that the positive control group had a statistically significant
increase in unscheduled death compared to the vehicle control group, (p<0.0001) in both male and female
mice.
2.2.2. Tumor data analysis
In the reviewer’s analysis, the tumor data were analyzed for dose response relationship across vehicle
control group and the treated groups, as well as the pairwise comparisons of vehicle control group with
each of the treated groups using the Poly-k method described in the paper of Bailer and Portier (1988) and
Bieler and Williams (1993). In this method an animal that lives the full study period ( wmax ) or dies before
the terminal sacrifice with development of the tumor type being tested gets a score of s h =1. An animal that
dies at Week w h without development of the given tumor type before the end of the study gets a score of s h
k

 w 
=  h  <1. The adjusted group size is defined as Σ s h . As an interpretation, an animal with score s h =1
 wmax 
can be considered as a whole animal, while an animal with score s h <1 can be considered as a partial animal.
The adjusted group size Σ s h is equal to N (the original group size) if all animals live up to the end of the

Reference ID: 5496510

NDA 219407 Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744)

Page 6 of 14

study or if each animal develops the given tumor being tested, otherwise the adjusted group size is less than
N. These adjusted group sizes are then used for the dose response relationship (or the pairwise comparison)
tests using the Cochran-Armitage test. One critical point for Poly-k test is the choice of the appropriate
value of k. For this study rat and mouse studies, a value of k=3 is suggested in the literature. Hence, this
reviewer used k=3 for the analysis of the data. Based on the intent to treat (ITT) principle Wmax was
considered as 26.
For the calculation of p-values, if there were less than 10 tumor bearing animals across all treatment
groups for a given tumor type, the exact tests based on the discrete permutation distribution were used,
with dose levels (0, 5, 10, and 20 mg/kg/dose, for males and, 0, 10, 20, and 60 mg/kg/dose, for females)
as scores, and asymptotic tests were used for tumor types with higher incidences. The tumor rate and the
p-values of the tested tumor types are listed in Tables 3A and 3B in the appendix for male mice and
female mice, respectively.
Multiple testing adjustments:
Following the recommendations by FDA statisticians for the carcinogenicity study design and data
analysis, this reviewer used significance levels of 0.005 and 0.025 for common and rare tumors,
respectively in dose response relationship (trend) tests and significance levels of 0.01 and 0.05 for
common and rare tumors, respectively in pairwise comparisons.
A tumor is defined as a rare tumor if the published spontaneous rate or the spontaneous rate of the vehicle
control of the tumor is less than 1%, and a common tumor is defined as one with tumor rate greater than
or equal to 1%.
Reviewer’s findings:
Following the multiple testing adjustment method described above, this reviewer’s analyses showed no
statistically significant dose response relationship across the vehicle control and the ISIS 721744 treated
groups in any tumor types in either male or female mice. The pairwise comparisons also showed no tumor
types with a statistically significant increase in tumor incidences in donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) or ISIS
722059 treated groups, when compared to the vehicle control group in either male or female mice.
The pairwise comparisons showed statistically significant increases in the positive control group for the
incidences of bronchioloalveolar carcinoma, bronchioloalveolar adenoma, in lung and hemangiosarcoma
in spleen, when compared to the vehicle control group in both male and female mice (p-values <0.0001,
<0.0001, <0.0001 for males, and <0.0001, <0.0001, <0.0001, for females, respectively). Also, the
pairwise comparisons showed statistically significant increases in the positive control group for the
incidences of hemangiosarcoma in the lung, and lymphoma, malignant in the hemolymphoreticular tissue
in male mice (p-values=0.0483, and =0.0483, respectively).
